title: fix(ui): pin the toolbar version in tests so a version bump leaves the shell snapshots alone
body:
## Cause
`crates/ui/src/build_info.rs` pinned the toolbar's build time (`TOOLBAR_BUILD_UTC`) and source sha (`short_source()`) under `#[cfg(test)]`, but `toolbar_lines` and the narrow version-only label in `panes.rs` rendered the real `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`. The release script commits the version bump after its gate runs, so every cut changed one glyph in three shell snapshots and turned main red (23 px each after 0.15.0).

## Fix
- New toolbar-only `TOOLBAR_VERSION`: `"0.0.0"` under `#[cfg(test)]` (never a released version), the real `VERSION` otherwise.
- `toolbar_version()` returns `v{TOOLBAR_VERSION}`. `toolbar_lines` uses it, and so does the narrow label in `panes.rs`, which now goes through `build_info` instead of reading `VERSION` directly.
- The debug-info dialog still shows the real `VERSION`, `BUILT_UTC` and `SOURCE_SHA`, and its tests still assert `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`.
- The snapshot tests are unit tests in the `camcraft-ui` lib (`egui_app::tests`), so the `cfg(test)` pin applies to the build that renders them.
- Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/449-pin-toolbar-version.md`.

## Tests
- New: `build_info::tests::toolbar_label_pins_the_test_version_not_the_package_version` checks that the full and compact top lines read `v0.0.0 · test` and that `toolbar_version()` returns `v0.0.0`, whatever `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` is.
- Snapshots regenerated once (`UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1`, CWD `crates/ui`): `egui_app.png`, `egui_app_light.png`, `egui_tool_editor.png`. Pixel diff against main: 177 px each, all inside the top-right badge (x 1224-1253, y 25-33). The badge now reads `v0.0.0` and nothing else in the images changed.
- Gate (CWD `crates/ui`): `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` gave 316 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored, including the three snapshot tests and the debug_info tests. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- Not exercised: the `crates/ui/tests/` integration binaries. They are untouched, and the only non-test change is the narrow-label string source.

Changelog: none

Fixes #449

title: chore(release): 0.15.0
body:
## CamCraft 0.15.0

A minor release headlined by multi-setup machining (setup tree #343, setup transform #316, carried stock #317, rest across setups #318, carried verify #319, stock source #320, fixtures/lathe/cache #321), inverted machine axes (#373, #374, #375), the Stock page / Theme ribbon button (#441), plus the other PRs merged since v0.14.0. Full notes in RELEASE_NOTES.md; 54 CHANGELOG rows; 59 decision files gathered into RECOMMENDED.md.

### BREAKING
Project files moved v50 -> v57. One WCS per setup, with G54-G59 only the post label (#342 / #354), and the setup defines the work offset instead of each height (#329 / #331). Files from 0.14.0 or earlier migrate on open; a project whose operations used different G54-G59 slots inside one setup is refused by name (open it in 0.14.0, align the slots, save). Older builds refuse files saved by 0.15.0.

### Known issues
Open P0 #424 and #425 (fixture law: upright rapids check only the flute; ramps are judged at their lowest z), present before 0.15.0 and being worked.

### Gate (scripts/release.ps1, release tier, no -SkipGate)
- Debug: all non-UI crates plus camcraft-ui from crates/ui - 2820 passed, 0 failed, 67 ignored
- Clippy over all crates, -D warnings - clean
- Release --ignored lanes: motion 44 passed, sim 1 passed, app 17 passed, 0 failed
- post.exe --version reports 0.15.0

### Artifacts
dist/camcraft-0.15.0-win-x64.zip built. No installer: ISCC.exe (Inno Setup) is not installed on this machine, so camcraft-0.15.0-win-x64-setup.exe was not produced.

Not tagged, not merged: the tag follows the merge (AGENTS.md cut step 4).

title: fix(mcp): refuse null ids, survive oversize and non-UTF-8 lines, name nested patch typos
body:
Rescues the stdio MCP hardening left uncommitted in the stale `issue/128-mcp-server` worktree (part of #128) onto current main.

## What changed
- `crates/app/src/mcp/mod.rs`: a request with `"id": null` is refused as an invalid request (-32600). `serve()` reads each line as bytes through a 16 MiB cap (`MAX_LINE_BYTES`); an oversize line is a parse error (-32700) and the rest of it is skipped buffer by buffer without being held in memory; a non-UTF-8 line is a parse error and the session reads on. Only an I/O failure of the streams ends the loop early.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs`: a misspelled field at any depth of a params patch is refused naming its dotted path (`unknown field clearance_z.ofset`); previously only top-level typos were caught and nested ones were silently dropped by serde.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`: `post` reports the path `v_post` actually wrote, not the path asked for.

## How tested
Own worktree + own target dir, on origin/main fc9b297:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp`: 8/8 pass, pinned by `a_nested_patch_typo_is_refused_by_its_path`, `a_null_id_is_an_invalid_request`, `a_non_utf8_line_is_a_parse_error_and_the_session_reads_on`, `an_oversized_line_is_a_parse_error_and_is_skipped`
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib`: 95/95 pass
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

## Not exercised
- No real MCP client session over a pipe (the tests drive `serve()` over in-memory byte slices).
- The `post` path change has no dedicated assertion of its own beyond the existing whole-job test.

## Overlap
Fork PRs #421, #422 and #428 also edit `crates/app/src/mcp/mod.rs` and `tools.rs`; whichever lands second resolves the conflict (keep both sides).

Changelog: MCP stdio server refuses null request ids, survives oversize and non-UTF-8 lines, names nested params-patch typos by path, and reports the post path actually written

Fixes #443

title: fix(post): judge the tool-number clash per machine
body:
**Stacked on #439** (#388, per-mount posting). The #438 work is 9d9ac93d.

## What changed
- **The tool-number clash check (#221) is judged per machine.** `tool_numbers::clash_per_machine` runs the existing `clash()` on each machine group from `program_mounts(world, false)`. `posting::op_streams` calls it, which covers per-op files too.
- **Why per machine, not per NC file:** a T number names a pocket in one machine's tool changer.
  - Two machines have two tool tables, so T2 on each is fine.
  - Two posts on one machine still load from one carousel, so a shared number there is still refused.
  - Grouping per file (machine plus post) would let that real clash through, so I rejected it.
- **Messages:** a single-machine program gets the exact #221 message, unchanged. A multi-machine refusal starts with the mount's label (`Setup1 (machine, post): tools '…' and '…' would both post as T3 …`).
- The rationale is in `docs/decisions/388-per-setup-mount.md` (#438 section).

## How tested
- New `setup_mounts_post::a_tool_number_shared_across_machines_posts_but_clashes_within_one`:
  - across machines: a mill tool numbered 2 and the lathe's T2 post as two files;
  - within one machine: a clash is refused, naming both tools, the T number and Setup1, and not the lathe tool.
- `tool_numbers::two_tools_posting_one_number_refuse_by_name` (single machine) is unchanged and passes.
- `setup_mounts_post` 6/6, `setup_mount` 6/6, `tool_numbers` 6/6, `posting` 17/17, `post_not_judged` 4/4. `clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

Changelog: The tool-number clash is judged per machine, so two machines in one program may each use the same T number (#438)

title: feat(turning): optional repeat pass at each threading depth
body:
**Stacked on #433** (#417), which is on #432 (#416). Part of #363. The #418 work is bf3b0d58.

## What changed
- **The option:** `ThreadInfeed.repeat_each_depth`, off by default. Every pass above the root is followed by an identical copy: same tip depth, same lattice shift, same helix phase. So a repeat can never cut deeper or move. The finishing and spring passes at the root are not repeated.
- **Alternating infeed:** the side flips once per depth, not per cut, so a repeat keeps its flank.
- **G76 refuses it by name.** The record carries a `repeat_each_depth` flag, written to the stream as `REP 1` only when set, plus a `RepeatEachDepth` post property. `fanuc-lathe.cps` refuses with "repeat each roughing depth is not a G76 cycle (the cycle cuts each depth once)".
- **Defaults are byte-identical:** the stamp adds one byte only when the flag is on, and no project key or stream word is written when it's off. No version rung.
- **UI:** a "Repeat each depth" checkbox on the Passes tab, after Spring passes. Its tooltip says G32 only, that G76 refuses it, and that tooling makers recommend against routine spring passes.
- `docs/decisions/418-thread-repeat-pass.md`

## How tested
- motion `turning_thread_infeed`, 10/10, including two new tests:
  - every roughing depth is cut twice (0.4, 0.4, 0.8, 0.8, 1.1, 1.1, 1.2, 1.2) and the default is unchanged move for move;
  - a repeat is the same pass under every method × schedule, and the verdict stays silent.
- app:
  - `turning_thread_infeed` 5/5: the toggle goes stale and back to OK, takes 3 then 5 plunges, with undo and redo; round-trip writes the key only when set;
  - `lathe_post_g76_schedule` 5/5: G76 refuses the repeat; `REP 1` rides the stream; G32 posts 5 passes.
- `turning_thread`, `lathe_post_g76`, `inverted_post`, `project_roundtrip` and the app lib pass. No golden changed.
- `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` on cl, post, motion, app and ui is clean.
- The only failure is the headless-GPU ui test (no adapter on this Mac).

## Not exercised (draft)
GUI check and a lathe sim or machine run. There is a combined test kit for #416, #417 and #418.

Changelog: Threading op: optional repeat of each roughing depth (G32 output; G76 refuses it by name) (#418)

Fixes #418

title: feat(tools): draw a milling tool's holder as a revolved outline in the tool editor
body:
**Stacked on #399** (tool editor body column), which is on #381 and #348. First slice of #93: the **holder** of a milling tool drawn as a revolved half-outline. The custom cutter/shank profile is a follow-up, hence `Refs #93`.

## What changed
- **`crates/tools/src/spun.rs`: `SpunProfile`**, a (z, r, arc) half-outline.
  - **Refusals by name, with 1-based point numbers:** 3..64 points; finite; r ≥ 0, z ≥ 0; closed to the axis at both ends; no interior point on the axis; segments ≥ 0.01 mm; an arc no tighter than its chord; the outline never running back down the axis; not flat; size caps.
  - **Arcs never under-read:** convex arcs are replaced by the polygon that encloses them, concave arcs by chords on the arc.
  - Its `bands()` feed #381's `HolderProfile` exactly.
- **Storage: a drawn holder is a `ToolBody`.** The outline's own bands are its envelope, so every #368 law reads it unchanged: fixture bands, `enclose`, the stamp, the fits/flutes/lathe refusals, undo and delete. Its facets are the revolve of the outline, so the sim draws it.
  - A new optional `ToolBody::spun` keeps the points for re-editing.
  - **No project version rung:** `ToolBodyDto` gets an optional `spun` key beside the facets, which are still written.
    - A reader that knows the key redraws the body from it.
    - A reader that doesn't judges the facets. Their ring points sit on the outline, so it can only over-report. A test pins this.
  - **Parametric means no body,** so a tool that never went Custom keeps identical stamps and toolpaths.
- **UI, milling kinds only.** The third column gets **Body / Profile** tabs; turning tools show the Body section unchanged, per the owner's comment on #93. The Profile tab has:
  - a Parametric / Custom toggle;
  - a points table with insert and remove (read-only in Parametric);
  - a to-scale side view: cutter and shank from the numbers, the holder amber when valid and red when not, flute/stickout/gauge ticks;
  - a live refusal by name;
  - **Apply profile**, which issues one undoable `SetToolBody::spun`.

  Parametric follows the draft numbers live; Custom keeps hand edits.
- `docs/decisions/93-spun-tool-editor.md`

## How tested
- tools lib: 21 pass (6 new).
- `tool_spun_profile` (6 tests):
  - bands exact;
  - a drawn flange is flagged by the fixture laws;
  - a parametric holder equals `HolderStack::cylinder`, and the stamp is unchanged after clearing;
  - undo and redo;
  - refusals, including into the flutes and on a lathe kind;
  - round-trip byte-identical, and a reader without the `spun` key over-reports.
- `tool_body` (8), `tool_body_view` (8) and `project_roundtrip` (69) pass.
- ui `tool_` tests: 22 pass. `tool_editor_snapshot` fails on purpose (release-lane, #359), because the tab row is new.
- `clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh batch` fails only on tests already red on main:
  - #415;
  - the headless-GPU ui tests;
  - the release-lane snapshot;
  - `swarf_pose_continuity` (PR #351).

## Not exercised (draft until the contributor's GUI check; a test kit is prepared)
Follow-ups:
1. A custom cutter/neck/shank profile (`SpunProfile::cutter_of` is in place).
2. Fillet-at-vertex arcs.
3. Dragging points in the side view.
4. Spun profiles in the tool library file (#348).

Changelog: The tool editor draws a milling tool's holder as a revolved outline (points, arcs, live side view); the collision checks judge the drawn shape (#93)

Refs #93

title: fix(post): G76 words state the thread passes that were verified
body:
**Stacked on #432 (#416).** Part of #363.

## What changed
**With the G76 cycle post option, the G76 words now describe the passes the verdict judged.**
- The record maps 1:1: `G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)` / `G76 X Z P(k) Q(dd) F`, where:
  - dd = the first pass's depth;
  - dmin = the step (constant depth) or the plan's minimum (constant area);
  - d = the finishing pass's own depth;
  - m = 1 + spring passes;
  - a = twice the flank angle.
- **Control model** (GSK988TA, Fanuc-compatible G76):
  - each roughing pass goes to `max(dd·√n, previous + dmin)`, up to k − d;
  - the first finishing pass cuts d, and m − 1 more repeat at k;
  - each pass starts `depth·tan(a/2)` along Z.
- **Refused by name with G76 chosen:** alternating infeed (the CL carries a new `alternating` flag; `ALT 1` is written to the stream only when set), a doubled angle outside 0/29/30/55/60/80 (so 29.5° is refused), and a one-pass thread.

**⚠ This changes posted output for the default G76 thread: `R0` becomes `R0.4`.** The golden `fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc` changes on one line: `G76 P010000 Q400 R0` → `G76 P010000 Q400 R0.4`.
- Why: with `R0` the control roughs 0.4, 0.8 and 1.2, then cuts its finishing pass at the root again. That is a fourth full-depth pass the verdict never judged. It's not a gouge, but it isn't what was verified.
- With `R0.4` it roughs 0.4 and 0.8 and finishes at 1.2: exactly the three passes we judge.
- Making `R0` true instead would have meant changing G32 output and the judged passes.
- Note: the #363 research said Q = infeed made the control cut a decreasing ladder. That isn't so, because dmin = infeed clamps every step equal. The real gap was R.

`docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md`

## How tested
- New app `lathe_post_g76_schedule` (4 tests):
  - a new flank, constant-area golden `thread_g76_area.nc` (`G76 P020055 Q100 R0.05` / `G76 X9.6 Z14 P1200 Q400 F2`): the control's schedule computed from the posted words matches the laid depths and stations within 1 µm;
  - the default (`R0.4`) and a 0.5 step (`Q500 R0.2`) also match;
  - one refusal per unexpressible option;
  - `ALT` survives the stream and the project file.
- Existing post, cl, inverted_post, lathe_post, golden_cl, project_roundtrip, tool_law, tool_gate and commands_undo suites are green.
- `clippy --tests -D warnings` (cl, post, motion, app, ui) is clean.
- The gate escalated to batch (cl changed). It fails only on tests already red on main: headless GPU, #415, and `swarf_pose_continuity` (PR #351).

## Not exercised / not confirmed by sources (draft until a lathe sim or machine run)
1. Which way Fanuc shifts Z per pass for flank infeed. This follows LinuxCNC's sign; either sign is gouge-safe.
2. Whether the control also shifts each pass's end Z. If not, early passes end up to k·tan θ off at the runout, shallower than the root.
3. How the minimum-depth clamp applies (read as a per-pass minimum, per the manual's definition).
4. Micron rounding of the words: the control's ladder can differ by under 1 µm.

None of these moves the finished thread form.

Changelog: G76 threading output states the passes that were verified: the finish allowance R is posted (default threads now post R0.4 instead of R0), and options G76 cannot express are refused by name (#417)

Fixes #417

title: feat(turning): threading infeed method and decreasing-depth pass schedule
body:
Part of #363 (peck threading; the research comment there has the sources). Follow-up #417 (PR stacked on this one) makes the G76 output match these passes.

## What changed
**New threading op param `infeed_plan` (`turning::ThreadInfeed`).**
- **Infeed method:** radial, modified flank at an angle θ, or alternating flank.
- **Depth schedule:** constant depth, or constant area (first depth × √n).
- **Minimum depth per pass, finish allowance, and spring passes** (default 0, capped at 98).
- The existing `infeed` is the first-pass depth.
- It's shown as rows on the op's Passes tab (`thread_infeed_page.rs`).

**Kernel.** `crates/motion/src/turning/infeed.rs` lays the passes from the plan. `thread_in` calls `thread_planned_in` with the default plan.
- **Flank:** each pass starts shifted by −(tip − root)·tan θ along its travel. Finishing and spring passes sit on the pitch lattice, so lead and spindle phase never change.
- **Safety:** every pass stays inside the finished V exactly when θ ≤ half the insert's included angle. A larger angle is refused by name at the command (create, paste, edit, retype via `thread_gate`) and again at Generate.
- **Alternating:** flips the side each pass.

**The verdict judges the laid passes.** `the_verdict_reads_the_shifted_pass` pins a past-half-angle pass being convicted. `attach_cycle` moved to `thread_cycle.rs`.

**Defaults are byte-identical.** The default plan makes the same `blade::rungs(root, ref_top, infeed, 0)` call at the same stations.
- The op stamp includes the plan only when it isn't the default, so cached threads stay fresh.
- The project key is written only when non-default, so there's no version rung. An older build drops a non-default plan and cuts the radial ladder; that's not a gouge.
- No existing golden changed.

`docs/decisions/416-thread-infeed.md`

## How tested
- New motion `turning_thread_infeed` (8 tests):
  - √n depths with the minimum-depth clamp;
  - allowance plus spring-pass count;
  - flank shift, including the full 30°;
  - alternating flip;
  - verdict silent for every method × schedule on the thread fixture;
  - a shifted pass is convicted;
  - refusals by name.
- New app `turning_thread_infeed` (4/4, plus 1 after the merge): the plan runs in a document; refusals at create and edit; undo/redo (op goes stale); project round-trip with no key for the default plan.
- Existing suites unchanged and green: motion `turning_thread` and `turning_thread_cycle`; app `turning_thread`, `lathe_post_g76`, `lathe_field_tools` and `project_roundtrip`.

title: feat(turning): an optional insert zone on a lathe holder body
body:
**Stacked on #395** (lathe holder bodies), which is on #381. The #396 work is 679380d5.

## What changed
- **The zone.** A lathe body can carry an optional **insert zone**: a box in the turning tool frame around the tip, `InsertZone { lo, hi }`, in `BodyFrame::Lathe`.
- **Exclusion.** Each facet is clipped against the outer side of each of the box's six faces. Only what lies strictly inside the box leaves the clearance bands; every part outside it is still banded exactly.
  - The size, flatness and degeneracy checks still read the whole mesh.
  - Display and placement are untouched.
  - The stamp moves because the bands move.
- **The bound, so a zone can't hide the holder.** No tool field states the insert's size, so the cap is the steel the insert sits on:
  - the box must be finite and must hold the tip;
  - from the tip it may reach no farther than the tool's `diameter` along each axis;
  - for groove and form blades, at most `width/2` along the spindle;
  - every cap is held to 25.4 mm, the largest ISO turning insert's inscribed circle;
  - some of the body must stay outside the box.
  - Refusals are by name, at command creation, `ChangeTool` and load.
  - Limitation: inside that cap the zone excuses what it holds. Holder steel beyond the box is judged as before, and the shoulder-rub test pins that. See `docs/decisions/396-lathe-insert-zone.md`.
- **Command.** `LatheBodySpec.zone`, and `SetToolBody::insert_zone(world, tool, Option<InsertZone>)` sets or clears the zone and keeps the mesh. Same command, so undo and redo come free.
- **Project file: no new version.**
  - The zone is an optional `insert_zone` key, left out when there is none, so the bytes are unchanged without one.
  - A reader older than #396 skips the key and judges the whole body. That over-reports and blocks the post; it never passes a rub.

## How tested
- New `crates/app/tests/turning_insert_zone.rs` (5 tests):
  - a plate-plus-shank mesh on a plain OD finish is a `HolderHit` today, and posts clean with the zone set (undo and redo included);
  - in a bar, rough then finish, the plate's own chip is cleared by the zone;
  - **a real shoulder rub is still convicted with the zone set** (3.2 mm short, post refused);
  - refusals by name: no lathe body, zones past the cap (z 20, z −30, a grooving blade's ±1.5 against its 1.0 cap), a NaN corner, a zone missing the tip, a body wholly inside its zone, and a `ChangeTool` to a smaller body;
  - save → load → save is byte-identical, and an over-cap zone in a file refuses the load.
- `crates/tools` unit tests: 3 new; all 24 pass, including a randomized check that every facet point outside the zone stays within its band's radii.
- `turning_holder` still passes 8/8.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` against #395's branch is green except #415 (red on main). `clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
- No GUI for the zone yet: it's set through the command and the project file. The editor's lathe-body UI would follow #399.

Changelog: A lathe holder body can carry an insert zone, so a vendor mesh that includes its insert plate no longer reads the plate's own chip as a holder rub; zones larger than one of the tool's inserts are refused by name (#396)

Fixes #396

title: feat(sim): judge fixture collisions against the fixture's real mesh
body:
Slice 1 of #339 (triage and split are on the issue). Fixture collisions are judged against the fixture's real mesh, so a path down a vise's gap posts clean.

## What changed
**The box laws still run first, and the mesh can only clear a hit.** When a fixture's world box flags an upright move (laws c2 and d2), the fixture's closed mesh gets the final say, and it can only clear that hit, never add one. That keeps the box laws' deliberate silences, such as a retract off the mounting face. Where nothing is cleared, output is identical to before, labels included.

**Test shape.** Each tool band (flute, shank, holder, and the spindle housing when stated) is an upright cylinder swept along the move, an exact convex shape. Arcs are split into chords, each padded by how far the true arc can stray from it, plus 1 µm.

**Why it can't miss a real hit:**
- A band counts as clear only when a GJK distance test proves a gap of more than `FIXTURE_HIT_TOL` (plus the arc pad) to every nearby triangle. If the search fails or runs out, the answer is a hit.
- A band far from every triangle could still be buried inside the solid, so a point of it is tested by ray parity. Six fixed off-axis rays are tried; any that graze an edge, vertex or face are discarded, and if all are ambiguous the point counts as inside.
- Only closed meshes judge (each edge used once in each direction).
- A bounding-volume tree over the triangles is pruned with the same proof at every node.

**What keeps the box verdict:**
- Meshes that are open, non-finite, fully collapsed or over 4M facets: a named `MeshError`, logged.
- Tilted moves, moves with a non-zero C angle, and XZ/YZ arcs.
- Lathe tool kinds and non-mill machines.
- A box shared by two fixtures.

**Performance (release):**
- A 203k-facet closed mesh: validate and build the tree in 0.05 s.
- Worst case, 2000 passes grazing it 0.05 mm off (every one inside its box): 0.74 s total (0.37 ms/move), all correctly cleared.

**Code:**
- New: `crates/sim/src/fixture_mesh/` (mod, gjk, bvh, ray), `crates/sim/src/verify/mesh_steel.rs`.
- Hooks: `fixture::meshes_for`, plus small edits in `operation/{job,generate}.rs` and `posting.rs` (meshes cached once per setup).
- `docs/decisions/339-fixture-mesh.md`

**Merge note for #381:** this edits next to #381's `HolderStack` changes in `posting.rs` `fixture_problems` and `generate.rs` `workholding_warnings`. Whichever lands second resolves by keeping `mesh_refined(path, &wh, &steel, rapids, |w| <law>)` with the closures calling #381's `_held` variants, and by building `steel_stack` from the `HolderStack` bands. The decisions file has the recipe.

## How tested
- `crates/sim/tests/fixture_mesh.rs` (8 tests, plus one in the heavy lane):
  - a vise-gap pass, plunge and arc are cleared;
  - a jaw-corner clip still hits, while the same line 4.95 mm off is cleared;
  - a jaw-face clip, a holder over a jaw, a rapid into a jaw top, and a tool buried in steel all still hit;
  - open, NaN, empty and collapsed meshes refuse by name and keep the box verdict;
  - a tilted move and a fixture-less table box keep the box verdict;
  - timings (heavy lane: the 200k-facet case).
- `crates/app/tests/fixture_mesh.rs` (3 tests), end to end through `posting::verification_gate` and regeneration:
  - vise jaws 3 mm off the pass: clean;
  - the same vise as an open sheet: box verdict;
  - jaws 1 mm into the pass: the post is blocked and generation warns.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main`: sim suites green; app suites green except `setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…`, which is red on plain main (#415). Every existing fixture suite is unchanged.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised / follow-ups
- **Two P0 gaps in the existing box laws** were found by this survey and filed separately: #424 (upright rapids check only the flute) and #425 (ramps judged at their lowest z). This slice does not fix them, since the mesh only clears hits. The triage's slice 2 makes the mesh law able to add hits too.
- The remaining #339 slices: tilted and rotary moves against the mesh, fixture UX, routing around fixtures, and a fixture library.
- No GUI change, and no change to posted G-code. More programs now post: those whose only "hit" was a box around empty space between jaws.

Changelog: Fixture collisions are judged against the fixture's real mesh (the box stays the broad phase), so a path between vise jaws no longer refuses the post (#339)

Refs #339

body:
## What changed
While a setup's settings page is open and its stock source is "What <previous setup> leaves behind", the viewport draws the incoming body as a translucent **teal** sheet, in the active setup's frame, distinct from the setup's own Stock node.

- App: new `setup_stock_view::incoming_shape(world, setup)` calls `stock_sim::incoming_body` once and returns the box/volume plus `body.display().surface(&[])` as triangles mapped into the viewport's frame (`A_active * inverse(A_setup)`; identity when the setup is active). An empty body or sheet is an error naming the setup; a bad index is skipped, never a panic.
- UI: `incoming_view::IncomingView` caches it keyed by (setup, active setup, `doc_version`) - measured once per document version, never per frame - refreshed at the end of `drain_actions` and cleared the moment the page closes, another page opens, or the setup switches to its own stock. A failed measurement is logged once and draws nothing.
- Drawing: `collect_parts` adds a stock-type part with vertex class 4; `fs_stock` paints class 4 as teal rgb (0.12, 0.66, 0.74) at alpha 0.45 in the existing translucent stock pass.
- The page's incoming box/volume text reuses the viewport's measurement, so there is one program sim per version instead of two.

title: feat(mcp): serve the MCP tool table live from inside the GUI
body:
## What changed
The GUI can host the same MCP tool table (`app::mcp`) live, so an agent drives the open document and the user watches it in the viewport.

- **Opt-in, loopback only.** Off by default; started with `--mcp-port <n>` / `--mcp-port=<n>` or `CAMCRAFT_MCP_PORT` (flag wins; `0` picks a free port). Binds 127.0.0.1. A bad value exits 2.
- **Transport:** plain TCP carrying the same newline-delimited JSON-RPC as `camcraft-cli mcp`, plus a stdio<->TCP bridge `camcraft-cli mcp --connect <host:port>` so stdio MCP clients can attach.
- **Threading:** a std listener thread (one client at a time) only moves text; each line goes over an mpsc channel to the UI thread with its own reply channel and wakes the idle winit loop (`EventLoopProxy`). No world access off the UI thread.
- **Same document, same History.** The UI thread answers in `State::drain_actions` after the user's own queued commands, through the existing `Server` dispatch (no tool code duplicated): the `Env` gets the GUI's world handle and borrows the GUI's own `History` for the call. An agent step is one Ctrl+Z, and the agent's `undo`/`redo` walk the user's steps too. Every call bumps `doc_version`; the status line reads `agent: <tool>`.
- **Status strip** shows `MCP listening on 127.0.0.1:<port>` while the server runs (default frames unchanged).
- **Never crash:** malformed JSON -> -32700; a dropped client, closed channel or >16 MiB line is logged and the listener carries on; dropping the `Inbox` stops and joins the thread (~50 ms) at shutdown.
- **Refused live:** `open_project` (would replace the user's document past the unsaved-changes prompt).
- New code: `crates/app/src/mcp/{listen,live,bridge}.rs`, `crates/ui/src/mcp_host.rs`; `mcp/tools.rs` and `mcp/edit.rs` untouched.

## Maintainer note (judgement call)
There is no authentication: any local process can drive the open document while the server is on. Being off by default and loopback-only is the guard; a token could be added later if wanted. `save_project` without a path saves over the open project but does not mark it clean, so the app may still ask to save. A long `generate` blocks the UI frame for its duration.

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1722 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main (`setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` #415; GPU headless trio). Clippy `-D warnings` clean. Hand run: `camcraft-ui --mcp-port 7333` driven through `camcraft-cli mcp --connect` (set_stock, add_tool, add_operation all `isError:false`; `get_job` over nc showed the op in the app's world).

## Pinning tests
- App `crates/app/tests/mcp_live.rs`: `a_live_call_lands_on_the_callers_history_and_its_undo_reverts_it`, `each_agent_step_is_one_undo_step_on_the_shared_history`, `the_live_session_refuses_open_project_and_reads_bad_lines_as_errors`, `the_port_flag_is_opt_in_and_checked`, `a_loopback_client_drives_the_owners_document_and_survives_bad_input` (real loopback TCP), `the_bridge_copies_stdio_to_a_live_session_and_back`.
- UI lib `egui_app::tests::mcp_live`: `an_agents_operation_shows_in_the_browser_and_ctrl_z_removes_it`, `the_status_strip_says_the_server_is_listening`.

## Not exercised
Ctrl+Z pressed by hand in the real window (harness only) - **draft until the GUI check**; Windows/Linux runs (std::net only); a real MCP client app beyond the bridge/nc; the bind-failure path (port in use). Posted G-code unchanged.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/183-mcp-live-gui.md`.

Changelog: The GUI can serve MCP live on a loopback port (`--mcp-port` / `CAMCRAFT_MCP_PORT`), so an agent's steps land in the open document and Ctrl+Z undoes them; `camcraft-cli mcp --connect` bridges stdio clients

Fixes #183

title: feat(app): Pause, optional stop and go-home entries in the operation list
body:
## What changed
**A new program-entry kind: Pause (M0), Optional stop (M1) and Go home.**
- Entries sit in the operation list alongside operations, using the same `OperationMeta.order`.
- The new component `schema::ProgramEntry { action, setup, suppressed }` is not an `Operation`. So `setup::operation_order`, and every walk built on it, skips entries without per-walk carve-outs: the post tool gate and freshness, `rest::ahead_of`, the program sim, the setup sheet, the tool list, verify and `RegenerateAll`.
- An entry has no generated status, so it never holds the post as "not generated".

**Posting.** Each entry folds into the posted op before it, as that op's `PARAM AfterOperation` word (one hook in `posting::op_streams`, logic in `program_entry::posted_afters`).
- A Pause after Face1 posts byte-identically to setting Face1's after-action to Program stop. This is pinned for all three actions on Fanuc and Haas.
- Equal asks in one gap merge, and a program stop absorbs an optional stop.
- An entry after a suppressed op attaches to the last op that posts.
- Suppress and "Skip pauses and homes" mute entries just as they mute op actions.
- **Refused by name:**
  - an entry before every posted op;
  - a Pause and a Home in the same gap (the stream holds one after-word per gap);
  - entries on the Tormach post, which doesn't read `AfterOperation`, the same as the per-op action there today.

**Commands, all undoable.**
- New: `AddProgramEntry` (after a named row, or at the end of the active setup), `EditProgramEntry::with_action` and `::with_suppressed`.
- Reused: `ReorderOperation` (drag) and `DeleteEntity` (Del or the menu).
- `ReorderOperation`, `CreateOperation`'s append and `DeleteSetup`'s refusal now count over `program_entry::sequence`, which equals `operation_order` on documents without entries.

**UI.**
- Every operation-list menu gains "Add pause (M0) after", "Add go home after" and "Add optional stop (M1) after".
- An entry row uses the Post glyph, with its action and SUPPRESSED in the suffix. Its menu offers change action, suppress, delete and add after.
- Entries drag like op rows.

**Project file: no version rung.**
- An entry saves as `"kind": "entry"` plus an `entry` payload.
- A document without entries writes neither key, so its bytes are unchanged.
- An older reader refuses a file with entries (serde: unknown variant `entry`) rather than dropping the stops.

**Posted G-code:** only documents with entries change. No `.cps` was touched, and every existing golden is unchanged.

`docs/decisions/155-pause-home-entries.md`

## How tested
- App `program_entry` (7 tests):
  - add, reorder, delete, undo/redo, new-op placement;
  - an entry equals the per-op words byte for byte;
  - Fanuc and Haas goldens, and the Tormach refusal;
  - Suppress, Skip and action edits;
  - the gap rules;
  - project round-trip, save → load → save byte-stable;
  - walks unaffected: `program_ops`, tool list, setup sheet, sim verdict, rest digest, verification gate.
- UI (3 tests): the menu rows; an entry row with undo; a click-through from op menu to add pause, suppress, delete and undo.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` (app and ui suites) passes except known failures:
  - `setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…`, red on main (#415);
  - the headless-GPU ui tests (no adapter on this Mac).
- `clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -D warnings` is clean. After the merge with main at #410, `program_entry` passes 7/7.

## Not exercised (draft until the contributor's GUI check)
- A hands-on check of the menus, drag and posted output in a release build. A test kit is prepared.
- Possible follow-ups:
  - Home-then-Pause in one gap (needs a compound after-word in every script that reads `afterModes`);
  - Tormach reading `AfterOperation`, which would change its output for existing per-op documents.

Changelog: Pause, optional stop and go-home entries can be placed between operations in the operation list; they post the same words as an operation's after-action (#155)

Fixes #155

body:
**Stacked on #382** (Machines pane, browse + validate): this branch carries #382's commits plus a merge of current main. Merge #382 first; this PR's own diff is then the last two commits (`cb293f30`, `35cfa074`) plus the merge.

## What changed
- The Machines pane's detail view gets a **"Use for this setup"** button under the validation verdict. Clicking it queues `CommandKind::UseCatalogueMachine(MachineSource)`.

- Validation is re-run at assignment: `machine::library::read_for_assign` re-reads the built-in text or file, runs `validate_text`, and refuses with the first refusal, so a refused machine never mounts even if the command is queued directly. Shared by `LoadMachine::from_catalogue`, the new `SetSetupMachine::from_catalogue` and the UI route.
- The button is disabled with the reason shown under it and on hover: "fails validation - <first refusal> (and N more)" or "it is already this setup's machine" (reads `machine::of`, the active setup's effective machine).
- `MachineSource::mount_path()` mounts built-ins at `built-in: <name>`, the path the Setup pane's Library list already uses.

title: feat(setup): per-setup post options and the setup's own tool-list export
body:
## What changed
**Post options per setup** (same own / follow-the-document law #343 gave the post itself):
- `SetupDef.post_options: Option<PostOptions>`; `None` follows the document (every older file and every new setup).
- New undoable command `SetSetupPostOptions`; a no-op request is refused by name. A datum transfer copies the source setup's options with its post.
- `posting::post_options` returns the active setup's own options, else the document's (mirrors `post_of`). "Skip pauses and homes" is read per operation from that op's setup, so one setup can skip its stops while another keeps them. Output (one file per op) and thread output are program-wide: setups that disagree are refused by name, next to #343's one-mount check.
- Project file: an additive setup key `post_options` (`{"threading":"g32"|"g76","skip_stops":..,"per_op_files":..}`), omitted when `None`; no version step (stays v57), so a document that never sets it saves byte-identically. An unknown threading word is a corrupt-file refusal naming the setup.
- UI: the setup's **Post** page ends with a "Post options" group - radios "Use the document's post options" / "This setup has its own post options" and a note saying whose options the widgets above edit. The existing option widgets route to the active setup's own options when it has them.

**Setup tool-list export**
- `app::tool_list_export` (pure read): rows in first-use order from `tool_list::for_setup` - T number, name, diameter (mm), kind, holder (`D x L` or `none`), ops using it. `.csv` -> RFC 4180 CSV (CRLF, quoted fields); any other extension -> fixed-column text.
- The setup's **Tool list** page gets an "Export tool list…" button (save dialog, CSV/Text filters, default `<Setup>-tools.csv`). A command-free file write like the setup sheet: nothing enters the history.

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (all camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1725 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main: `setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` (#415) and the GPU headless trio (`headless_run_succeeds`, `headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`, `egui_headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`). title: feat(mcp): pick faces, edge chains and loops for an operation's area
body:
## What changed
Four MCP tools so an agent can pick what an operation machines, each write going through the existing undoable commands:

- `list_features {model, kinds?, limit?}`: a model's pickable features in world coordinates - planar faces (normal, facing up/down/side/inclined, area, bounds, the smooth patch it belongs to, each boundary loop outer/hole/open with the edge-chain ids that run it), edge chains (closed, edge count, length, ends, bounds), welded patches and corner vertices. 500 rows per kind by default (`limit` up to 20 000, `truncated` flags a cut).
- Ids are strings `"face:0x…"`, `"chain:0x…"`, `"patch:0x…"`, `"vertex:0x…"` (the geometry-hash ids of `model::features_of`), so a JavaScript client never rounds the 64-bit hash. A loop is picked by passing its chain ids.
- `set_operation_geometry {operation, picks:[{model,id}]}` -> `SetOperationGeometry`, one undo step. `get_operation_geometry {operation}` reads source, area controls and notes.
- `set_operation_area {operation, area}` -> `EditOperationParams::with_area` with the op's current params, one undo step; the object replaces all area controls, `{}` resets.
- Refusals are tool errors: malformed/unknown ids, non-model entities, unknown ops, empty picks, unknown area keys, and a feature kind the op can't take (generation's own refusals, said earlier). None reach the history.
- New code in `mcp/features.rs`, `mcp/pick.rs`, `mcp/area.rs`; `tools.rs` / `mod.rs` get only the registration lines. `operation::selection_drives_region` widened to `pub(crate)`.

Note: #421 (MCP setup tools) also registers tools in `mcp/tools.rs`; whichever merges second takes a trivial merge of the registration lines.

`setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip_starts_from_its_own_stock_and_undoes` was red on main. The **test's expectation** was wrong; the sim code is correct. This is a test-only change.

title: fix(sim): sweep XY arcs exactly in the column engine, not as inscribed chords
body:
## What changed
The program sim's column engine, which feeds the post gate's verdict, now sweeps XY arcs (G2/G3 in G17) on the **true circle**. Before, it cut them as chords drawn inside the arc.

**Why:** the inside chords err on both sides.
- **False gouge (#402):** near a convex corner, the arc's centre is the part's corner, so the chords bring the simulated tool up to one sagitta closer to the part than the real arc. On the issue's L-block, one 0.375 mm column 0.088 mm inside the riser corner was clipped. Judged by height alone, that read as a 10 mm gouge, and the post gate refused a clean 2D Contour.
- **Hidden real cuts:** at a concave corner the part lies outside the arc, and the chords stopped up to one sagitta (`cell/4`) short of the wall. A small over-cut there went unseen. On a bull-nose helix arc, a column the true arc cuts 2.5 mm deep was missed.

**Fix:** a new `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/dexel_arc.rs` (302 lines, provenance header) sweeps every tool shape (flat disc, ball, cone, bull nose) along the exact arc.
- **Reach window:** for each column, the reachable stretch of arc has a closed form from the circle-point distance law (`d² = (R−ρ)² + 4Rρ·sin²(u/2)`).
- **Flat tools and level arcs:** exact.
- **Helical ball, cone and bull arcs:** the window is split where the bottom's curvature can change sign, and each piece is searched with samples plus a golden section. The search only returns real evaluations, so it never cuts deeper than the tool went.
- **Arc end points** are judged as discs.
- **Unchanged:** XZ/YZ arcs keep their chords, the gouge verdict (`deviate`) gets no slack or tolerance, and #299 / #303 are untouched.

**Why it's conservative both ways:** the simulated swept area *is* the real arc's swept area. It cannot reach toward the part where the real tool didn't, and it cannot leave material the real arc cut. Alternatives considered and dropped (in `docs/decisions/402-arc-chord-sagitta.md`):
- outside chords, which hide concave gouges;
- mixed chords, which over-cut both ways;
- an exact arc only in the verdict, which leaves the stock wrong and is close to #299's slack question;
- finer chords, which only shrink the error.

## Pinning tests
- **New `app/tests/contour_arc_sim.rs`:** the issue's MCP job on the L-block. The post gate reports no gouge. This failed before the fix.
- **New `sim/tests/arc_sweep.rs`** (5 tests; the old code fails 4):
  - flat-tool exactness, including sweeps over 180° and a sweep crossing ±180°;
  - every tool shape, level and helical, matched against a dense true-arc scan;
  - the issue's own lattice, column (146,13);
  - a **planted convex gouge** (corner arc R 2.5 with a 3 mm tool), still convicted at 10 mm;
  - a **concave fillet** case: clean when correct, and when over-cut by 0.06 mm, it flags exactly the wall columns the true arc reaches.
- **Rewritten in place:** `stock_sim::arc_chords_under_sweep_so_the_sim_only_over_reports` is now `xy_arcs_sweep_the_true_arc_whatever_the_chord_budget`, so the test count is unchanged. The old name asserted the chords were conservative, which they weren't.
- **`stock_bull_nose::both_engines_cut_a_bull_nose_alike`:** straight moves still need 1e-5 agreement. The helix arc now uses `arc_parity`, which allows the field engine's chord error away from the cut's edge, because the field engine still chords. That is filed as **#413**.

## Readings
- The worker ran the batch tier: geometry, cl, tools, post, sim and app all pass, including `golden_cl`, `posting`, `stock_sim_document`, `setup_carry`, `stock_engine_agreement` and `rotary_field_parity`.
- No golden changed.
- clippy `-D warnings` is clean for all crates.
- **Quick gate after merging upstream/main** (clean): post, sim and app are green. The remaining reds also fail on main: `swarf_pose_continuity` (#351) and the GPU headless tests.
- **Side effect:** rest material and 3D roughing's prior stock (`machining3d::feed` uses `Dexel::subtract`) now also see the exact arc.

**For the maintainer:** this changes the simulator behind the post gate's verdict. Please give it a close look, even though it is flagged ready.

Changelog: The program sim cuts XY arcs on the true circle instead of inscribed chords, so the post gate no longer reports a false gouge at a convex arc corner and no longer misses a sub-sagitta cut at a concave one (#402)

Fixes #402

title: feat(carry): fixtures read the carried stock; lathe carry refused by name; carried body cached
body:
Stacked on #410.

## What changed
- **Workholding reads the carried stock** (`app::fixture_carried`, post gate). In a setup entered with a carried body (#317), each tagged fixture is checked against the body the setup is entered with (`rest::entered_body`). A fixture standing inside material the earlier setups left (column centres strictly inside its footprint, Z overlap beyond the 1 nm fixture tolerance) refuses the post by name: setup, fixture, origin setup, depth (`FIXTURE_IN_CARRIED`). A fixture seated on a face setup 1 machined is clear, even where the declared block still reaches through it. The check runs live, like every workholding law, and the machine table is not read. Tool and holder against the carried stock were already judged by #410's union box. This change adds the fixtures themselves read against the carried body.
- **Lathe / mill-turn second op: refused by name, not implemented.** The reasons are in the decision record. The refusal is now one constant, `stock_sim::CARRY_MACHINE_REFUSAL`. Generation and the rest chain name it. A path cut on the mill before the machine changed goes stale, because its stamp digests the refused carry, so the sim and the post refuse that op by name.
- **Carried-body cache** (`rest::carried_cache`). `rest::across::carried_body` is memoized: thread-local, the 4 most recently used bodies, keyed by everything the sweep reads (origin stock placement/signature/shape, lattice radius, every turn, every cutting atom's exact moves and tool atom). Names, the consumer setup's own ops (for the entered body), the viewport and the gate never enter the key. A stock without a geometry signature is never cached. The cache is cleared on `project::open` and `world::new_world`. The test-visible counter is `rest::carried_body_computes()`.

## How tested
New suite `carried_fixtures_cache` (5 tests):
- `a_jaw_modelled_into_material_setup1_left_refuses_the_post`: the collision exists only against carried material outside the declared stock. Gate and post refuse, 3.00 mm deep.
- `a_jaw_where_setup1_faced_the_material_away_is_clear`: no false positive where setup 1 removed material that the declared block still claims.
- `the_carried_body_is_not_recomputed_on_an_unrelated_edit`: the consumer's feed edit, an upstream rename and a gate read are hits. An upstream Face edit recomputes and the regenerated verdict reads the new body, so nothing stale is served.
- `a_new_document_starts_with_no_carried_body_cached`
- `a_carry_on_a_lathe_or_mill_turn_is_refused_by_name_on_every_path` (Lathe and Mill-turn)

Gated in the worktree (debug): carried_fixtures_cache, carried_verify, setup_carry, rest_across_setups, fixtures, stock_sim_document, posting, golden_cl, lathe_field_sim, setup_relative, commands_undo all pass. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised / owed
- `stock_sim::incoming_body` (the program walk #320's display reads) does not go through the cache.
- No heavy-lane measurement on the big fixtures. The counter pins the behaviour.
- Fixture sampling resolves to the carried grid's pitch. An overlap narrower than half a cell beside a face can pass. This is stated in the decision record.
- #408's `Entry::NewBlock` breaks the chain like the clip, so the cache needs no extra rule whichever lands second.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/321-carry-fixtures-cache.md`.

Changelog: A later setup's fixtures are checked against the stock carried from earlier setups (a fixture modelled into that material blocks the post by name); a lathe/mill-turn part flip is refused by name; the carried body is cached and recomputed only when an upstream input changes (#321)

Fixes #321

title: fix(sim): refuse carrying stock between setups on different machines
body:
## What changed
Follow-up from the review of #401 (carry the machined body into the next setup).

**The missing refusal.** #401's notes credit the cross-machine refusal to "#390's refusal", but no such check existed in the program sim. #390 is the browser tree. The only mount refusals (#343) sit at generation and at post, and the sim walk checked only the **active** setup's machine kind.

Changes in `crates/app/src/stock_sim_carry.rs` (the constant is re-exported from `stock_sim.rs`):
- **New refusal:** `CARRY_MACHINE_REFUSAL`, raised by `one_machine(world, from, to)`. It compares the two setups' own machines (`setup_mount::machine_of`: the setup's machine, else the document's). The message names both setups and both machines, e.g. `'Setup1' on no machine, 'Setup2' on Tormach 770M`.
- **At the carry:** `carry::entry` refuses a carry onto another machine. The lathe/mill-turn check now reads the two setups' shared machine instead of the active setup's. Because `entry` is shared with the rest reading (#318), an op in the later setup is refused at generation with `REST_CARRY_REFUSAL` plus the machine reason.
- **In the program walk:** `carry::walk` (behind `simulate_document` and `incoming_body`) refuses every setup change onto another machine. That includes a clip between setups that hold the part the same way, because a clip keeps what the earlier setup left standing.
- **Clip in the rest reading:** deliberately **not** refused. There, the later setup starts from its own block and reads nothing across. Refusing it would block generation in every two-machine document whose setups hold the part alike, which #343 allows.

**Off-grid alignment** is represented exactly, so it is pinned rather than refused. `Body::carry` takes the image origin from the turned lattice corners, so every image cell centre is a transformed source centre, and nothing snaps to the old grid.

`docs/decisions/317-carry-body.md` is left unedited, per the decisions README (a PR does not edit another PR's file). `docs/decisions/404-carry-machine-check.md` records the correction.

## Pinning tests
- `sim/tests/stock_carry.rs::an_odd_lattice_carried_off_the_grid_keeps_whole_cells`: a 7 × 5 lattice at 0.5 mm with a distinct height per column. It is carried through a flip over X and a quarter turn, each translated by (0.37, −1.13). The test checks a one-to-one column map, image centres equal to the transformed source centres, exact heights, and exact origin, volume and bounds.
- `app/tests/setup_carry.rs::a_carry_between_setups_on_different_machines_is_refused_by_name`: generation is refused naming both setups and both machines. `simulate_document` and `incoming_body` error, and undo restores the carry bit for bit.
- `app/tests/setup_carry.rs::a_clip_between_setups_on_different_machines_is_refused_by_name`: generation still works, and the program sim refuses by name.
- `app/tests/setup_carry.rs::a_flip_about_a_centre_off_the_grid_carries_whole_cells`: a part centred off-grid in a 61 × 47 block, flipped. The incoming body is the exact mirror, and the verdict shows no gouge.

## Readings
- These suites all pass: `setup_carry` 8, `rest_across_setups` 5, `stock_sim_document` 9, `setup_align` 9, `setup_mount` 6, `setup_relative` 8, `setups` 11, app lib 95, `stock_carry` 7, `stock_sim` 24.

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- No posted G-code and no GUI change.

Changelog: The program sim refuses by name to carry or clip the stock between setups on different machines (it used to check only the active setup's machine) (#404)

Fixes #404

title: feat(verify): later setups judge rapids and entries against the carried body
body:
Was stacked on #405 (#318), which has merged; this branch has `origin/main` merged in and targets `main`.

## What changed

- **A later setup's verdict never sees less material than the carried body.** When an op's setup is entered with a carried body (#317 / #318's chain), `operation::carried_stock::judged` checks the setup's declared stock against the incoming body. The first check is cheap: the origin stock box carried uncut through the turns. If that fails, the real carried grid is cut and its bounds are clamped to the uncut block. If the declared stock is a box that already holds the body, nothing changes. Otherwise the job's `stock_facets` / `stock_aabb` become the box enclosing both. Every stock-reading law reads that box: the rapid-in-stock column and footprint rings, the stock top, the entry/plunge solid, reach, top-stock, and the tilted slab. The prior acquittal still clears dives into material earlier setups really cut. The post blocks on the same cached WARN records, so post and generation agree.
- **A mismatch is named, and refused wherever a feed move cuts into it** (review round 2). If a feed move reaches carried material outside the declared stock, the path carries `operation::CARRIED_OUTSIDE_DECLARED`, which names both setups, the overhang and the move, and the post gate (`operation::carried_problems`) refuses by name. The reach test reads the carried grid's columns under each feed chord's footprint box. An overhang that no feed move reaches is only noted (`CARRIED_OUTSIDE_NOTED`).
- **Declared material beyond the carried block is present** (#405 review a). Where the declared stock reaches past the uncut carried block in XY, neither verify's prior nor the rest mask is read, and the raw stock judges. Before this, the prior acquitted a dive there because its disc still caught the grid's low edge cells. The fix is pinned, and the test fails without it.
- **A refused carry refuses every op of the setup**, posed ones included. Before, only ops that read the prior were refused. A posed op in a carried setup now carries the rest-chain digest in its stamp (`rest::carried_digest`). No other stamp moves.
- `rest::across`: `carried_stock_block`, `carried_stock_body`, `carried_digest`. `carried_grid` can stop at the body the consumer setup is entered with.

## Not done here (refused or owed, see `docs/decisions/319-carried-verify.md`)

- Non-rest kinds still use the declared stock as their machining region (Face, 2D pocket/adaptive, contour). Carried material outside it is judged but not machined, and the note says so. A declared stock larger than the carried body still cuts air there. Pocket3D and Multi-Axis Rough already bound their cut by #318's mask. Bounding every kind's region is #320's stock-source question.
- Lateral rapids are still acquitted only as today: vertical dives only (#96).
- #408 (#320, the per-setup stock source) is not merged yet. This code keys on `carry::entry` through #318's chain, so whichever PR lands second makes the chain honour the source.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/carried_verify.rs` (new, 5 tests):
- `a_dive_clear_of_the_declared_block_into_carried_material_is_refused`: Setup2's declared top is 5 and the carried body stands to 9. The contour's dive is convicted, the note names Setup1/Setup2, and `post_setup` is blocked on that rapid move.
- `a_dive_into_material_setup1_removed_is_allowed`
- `a_flipped_carry_judges_the_dive_against_the_flipped_body` (#405 review c)
- `declared_stock_beyond_the_carried_block_is_judged_present` (#405 review a; it fails with the prior read)
- `a_turn_off_the_quarter_with_only_a_non_rest_op_after_it_is_refused_by_name` (#405 review b). With a 30-degree turn, the non-rest op's generation is refused with `CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL` naming both setups, and the program sim and the gate never judge it. With every op of the setup now refused at generation, `simulate_document` cannot reach the carry itself: it refuses earlier, on the stale op.

## Gate (on the tree merged with current main)

Debug, own target dir, camcraft-app: carried_verify (5), rest_across_setups (5), setup_carry (5), vertical_rapid_stock (10), posting (17), golden_cl (23, goldens unchanged), stock_sim_document (9), setups (11), operations (117 + 6 ignored), drill_prior (12), drill_prior_kinds (4), top_stock (4), remachining (6), suppressed_rest (2), setup_relative (8), setup_align (9), stock_stamp (4), lib (95). All green. clippy `-D warnings` on camcraft-app, all targets: clean. The sim crate is not touched.

Changelog: In a later setup that holds the body carried from earlier setups, rapids, entries and links are judged against that body even where it stands outside the setup's declared stock. A feed move into carried stock outside the declared stock refuses the post by name, any other mismatch is noted, and a carry the lattice cannot hold refuses every operation of that setup.

Fixes #319

## Summary

- Move `DeleteSetup`, including the operation and linked-setup deletion guards and undo snapshots, into `commands/setup_delete.rs` without changing behavior. Preserve `commands::DeleteSetup` and `commands::setup::DeleteSetup`; keep the shared stock snapshot internal to commands.
- Pin a generated linked child's toolpath becoming stale when its parent's alignment moves it, fresh again after one undo without regeneration, and stale after redo.
- Remove the stray blank line in `commands/setup_align.rs` and record the bounded decision in `docs/decisions/398-setup-delete-staleness.md`.

`commands/setup.rs` is now 335 lines (from 445); the deletion module is 124 lines.

## Pinning and preservation

`a_parent_alignment_makes_a_linked_childs_toolpath_stale_and_undo_restores_it` uses the real link, activate, create, generate and history commands. It first proves the operation belongs to the linked child and has a nonempty fresh path. A parent quarter-turn must move the child's alignment and a transformed part corner while leaving the square stock's shape/location unchanged, then report `Stale`; undo restores placement and `Ok`, and redo restores `Stale`.

Independent static review compared the complete moved `DeleteSetup` definition with the base: equal after whitespace normalization, including refusal order/messages, furniture ownership, removal and restoration. No actionable findings. Existing setup tests are retained; exactly one regression was added. No production transform/stamp, safety gate, schema or dependency change.

Readings: issue #398 and its thread; current `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `docs/decisions/README.md`; setup command/alignment/relative, history and operation-stamp code and existing setup fixtures. No vendor implementation or assets consulted.

## Validation

Native Windows verification on this PR's exact tree, based on `37eacee3c7431ffd05783d84f38b7d18ad8dd623`:

- Exact new regression: **1 passed**.
- `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -Base 37eacee3c7431ffd05783d84f38b7d18ad8dd623`: **870 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored**, two steps, exit 0 (app 818; mapped UI integration 52).
- All eight app `setup*.rs` suites: **58 passed**. Seven ran in quick; the omitted `setup_defines_wcs` ran separately (**4 passed**). These counts overlap the quick/regression results and are not additive.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0.
- New-module Rust 2024 rustfmt check and base-to-tree `git diff --check`: exit 0.

The committed tree matches the independently reviewed and verified tree. Current-main integration preview is clean; no unrelated main advance was folded into the tested candidate.

Not exercised: full release/heavy lanes (8 ignored in quick), Linux/macOS, manual UI or CNC. Internal UI setup-tree tests were not separately selected by the mapped gate. Graphify is unavailable, so source-level inspection was used. Hosted checks are intentionally absent under repository policy; no hosted CI-green claim.

Changelog: none (behavior-preserving extraction and regression coverage).

Fixes #398

title: feat(setup): per-setup stock source and the incoming stock on the setup page
body:
Was stacked on #401 (#317), now merged - this PR targets `main`.

## What changed

- **A per-setup stock source** (`SetupDef::stock_source: Option<StockSource>`, `camcraft_app::setup_stock`): `Own` ("Its own stock (the Stock node)") or `FromPrevious` ("What <previous setup> leaves behind"). The first setup has no choice.
- **`SetSetupStockSource`** (undoable): validated at construction - not the first setup, a carry the sim can verify (refused by name otherwise), and a real change. Undo restores the stored value, including "never picked". The pick rides the setup's operation stamps, so its operations go Stale.
- **Sim** (`stock_sim_carry::entry`): `FromPrevious` carries the body (#317). `Own` keeps the M3.2 A clip when the part is held the same way, and takes a **new block** when it is held differently. When the program moves to a new block, the gouges of the block it leaves are folded into the program verdict (`fold_left`), so a gouge cut before the new block still blocks the post.
- **Setup page** (`setup_stock_pick.rs`): the option is enabled from the second setup on. A refused carry disables it, with the reason as hover text. If the unpicked default is a refused carry, the page names the reason in error ink and points to "Its own stock". When the setup takes what the previous one leaves, the page shows the incoming body's box and volume and says the setup's own Stock node is not cut from (#401's reviewer note). These are measured once per document version, not every frame.
- **Setup sheet**: STOCK prints `source   <words>` for setups after the first. For a carried stock it also prints the incoming box and volume.
- **Project v57**: `"stock_source": "own" | "from_previous"`. The key is absent when the source was never picked. An unknown word is a corrupt file, refused by name. This is not breaking: v56 files load and simulate unchanged.

## Default mapping (existing files are byte-identical)

An unpicked source (`None`) is #401's implicit rule:

| Setup 2+ against the setup before it | Reads as | Sim |
|---|---|---|
| placed relative to it (#316 link, "Same as" included) | What it leaves behind | carry |
| holds the part differently | What it leaves behind | carry |
| holds the part alike, not linked | Its own stock | M3.2 A clip |

Nothing is written to a file or a stamp until a pick is made. The goldens are unchanged, and every `setup_carry` test passes as it did. Decisions: `docs/decisions/320-stock-source.md`.

## Not in this PR

The viewport preview of the incoming body is follow-up #406. The viewport has no overlay path for a column body yet.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/setup_stock_source.rs` (new, 6): `unpicked_setups_read_the_317_rule_and_simulate_unchanged`, `a_new_block_after_a_flip_starts_from_its_own_stock_and_undoes`, `a_gouge_before_a_new_block_still_reads_in_the_verdict`, `a_refused_carry_and_the_first_setup_cannot_be_picked`, `the_pick_round_trips_and_older_or_broken_files_read_by_name`, `the_setup_sheet_states_the_stock_source`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_stock_tests.rs` (new, 3): `the_first_setup_offers_no_choice`, `picking_what_setup1_leaves_shows_the_incoming_stock_and_undoes`, `a_refused_carry_disables_the_option_with_its_reason`
- `setup_relative`: the version assert moves from 56 to 57.

## Gate (on the branch merged with current main)

- app: lib (95), setup_stock_source (6), setup_carry (5), setups (11), setup_relative (8), setup_align (9), project_roundtrip (69), commands_undo (32), setup_sheet (7), stock_sim_document (9), golden_cl (23, goldens unchanged), posting (17), post_not_judged (4): all green
- ui lib from CWD crates/ui: 308 passed, 2 ignored. No snapshot changed.
- clippy `-D warnings` on camcraft-app and camcraft-ui, all targets: clean

Changelog: A setup after the first can take its own stock or what the setup before it leaves behind; the setup page shows the incoming stock's box and volume and names why a carry is refused, and the setup sheet states the source (project v57).

Fixes #320

title: feat(post): machine files for the PCNC 770 and PCNC 1100 from their manuals
body:
## What changed
Four more Tormach machine files, each built from its own operator's manual. They follow the pattern from #259.

| File | Machine | Manual | Spindle (belts) | Rapid = feed ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tormach-pcnc770-s3.mch` | PCNC 770 (Series 3) | 32426 Rev C1-1 (2011), p. 9-2 | 175–10200 rpm (175–3250 / 525–10200) | X/Y 135, Z 100 IPM |
| `tormach-pcnc1100-s1.mch` | PCNC 1100 (Series I) | 30625 Rev C4-1 (2008), p. 9-2 | 300–4500 rpm (300–1750 / 800–4500) | 65 IPM on all axes |
| `tormach-pcnc1100-s2.mch` | PCNC 1100 (Series II) | 31138 Rev B1-4, p. 9-2 | 100–5140 rpm (100–2000 / 250–5140) | X/Y 90, Z 65 IPM |
| `tormach-pcnc1100-s3.mch` | PCNC 1100 (Series 3) | UM10087 1013A (2013), p. 121 | 100–5140 rpm (100–2000 / 250–5140) | X/Y 110, Z 90 IPM |

- **Common to all four:** inch, R8 spindle, coolant M7 mist / M8 flood, and `rigid_tapping: false`. These manuals tap with tapping-head macros (M871–M874), so the Tormach post refuses G84 by name on these machines, as it already does on the 770M and PCNC 440.
- **Spindle power** is the continuous rating, not the peak, as in the PCNC 440 file: 770 S3 0.75 kW, the 1100s 1.12 kW.
- **Travel:** 770 S3 is 14 × 7.5 × 13.25 in. The 1100s are 18 × 9.5 × 16.5 in.
- **Registration:** the files are registered in `MACHINES` (`crates/app/src/posting.rs`).
- **Text-only edits:** the README's machine list, and the rigid-tap comment in `tormach.cps` (no output change).

**Manual identification.** The decisions file records every figure with its manual, page and revision.
- `pcnc1100-3-um-c4.1` is the **Series I** manual (C4-1, 2008). The Series II manual's revision history confirms this.
- UM10087 1013A is the **Series 3** manual: its page footers read "PCNC_1100_SERIES_3".
- The two 770 manuals differ only in the X/Y rapid: B1-4 (the pre-Series-3 770) gives 130 IPM and C1-1 (Series 3) gives 135. Only Series 3 got a file.

**Still open on #170:** the PathPilot-era **1100M / 1100M+** that PathPilot Hub lists. We have no manual for them, so this PR says `Refs #170`.

## Readings / tests
- `tormach_machines` 5/5. Its manual-figures table now has 10 rows, and there are belt-note checks for the Series I ranges, the 1100s' 150 rpm low range and the 770 S3's 10100 rpm high range. All four new machines are covered by the rigid-tap refusal test.
- `machine` 32/32, `tormach_post` 10/10, `posting` 17/17.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` (upstream/main merged, clean): post, sim and app are green. The remaining reds also fail on upstream main: `swarf_pose_continuity` (fixed by #351) and the GPU headless tests.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.

**Not exercised:** a Hub simulation. PathPilot Hub has no simulator for these Mach3-era machines; the closest is the 770M. A GUI check of the machine list is pending with the contributor, so this stays a draft until that is done.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/170-tormach-pcnc.md`.

Changelog: Machine files for the Tormach PCNC 770 (Series 3) and PCNC 1100 (Series I, II, 3), each from its operator's manual; these R8 mills refuse rigid taps by name (#170)

Refs #170

title: feat(rest): rest machining across carried setups; upstream changes stale later setups
body:
## What changed

Was stacked on #401 (#317). That PR has merged, so this branch has origin/main merged in and targets `main`.

- **Rest crosses setups where the body is carried.** A Setup2 op that reads the program ahead (a Pocket3D or MultiAxisRough rest mask, the verify prior used by the rapid, reach and top-stock laws) now reads what Setup1 cut. The rest grid is the origin setup's block. Each setup's cut moves are swept into it, and the body is carried at every boundary through `stock_sim::carry::entry` + `Body::carry`, which is the same call the program sim makes (`crates/app/src/rest/across.rs`, new).
- **Clip-entered setups keep their own block.** Two setups that hold the part the same way and are not linked are entered by the M3.2 A clip. Rest there still starts from the setup's own block, as before. It is not yet stated whether that setup gets a fresh blank or the same part (#320), and the fresh block never assumes material is gone.
- **Staleness.** When the chain crosses a setup boundary, the rest digest adds the setups it crosses, each lattice turn and the origin setup's stock to the predecessors' path digest. So any of these stales the later op: regenerating a Setup1 op, re-aligning, linking or unlinking a setup, a Setup1 stock edit, a deletion or a reorder. Undo un-stales it. `stale_reason` names the predecessor and the carry.
- **Suppressed-ahead refusal** (`rest::suppressed_cuts_ahead`, #161) walks the same chain, so a suppressed Setup1 cut refuses the Setup2 op at the post by name.
- `operation::write_setup_stock` and `carry::first_body` are now `pub(crate)`. `rest.rs` was split, with the pilot and turned readings moved to `rest/pilots.rs` (400-line law).

## Refused by name

- **A carry the lattice refuses** (side-on turns, Z turns off the quarter, lathe or mill-turn). Every `reads_prior` op in the receiving setup is refused at `collect_job` with `REST_CARRY_REFUSAL` plus the carry's own reason, which names both setups. It is never generated against a fresh block.
- Left for #319, unchanged here: raw-stock convictions in a later setup still read that setup's declared block. The carried prior only *acquits*, and only where the carried body really is cut. Convicting against carried material that stands outside the declared block is #319's job. `drills_ahead` and `turned_ahead` stay same-setup; they are lathe-only, and the carry is refused on a lathe.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/318-rest-across-setups.md`.

## Readings

- Setup2 linked "Same as" Setup1: Rest2's path is bit-identical to the same op's path when both ops sit in one setup. With the clip (not linked), Rest2 re-cuts the pocket Rough1 cleared, and its cutting length below the stock top is strictly larger.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/rest_across_setups.rs` (new, 5 tests):
  - `a_second_setup_rest_pass_skips_what_the_first_setup_cleared`
  - `a_change_ahead_in_the_first_setup_stales_the_second_setups_rest_and_undo_restores_it`
  - `a_suppressed_first_setup_cut_refuses_the_second_setups_rest_by_name`
  - `a_clip_entered_setup_does_not_read_the_first_setups_cuts`
  - `a_carry_the_lattice_refuses_refuses_the_rest_reading_by_name`
- `setup_carry::a_turn_the_lattice_cannot_carry_is_refused_by_name`: the refusal now arrives earlier, at Face2's generation, and names the carry. Before, it only reached the program sim.

## Gate (on the tree merged with current main)

- app: lib (95), rest_across_setups (5), remachining (6), suppressed_rest (2), setup_carry (5), setup_relative (8), setups (11), setup_align (9), posting (17), golden_cl (23, goldens unchanged), operations (117 + 6 ignored), drill_prior (12), drill_prior_kinds (4), drilling_axial (7), stock_stamp (4), stock_sim_document (9), lathe_field_sim (6): all green
- clippy `-D warnings` on camcraft-app and camcraft-sim, all targets: clean. The sim crate is not touched.

Changelog: Rest machining in a later setup reads the stock carried from earlier setups (rest passes skip material already removed), an upstream change marks the later setup's operations Stale, and a carry the lattice cannot hold refuses the rest-reading operation by name.

Fixes #318

title: feat(sim): carry the machined body into the next setup
body:
## What changed

- **The program sim carries the machined body into the next setup.** When the program enters a setup that holds the part differently from the one before it, or one placed relative to it with #316's link ("Same as" included), the body the earlier setups left is moved through `setup_relative::transform_between`. The later setup starts from that body, not from a fresh block. #341/#326's refusal "the program spans setups that hold the part differently" is lifted for these programs.
- **Engine** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/carry.rs`, new): `Body` is a two-sided column body, with a top (the existing dexel) and a floor per column. `LatticeTurn` reads the rigid transform. The carry re-indexes the lattice. It never re-samples.
- **App walk** (`crates/app/src/stock_sim_carry.rs`, new): `simulate_document` walks the program through `carry::walk`. At each setup change it either carries or keeps the old clip. The verdict is read in the frame of the setup the program ends in. The M3.2 A clip moved here unchanged.
- **`stock_sim::incoming_body(world, setup)`** returns the stock a setup starts from, in that setup's frame. #318 (rest) and #320 (incoming-stock display) can use it.

## Design (per #308's research decision)

There is one body, viewed through each setup's transform. It is not re-sampled onto each setup's grid.
- **Which turns carry exactly:** flips over X or Y, quarter turns about Z, and their products. These are the eight signed permutations that keep Z on +-Z. Each one maps every column centre exactly onto a column centre of the image lattice, so no value is interpolated.
- **Two sides:** a flip swaps the sides (`top' = tz - floor`, `floor' = tz - top`). A column that was cut through stays cut through.
- **Floor verdict:** once the floor has faced a tool (after a flip), it is judged against the part's bottom, so a gouge cut before the flip is still judged after it. A body that is never flipped gets exactly the old one-sided verdict.
- **Carry vs clip:** two setups that hold the part the same way and are not linked keep the M3.2 A clip. This is #320's planned default, before #320 makes it a per-setup choice.
- **Incoming stock:** a carried setup's own stock entity is not read by the sim. Its incoming stock is the carried body.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/317-carry-body.md`.

## What is refused (by name)

- A turn the lattice cannot carry exactly: side-on, Z turns off the quarter, mirrors. The refusal is `CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL` and names both setups.
- A lathe or mill-turn machine.
- Lathe, rotary and posed programs, refused before the walk as before.
- Setups with different machines (#390's refusal, unchanged).
- The field view and playback still draw one setup only. Their refusal text now says the program verdict carries the stock.

## Readings

- **Flip over X** (stock Z -2..18, part Z 0..16, Setup1 faces to 16): Setup2's incoming body spans Z 0..18 and holds 60x60x18 = 64800 mm³ exactly. The 2 mm Setup1 removed is absent from below. After Setup2 faces the former bottom to 16, the verdict is clean on both sides, and every column matches a single-frame reference (block Z 0..18 faced to 16) within DEV_TOL.
- **Gouge before the flip:** Setup1 faces to 15, 1 mm into the part. After the flip the verdict reads a gouge of exactly 1.0 mm at Z 1, on the floor side.
- **Quarter turn:** the 60x40 block lies 40x60, Setup1's face stays on top at 16, the volume is unchanged and the verdict is clean.
- **Identity:** Setup2 linked "Same as Setup1" gives the same verdict, bit for bit, as both faces in one setup.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/sim/tests/stock_carry.rs` (new, 6 tests):
  - `identity_carries_the_body_onto_itself`
  - `a_flip_over_x_swaps_the_sides_exactly_and_twice_is_home`
  - `a_quarter_turn_reindexes_the_lattice_and_four_are_home`
  - `turns_the_lattice_cannot_carry_are_refused_by_name`
  - `a_flipped_body_is_judged_on_both_sides`
  - `a_column_cut_through_is_air_to_the_eye_and_a_gouge_to_the_verdict`
- `crates/app/tests/setup_carry.rs` (new, 5 tests):
  - `a_flipped_setup_starts_from_what_the_first_one_cut`
  - `a_gouge_cut_before_the_flip_is_still_judged_after_it`
  - `a_quarter_turn_carries_the_body_reindexed`
  - `a_setup_linked_same_as_the_first_carries_the_body_unchanged`
  - `a_turn_the_lattice_cannot_carry_is_refused_by_name`
- `crates/app/tests/setup_align.rs`: `the_program_sim_refuses_by_name_across_differently_held_setups` is now `the_program_sim_carries_the_stock_across_differently_held_setups`. That behaviour changed on purpose.

## Gate (on the tree merged with current main)

- sim: `stock_carry` (6), `stock_sim` (24), `stock_columns`, `stock_backend_parity` - all green
- app: lib (95), `setup_carry` (5), `setup_align` (9), `setup_relative` (8), `setups` (11), `stock_sim_document` (9), `posting` (17), `golden_cl` (23, goldens unchanged), `post_not_judged` (4), `lathe_field_sim` (6), `rotary_field_parity` (3 + 1 ignored heavy lane) - all green
- clippy `-D warnings` on camcraft-sim and camcraft-app, all targets: clean

Changelog: The program sim carries the machined stock into the next setup through the setup transform (flips over X/Y, quarter turns about Z), so a later setup starts from what the earlier one cut and a gouge cut before a flip is still reported; other turns are refused by name.

Builds on #397 (merged).

Fixes #317
