title: fix(world): finish flecs' OS API setup once, before the first world
body:
## What changed
A race in flecs' first-world setup crashed test binaries under load: SIGSEGV in `scripting`, and very likely the earlier one-off SIGABRT in `project_roundtrip`.

flecs keeps its OS API (malloc, free, abort, clock hooks) in one process-global C struct, filled in without a lock on the first world.
- `flecs_ecs::ecs_os_api::ensure_initialized` (flecs_ecs 0.2.2) claims the first fill under a mutex, but writes the struct after releasing it.
- `ecs_mini`, the C side of `World::new`, copies the struct and writes it back.
- A second thread creating its first world at that moment can copy a half-written struct. `ecs_mini` then aborts on `ECS_MISSING_OS_API` (SIGABRT) or later calls a NULL hook (SIGSEGV).

**Fix:** `crates/app/src/world.rs`. `new_world()`, the only place a `World` is built (a grep finds no other `World::new` / `World::default`), now runs `ecs_os_api::ensure_initialized` once behind a `std::sync::Once`, before building any world. After that first fill, flecs marks the API initialised and later constructions only read it. No `unsafe`, and no change to the vendored C.

## Readings
- **Stack**, captured with lldb from a reproduced crash: `abort <- ecs_mini.cold.1 <- ecs_mini (flecs.c:21288, ecs_os_has_heap check) <- ecs_init <- World::default <- camcraft_app::world::new_world <- script::Env::fresh <- script::run`. At the same moment a sibling test thread was inside `ecs_set_hooks_id` building another world.
- **Scripting suite**, 8 parallel copies, `--test-threads=32`: before, 7 crashes in 1200 runs (6 SIGSEGV, 1 SIGABRT); after, 0 in 1600.
- **`world_init_race` children:** before, 6 crashed in 1920; after, 0 in 3840.
- **`project_roundtrip`**, 6 × 60 runs at 32 threads: 0 crashes in 360.
- **Quick gate** (upstream/main merged, clean): app and post green. The remaining reds also fail on upstream main: `swarf_pose_continuity` (fixed by #351) and the GPU headless tests.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.

## Pinning test
`crates/app/tests/world_init_race.rs::first_worlds_on_many_threads_never_crash` (gate map `app::world`).
- It reruns its own binary as 720 child processes in waves of 24, under spinner load.
- In each child, 32 threads wait at a barrier and then all build their first world. Every child must exit cleanly. It takes about 4 s.
- It is a stress test: without the fix it fails in roughly 2 runs out of 3.

## Not addressed (possible follow-ups)
- **Windows:** flecs bumps `ecs_os_api_init_count` without atomics. That is harmless on POSIX (the guarded hooks are NULL), but a lost update on Windows could run `win_fini` early. Never observed.
- **Stack margin:** a debug script run uses about 950 KB of stack against 2 MiB test threads, so the margin is only about 2x.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/379-scripting-sigsegv.md`.

title: feat(ui): import, place and draw a tool's holder body in the tool editor and sim
body:
**Stacked on #381** (tool bodies: `SetToolBody`, the envelope) **and #348** (tool library buttons in the same editor page). This diff includes both until they merge; the #371 work is e0219f1. Part of #361.

## What changed
**Tool editor: a "Tool body" column.**
- **Import body…** (STEP/STL/OBJ through the app's importer) and **Clear body**.
- Placement controls: an axis combo (±X/±Y/±Z of the model, or a picked direction), **Tip offset**, and **Pick tip** / **Pick axis** toggles.
- A small 3D preview: egui-painted, drag to orbit, no GPU.
- A live placement note ("placed: foot … to top …" or the reason it won't place), and **Apply body**.
- The 2D profile preview draws the placed body's revolved envelope in amber over the cylinders.
- A tool not yet in the document shows "Add the tool first…".

**Picking.** A click casts a ray through `tool_body_view::pick`.
- **Pick tip** snaps to the nearest corner of the hit facet and sets the offset so that corner is the tip.
- **Pick axis** takes the clicked facet's outward normal.
- Picks only fill the fields; they never queue a command.

**Commands.**
- **Apply body** queues one `SetToolBody`, a single undo step. **Clear body** is the same command with `None`.
- Refusals show in the editor by name ("tool body not set: …", "tool body not imported: …") and the draft is kept.
- The draft reloads only when the world's body changes (Apply / Undo / Redo / Open), so an unapplied import survives other edits.

**Simulation.** While the transport runs, the running tool's body is posed at the playhead (read from the cached timeline) and drawn as a shaded, depth-tested part. A tool without a body draws exactly as before.

**App-layer helpers**, so ui stays thin: `crates/app/src/tool_body_view.rs` holds `load`, `preview` (the same place-and-envelope step as the command, uncommitted), `pick`, `tip_offset_at`, `posed` and `body_for_operation`.

`docs/decisions/371-tool-body-ui.md` records why picking lives in the editor's own preview rather than the main viewport. Among other reasons, a pick mode there would compete with the face/edge/vertex picks.

## How tested
- New app `tool_body_view` (6 tests). `tool_body` (8) still passes.
- 6 new structural UI tests (`egui_app/tests/tool_body.rs`):
  - the editor offers Import/Clear;
  - Apply lands one `SetToolBody`, with Undo/Redo and Clear plus its undo;
  - a degenerate placement is refused by name;
  - a tip pick fills the offset and queues nothing;
  - a missing file is refused by name;
  - the sim draws the body at the playhead, and nothing without one.
- `camcraft-ui --lib`: 307 passed. `--test operations`: 31/31. `clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings`: clean.
- **Expected failure: the pixel snapshot `tool_editor_snapshot`.** The editor is wider (third column) and anchored further left, so its pixels changed. The PNG is deliberately **not** regenerated: #359 (#255) moves pixel goldens to the release lane, after which this test runs and is refreshed only at the cut. The headless-GPU tests also fail here (no adapter on this Mac), the same as on main.

## Not exercised (draft until the contributor tries a build)
- Hands-on GUI check: the import, picking, apply/undo and simulation flow, on a release build.
- The body file is read on the UI thread, so a very large vendor STEP freezes the window briefly while loading.
- Not in this slice: lathe-body placement UI (#369's frame), turning the body about its axis for display, and drawing a body outside the simulation.

title: feat(setup): place a setup relative to another; transform between setups
body:
## What changed

- **`setup_relative::transform_between(world, from, to) -> Result<Location, String>`** (new `crates/app/src/setup_relative.rs`): the rigid transform that takes the part as setup `from` holds it to where setup `to` holds it, `T = A_to * A_from^-1`, derived from the two setups' #326 part alignments. It is the identity for a setup and itself, composes (A->C = (B->C)(A->B)) and inverts. It refuses by name a missing setup, a name that is not a setup, and a stored alignment that is not finite or not a unit rotation; it never falls back to the identity. #317 and #318 will read it. `carry_point` maps one point.
- **A setup placed relative to another**: `SetupDef::relative_to: Option<String>` plus the undoable `SetSetupRelative::link(world, setup, parent, [x, y, z] degrees)` / `unlink`. The turn ("Flip over X / Turn 90° about Z / typed angles from Setup1") is applied to the setup's part alignment through `AlignPartToSetup`, so the stock follows the same way it does in #326. The relation shown on the page is read back from the two alignments.
- **A change to the parent carries through**: `AlignPartToSetup` on a setup that others are linked to re-places each of them, including links of links, so each keeps its transform to its parent. Their following stocks move too, all in one undo unit. If any linked setup cannot follow (for example a cylinder stock would lie on its side), the whole change is refused and the message names that setup.
- **Refusals**: linking a setup to itself or closing a loop is refused when the command is built. `DeleteSetup` refuses a setup that another is linked to and names the linked setup. The loader rejects a link to a missing setup, or a loop of links, as a corrupt file before writing anything to the world.
- **Project v56**: `SetupDto::relative_to` (absent = not linked). v55 and older files load unchanged.
- **UI**: every setup after the first gets a "Relative to previous setup" row on its settings page (#390): Not linked / Same as <prev> / the flip and turn presets "from <prev>", plus typed angles with Apply. It queues `CommandKind::SetSetupRelative`, and a refusal goes to the status line.

## Design vs #326's alignment

There is no second transform. #326's per-setup `part_alignment` stays the only stored transform. #316 adds a derived setup-to-setup transform and a link, and the link only carries later edits of the parent. Decisions are in `docs/decisions/316-setup-transform.md`:
- **Datum transfer**: does not link. Its transform is already derivable (the identity when the setup is created). A transfer is a clone, not an alias: its stock and WCS do not follow the source either.
- **Work offset**: no transform is read from it. It is a translation in the setup frame and says where program zero is, not how the part moved. G54-G59 still come from the setup, and rotated offsets are still refused.
- **Child edits its own alignment**: the link stays, and the relation shown is whatever the new difference is.

## Readings

- Flip over X about the part centre (0, 0, 10): top corner (-20, -20, 20) maps to (-20, 20, 0).
- Quarter turn about Z: (-20, -20, 20) maps to (20, -20, 20).
- Parent turned 90° about Z with a linked child (flip) and grandchild (turn): `carried_count() == 2`, both relative transforms are unchanged, and a single undo restores all three.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/setup_relative.rs` (new, 8 tests):
- `transform_between_reads_identity_flip_and_quarter_turn`
- `transforms_compose_and_invert`
- `transform_between_refuses_by_name`
- `a_linked_setup_resolves_its_turn_into_its_alignment_and_undoes`
- `a_change_of_the_parent_carries_into_linked_setups_in_one_undo_unit`
- `a_linked_setup_that_cannot_follow_refuses_the_parent_change_by_name`
- `links_refuse_self_loops_and_missing_setups_and_guard_delete`
- `links_round_trip_and_older_or_broken_files_are_read_by_name`

`crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_relative_tests.rs` (2 tests):
- `the_relative_control_links_the_setup_through_the_command`
- `typed_turns_unlinking_and_refusals_go_through_the_drain`

Gate on the tree merged with current main:
- app: setup_align, setup_mount, setups, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, golden_cl, setup_sheet, one_wcs, setup_relative
- ui: lib, run from `crates/ui`
- clippy `-D warnings` on app and ui (all targets)

Builds on #390 (merged).

Changelog: Setups can be placed relative to the previous setup (same way up, flipped, turned, or by angles); changing that setup's part alignment carries into the linked setups; the transform between two setups is derived from their part alignments (project v56).

Fixes #316

title: feat(turning): judge a modelled lathe holder body against the revolved stock
body:
**Stacked on #381** (#368, tool bodies from STEP). This diff includes #381's commits until it merges; the #369 work is 99273c8 plus a docs fix. Part of #361: the lathe case the issue asks for (Capto/KM holders, boring bars).

## What changed
**Lathe tools can carry a body.** Turning, Groove, Thread, Form and Bore tools accept a body through `SetToolBody::lathe` / `lathe_from_file`. The placement is nine numbers:
- the model direction that is tool +x (radially out, on the path's own meridian side);
- the model direction that is +z (lathe +Z);
- the model point that is the tip (the point the moves already carry).

Directions within 0.01° of square are squared up; anything worse is refused by name. The frame is derived from the existing turning code and documented in `docs/decisions/369-lathe-holder-body.md`.

**Clearance bands** (`crates/tools/src/lathe_holder.rs`):
- The body is cut into bands of at least 0.25 mm along z. Each facet is clipped exactly to each band, which keeps the x and |y| bounds of what it holds.
- With the tip at signed radius X, every body point in the band lies between a radial floor and a ceiling (formulas in the decisions file).
- The ceiling matters for a boring bar, whose far side or flats rub the bore wall; "min x, ignore y" would miss it.
- The bounds are a box around the body's points, so they can only over-report.

**The judge** (`operation/turning_holder*.rs`):
- **Moves:** every feed and rapid is walked at 0.25 mm steps.
- **Reading the material:** each band is read against a station table of the part and the in-process stock (outline knots, facet vertices, a 0.25 mm grid) at its ends and every station inside it, so the skins are read exactly.
- **What stands:** the stock counts less every cut before that instant, by the same reading as the bar law (#146): earlier ops and pilots, the program's facing, this path's earlier cuts, and this move's own sweep so far. The insert's own footprint is excluded.
- **Finding:** a rub is a new `Warning::HolderHit` that **blocks the post**: `<op>: holder body at move N rubs the part - X mm short of clearance`.

**Unchanged without a body.** A turning tool without a body gives identical moves, warnings and goldens. It gains one non-blocking path note, "holder not judged".

**Project file.** No version bump beyond #381's v55. A lathe body is written as `lathe: {radial, along, tip}` with no `axis`/`offset`, so a #381-only reader refuses the file rather than misreading it. The clearance bands are re-derived on load.

## How tested
- New `crates/app/tests/turning_holder.rs` (8):
  - OD holder rubs a stepped part's shoulder: part hit, 3.2 mm short, post refused. The same op without a body is identical.
  - A clear holder passes.
  - Uncut bar under the holder is a stock-only hit; a rough op first clears it.
  - A fat boring bar is a part hit on rapids and feeds; a slim bar passes.
  - A grooving holder 0.05 mm inside the blade band passes; a fat one rubs the walls.
  - Refusals by name: zero, non-square or NaN placement, tip far from the body, empty or flat body, a lathe body on an end mill.
  - Undo; save → load → save byte-identical.
- Unit tests:
  - Tools (6): a randomized check that every facet point sits within its band's radii; facets crossing bands with no vertex in them; the placement mapping.
  - App scene (2): the station-line cut against brute force for a capsule, a disc, a hexagon and a cut through the axis.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main` (macOS): tools, sim and app suites green. Every turning, lathe, golden, project and undo suite is unchanged. In the ui suites, only the three headless-GPU tests fail (no graphics adapter on this machine); they fail the same way on `upstream/main`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests` is clean.

## Not exercised
- No UI: attaching a lathe body is reachable through the command and the project file only (#371).
- No real vendor Capto/KM file was tried, only test meshes. Real vendor files are often large, and the judge's work grows with instants × band runs (see the decisions file).

Changelog: Turning tools can carry a modelled holder or boring-bar body; a body that rubs the part or in-process stock blocks the post by name (#369)

Fixes #369

title: fix(post): engage cutter compensation in G17, never in a stale G18/G19
body:
**Cause.** In `fanuc.cps`, `haas.cps`, `mazak.cps` and `sinumerik.cps`, the modal plane went back to G17 only in three places: before the next XY arc, before a canned cycle, and at section end. So a COMP engage (G41/G42 on the next G01) or a cancel (G40) that came after an XZ (G18) or YZ (G19) arc was written while G18/G19 was still the active plane, and the control compensated in that plane instead of XY. Nothing stopped an XZ/YZ arc from being written while comp was on either.

**Fix (per script; plane and comp state live in the scripts, not the engine).** The same two helpers sit next to `restorePlane` in each of the four posts:
- `compPlaneWord(cg)`: the block that writes G41/G42/G40 starts with `G17` when the modal plane is not 17, e.g. `G17 G01 G42 X0 Y0 Z-2 D02 F500`.
- `compPlaneRefuse(g)`: an XZ/YZ arc that arrives while comp is engaged is refused by name with a counted warning, which blocks the post. It is not written, so the plane never switches under comp.

Fanuc, Haas, Mazak and Siemens 840D are all fixed. Heidenhain, Tormach and the Fanuc lathe already refuse control compensation. A program that never leaves G17 posts byte-identically, so no golden changed. This also makes the "step back to G17 before comp" workaround in PR #393's fixture unnecessary.

**Readings.** All four posts now write G17 on the engage block after a G18 arc and after a G19 arc. The RS-274 modal check finds 0 faults. With the script changes stashed, the two pinning tests fail.

**Pinning tests** (`crates/post/tests/comp_plane.rs`, a small RS-274 modal reader that checks the plane at every G41/G42/G40 and looks for a plane switch while comp is on):
- `every_comp_post_states_g17_before_engaging_after_an_xz_or_yz_arc`
- `every_comp_post_refuses_an_xz_or_yz_arc_while_compensation_is_engaged`
- `a_program_that_never_left_g17_gets_no_extra_plane_word`

**Gate.** camcraft-post: every test binary green (comp, comp_plane, post_engine, axis_direction_cli). camcraft-app: control_comp, wear_comp, conformance, golden_cl, fanuc_post, posting all green, goldens unchanged. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Decision: `docs/decisions/391-comp-plane.md`.

Changelog: Fanuc, Haas, Mazak and Siemens 840D posts state G17 on the cutter-compensation block after an XZ/YZ arc and refuse an XZ/YZ arc while compensation is engaged

Fixes #391

title: feat(post): write an inverted machine axis mirrored - sign, I/J/K, G2/G3, G41/G42
body:
## What changed

Part of #372 (decision: the machine's axis really moves the other way; the CAM side stays right-handed). This builds on #385 (merged), which added the per-axis `direction`. #385 refused posting for any inverted axis. This PR replaces that refusal with a translation, plus named refusals for what is not verified.

- **One place: the engine** (`crates/post/src/post/invert.rs`, called from `engine::run_numbered_with` before any hook). The record stream is mirrored into the controller's frame, so every script sees the controller's coordinates. No script grows sign logic. A standard machine gets its records back untouched.
- **How the machine reaches it:** `machine::mirror` writes `"invertedAxes": [...]`, but only when some axis is inverted, so standard mirrors stay byte-identical. Through the raw door (a `.mch` file's own JSON, the CLI's `--machine`), the engine re-reads `"direction"` with `parse_mch`.
- **Which scripts may post it:** a new manifest flag, `axisInversion = true`, set in `fanuc.cps` and `haas.cps` only. It is documented in `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`.
- The app's verification gate and the CLI keep `Machine::inverted_post_refusal()`. It now refuses only what the post cannot translate (Z or any other letter). The machine editor's note now says "posted mirrored: Fanuc / Haas posts only" for X/Y and "posting refused for this axis" for anything else.
- Decisions are in `docs/decisions/374-inverted-axis-post.md`.

## Translation rules (for each inverted X / Y)

1. That axis's coordinates get the opposite sign. This covers move and cycle end points, arc centres (so I for X and J for Y flip with them), the `StartX/Y` chain and the work-offset origin (`OriginX/Y`). The stock box edges negate and swap (left <-> right, front <-> back).
2. An arc in a plane that contains exactly one inverted axis reverses sense: CW <-> CCW, so G2 <-> G3. Two inverted axes in the same plane cancel.
3. XY cutter compensation swaps sides (G41 <-> G42) when exactly one of X and Y is inverted.

## Refused by name

These are hard `PostError::Refused` errors and nothing is posted. They are not counted warnings, because the CLI writes its output file even when there are warnings. Each refusal is listed once per run.

- An inverted **Z** ("tool-length compensation (G43) and the canned cycles' retract assume the controller's +Z leaves the work"), or any letter other than X / Y.
- Any post script without `axisInversion = true`: Sinumerik, Heidenhain, Mazak, Tormach, Fanuc Lathe, and user scripts.
- Helical arcs, threading cycles, tilted (A/B/C rotary) moves, C-axis live tooling (polar / G12.1).
- Probing (TOUCH/RETREAT/FOUND). Follow-up: #392.
- A stock box edge without its pair.
- A static-grammar axis stating `"reversal": true`. Before this PR that key was silently ignored.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/inverted_equivalence.rs`:
  - `an_inverted_machine_cuts_the_cam_path` is **the key safety test**. A small RS-274 reader interprets the posted Fanuc and Haas programs as a controller whose axes are inverted (X, Y, and X+Y). It maps the motion back through the work offset and compares it with the CAM path: lines, G2/G3 in G17/G18/G19 with I/J/K, the drilled hole, and the physical comp side. Tolerance is 0.002 mm.
  - `the_standard_program_on_an_inverted_machine_strays` is the converse: the untranslated program fails the same reader, so the reader is not a tautology.
- `crates/app/tests/inverted_post.rs` (15 tests):
  - Goldens: `inverted_x_goldens_for_fanuc_and_haas` (`golden/nc/inverted/{fanuc,haas}_x.nc`) and `the_inverted_x_golden_carries_the_translated_words`.
  - Standard machines untouched: `a_standard_machine_posts_byte_identical`, `the_mirror_states_the_inverted_axes_only_when_there_are_any`.
  - Translation of params: `the_stock_box_and_origin_mirror`, `the_raw_door_reads_a_files_direction`.
  - One test per refusal: `a_helical_arc_refuses_by_name`, `a_tilted_move_refuses_by_name`, `live_tooling_refuses_by_name`, `a_threading_cycle_refuses_by_name`, `probing_refuses_by_name`, `every_refusal_is_named_once_in_one_run`, `an_inverted_z_or_other_letter_refuses_by_name`, `every_unverified_dialect_refuses_by_name`, `an_unread_machine_word_refuses_by_name`.
- `crates/app/tests/axis_direction.rs`: the two #385 refusal tests are replaced by `an_inverted_x_machine_posts_the_mirrored_program` (a real document posts through `post_setup`; every X/I word is negated and G2/G3 swapped against the standard post), `an_inverted_z_refuses_posting_by_name` and `the_refusal_names_every_inverted_axis`.
- `crates/post/tests/axis_direction_cli.rs`: `the_cli_posts_an_inverted_x_mirrored`, `the_cli_refuses_an_inverted_z_by_name`, `the_cli_refuses_an_unverified_script_for_an_inverted_x`.

## Gate (quick, debug, this worktree, after merging origin/main)

- app suites, all green: axis_direction 12, inverted_post 15, inverted_equivalence 2, posting 17, conformance 6, golden_cl 23, fanuc_post 8, machine 32, control_comp 5, wear_comp 5, arc_planes 8, c_axis_live 4, heidenhain_arc_centre 2, heidenhain_block_form 4, lathe_post 7, lathe_post_g76 5, lathe_post_refusals 5, probe_op 11, scripting 17, tormach_machines 5.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`, all green: post_engine 33, comp 9, axis_direction_cli 3.
- None of the existing goldens changed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Not exercised: the machine editor's new note (the GUI was not launched), and any real controller.

Found on the way: #391. Fanuc/Haas engage G41/G42 while a G18/G19 plane is still modal. This is not specific to inversion; the probe stream steps back to G17 before its COMP so the goldens do not lock that behaviour.

Changelog: A machine with an inverted X and/or Y axis now posts through the Fanuc and Haas posts. The program is mirrored for the controller: the axis's coordinates and I/J/K are negated, G2/G3 and G41/G42 swap where exactly one inverted axis is in the plane, and the work-offset origin is negated. An inverted Z, helical arcs, threading, rotary/tilted moves, live tooling, probing and every other post are refused by name.

Fixes #374

title: feat(ui): each setup owns its WCS, Stock, Machine, Post, Fixtures and Tool list in the browser
body:
## What changed

**Browser tree (per setup).** The Setup section shows the Setups manager row, then one node per setup. Each node has a radio for the active setup (`ActivateSetup`, undoable) and its own children in the maintainer's order: **WCS, Stock, Machine, Post, Fixtures** (each fixture is a child row), **Tool list, Operations** (1+n, in machining order). A document without setups shows the same children for its implicit setup. The document-wide Operations section is gone. Models and the document's Tools library stay top-level.

**Node pages (right pane).**
- **Setup row:** opens the setup's settings. These are the active radio, the stock source, part alignment, plane pick, the WCS label (G54-G59) and Delete. The stock source shows "its own stock". From the second setup on it also shows a disabled "the stock <previous setup> leaves behind" option, which is the hook for #317/#320 and is not implemented here.
- **WCS:** the origin dialog, plus the setup's G54-G59 label picker.
- **Stock:** unchanged.
- **Machine / Post:** a choice between the document's machine/post and the setup's own, then the existing selector.
- **Fixtures:** load and position this setup's fixtures.
- **Tool list:** a table of the setup's tools (T number, size, op count, Edit), the number-clash warning, the per-setup tool list and the setup-sheet export.
- **Operations:** as before.

Clicking any node under a setup activates that setup first, in one undoable step. The Stock, WCS, Fixtures, Machine and Post editors work on the active setup, so this way they can never edit a setup the clicked node does not belong to.

**Machine and post per setup.**
- `SetupDef` gains `machine: Option<MachineDef>` and `post: Option<PostRef>`. `None` (every older file, every new setup) means the setup follows the document's machine/post.
- New undoable commands `SetSetupMachine` and `SetSetupPost`. They are validated like `LoadMachine` / `SelectPost` and refuse by name.
- A datum transfer carries the source setup's machine and post.
- The existing machine and post verbs (ribbon, Stock page, editor) go to the active setup's own machine/post when it has one, and to the document's otherwise.
- Project version is now **v55**. v54 files open unchanged, and an old build refuses a v55 file.

**The one-mount rule.** The app reads one mounted machine and post, the active setup's (`machine::of`, `kind_of`, `posting::post_of`). Work that would use two different machines or posts is refused by name:
- generating an op whose setup is on a different machine or post: "activate 'SetupN' first";
- posting a program whose setups use different machines or posts: "one program is written by one post for one machine".

With no setup owning a machine or post, neither refusal can fire, so existing documents generate and post byte-identically.

title: fix(pick): refuse face-normal alignment on an inside-out or open body
body:
## What changed
Face-normal alignment picks no longer trust facet winding blindly. Before, an inside-out mesh made "lay this face on G17" turn the part upside down, and made a 3-2-1 pick the opposite side, silently.

**New `crates/app/src/pick/winding.rs`** gives each body a verdict.
- A body is a set of facets connected through shared edges. Vertices within 1e-4 mm count as the same point.
- Edges are counted by direction, which sorts a body into **Open**, **NonManifold** or **Mixed** winding.
- The signed volume (divergence theorem; Zhang & Chen 2001) gives **Outward**, **InsideOut** or **Flat**.
- Verdicts are cached for the last 8 meshes (thread-local), keyed by a hash of the facets that depends on winding.

**`pick/align.rs` `outward_normal`** refuses, by name, any face whose body is not Outward. The face lay, the two-edge lay and the 3-2-1 all go through it. Example message: `face … of 'cube_inside_out' belongs to a body whose facets are inside-out (wound inward), so its outside would be read backwards - fix the model's facet winding (re-export it) before aligning to it`.

**The design is to refuse at pick time; nothing is repaired at import.** User geometry, existing toolpaths and the goldens are unchanged. Alternatives are in `docs/decisions/366-inverted-winding.md`.

**Behaviour change users will notice:** face-normal picks on an **open or non-manifold** mesh, which used to be accepted, now refuse by name. That is what the issue asks for. The existing Repair mesh button is the way out.

## Readings
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test winding_align`: 9/9 pass.
- These existing suites pass: plane_align, plane_align_edges, wcs_align, setup_align, vertex_pick, face_origin, pick and repair_model.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main` (after merging upstream/main): every app suite passes.
- camcraft-ui suites: only the known GPU headless reds (`headless_run_succeeds`, `headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`, `egui_headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`).
- All five shipped testdata models read Outward.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/winding_align.rs`)
- An inverted cube refuses the face lay and the plane-side readout, the two-edge lay and the 3-2-1.
- The same cube wound outward still aligns.
- An open box refuses all three picks.
- Mixed-winding and non-manifold bodies refuse.
- In a two-body mesh, the good body lays and the bad one refuses.
- The shipped models read Outward.
- The fixture `testdata/models/cube_inside_out.stl` refuses.

## Not exercised
- No GUI hand test yet; a test binary has been built.
- Large-mesh performance was not measured. The check runs per pick and per frame for the plane-side readout. It is cached, but the content hash is computed each time, at about the cost of the existing feature digest.
- A face that spans two bodies has its logic reviewed but no test.

Changelog: Alignment picks (face lay, two-edge lay, 3-2-1) refuse by name on a body whose facets are inside-out, open or non-manifold, instead of silently flipping the part (#366)

Fixes #366

title: fix(post): Fanuc probe result folds the expected value's sign into the operator
body:
## What changed
The Fanuc post (`assets/posts/fanuc.cps`) wrote a doubled sign whenever a probe's expected value was negative in the active work offset. This happened in two places:

| Where | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `onProbeResult` deviation, edge at X -15 | `#190=#100--17` | `#190=#100+17` |
| `onProbeResult`, corner at (-15, -10), Y | `#191=#104--12` | `#191=#104+12` |
| `onProbeMove` no-contact check | `IF[ABS[#5061--12]LT0.001]...` | `IF[ABS[#5061+12]LT0.001]...` |
| expected value 0 or -0 | `#190=#100-0` | `#190=#100` |

- A new helper, `minusU(expr, v)`, writes `expr - v` with v's sign folded into the operator. A value that formats to 0 adds no term.
- The output stays unbracketed: macro B's arithmetic form is `#i=#j-#k`. This keeps `probe_bore_centre.nc` byte-identical. The bracketed option and why it was dropped are in `docs/decisions/377-fanuc-probe-sign.md`.
- The change stays clear of the comment block that #360 and #376 edit in fanuc.cps (lines 225-320).
- Other posts:
  - fanuc-lathe and heidenhain have no probe output.
  - The Haas, Mazak, Sinumerik and Tormach probe hooks arrive with #360 and #376, which fix the same pattern on their own branches.

## Readings
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test fanuc_post`: 11/11 pass.
- `--test probe_op`: 11/11 pass. No existing golden changed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

title: feat(machine): per-axis direction in the machine file; inverted axes refuse posting until #374
body:
## What changed

Part of #372 (decision: the machine's axis really moves the other way; the CAM side stays right-handed per ISO 841).

- **Machine file:** a linear part of a file-form `.mch` takes `"direction": 1 | -1`. Absent or null means `1`. Anything else (`0`, `2`, `0.5`, `"-1"`, a vector, a bool) refuses at load and names the axis: `machine file: axis X direction must be +1 or -1, not 2`. A numeric `-1` on a rotary part refuses too (a reversed rotary is not supported).
- **Model:** `AxisLimits::direction: machine::AxisDirection { Standard, Inverted }` (new `crates/post/src/machine/direction.rs`), plus `Machine::inverted_axes()`, `Machine::inverted_post_refusal()` and `AxisLimits::program_travel()`, ready for #374 to read. The project file stores it as `1`/`-1`; a bad value refuses the load. A standard axis writes no key, so every shipped machine, every saved project and the post mirror are byte-identical.
- **Travel check:** a stated stroke is the machine's own, in the coordinates its controller reads. An inverted axis is judged as `-v` against `[lo, hi]`, and the breach line says `(inverted axis)`. The derived table box maps the stroke to `[-hi, -lo]` in the program frame.
- **Posting is refused until #374:** the verification gate adds `machine <model> has an inverted X axis; posting for inverted axes is not supported yet (#374)`. That one gate blocks the single post, per-op posts and the script API's gate. The CLI `post --machine` refuses the same way, and now also refuses a file that `parse_mch` refuses. Standard-sign code is never posted for an inverted machine.
- **Machine page:** the machine editor gets a per-axis choice: "X+ moves: right / left", Y "away / toward you", Z "up / down", other letters "standard / reversed". An inverted axis shows a note that posting is refused until #374. The editor edits a draft that is applied through the existing undoable `EditMachineApply` -> `LoadMachine` command, so no new command was needed.
- Docs: grammar row in `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`; decisions in `docs/decisions/373-axis-direction.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/axis_direction.rs` (11 tests):
  - `direction_reads_plus_one_minus_one_and_absent`, `any_other_direction_refuses_by_name`, `a_reversed_rotary_refuses_and_other_rotary_shapes_are_not_read`
  - `every_shipped_machine_stays_standard` (every `posting::MACHINES` entry: no inverted axis, no serialized key, mirror unchanged)
  - `direction_round_trips_through_serde_and_refuses_garbage`, `an_inverted_machine_survives_a_project_save_and_load`, `loading_an_inverted_machine_undoes`
  - `travel_is_judged_in_the_machines_own_coordinates`, `the_table_box_maps_an_inverted_stroke`
  - `an_inverted_machine_refuses_posting_by_name`, `the_refusal_names_every_inverted_axis`
- `crates/post/tests/axis_direction_cli.rs`: `the_cli_refuses_an_inverted_machine_by_name`

## Gate (quick, debug, this worktree)

- Merged origin/main (#354 one-WCS) cleanly; app suites green after the merge: axis_direction 11, machine 32, tormach_machines 5, posting 17, conformance 6, golden_cl 23, fanuc_post 8, project_roundtrip 69, fixtures 14, setup_sheet 7. The goldens are unchanged.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all suites) green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- `camcraft-ui --lib` run from `crates/ui`: 297 passed, 2 ignored (after merging origin/main; on the pre-merge base, `egui_shell_snapshot_light` and `tool_editor_snapshot` failed the same way without this change - #354 regenerated those snapshots)

title: feat(tools): judge a modelled tool body by its revolved envelope
body:
First slice of #361 (vendor STEP tool models): milling.

## What changed
- **`SetToolBody` (new, undoable: set / replace / clear).** It attaches a holder or assembly mesh (STEP, STL or OBJ, through the existing importer) to a milling tool.
  - **Placement** is numeric: which model direction is the tool axis, and the model origin's height above the tip.
  - **Validated at command creation, refusals by name:** non-finite, empty or degenerate meshes; a body whose XY bounds don't contain the axis; a body reaching below the flute top; lathe insert kinds (that is #369).
  - `ChangeTool`, generation and the post gate also refuse a body that would sit over the flutes.
- **The revolved envelope** (`crates/tools/src/holder_profile.rs`):
  - Each triangle is clipped exactly to every band it crosses, and the band takes the farthest clipped vertex. It is exact, so a facet crossing a band with no vertex in it still counts.
  - Bands are cut at 0.25 mm or more (at most 2048), then merged down to at most 32, each merge keeping the larger radius. The envelope can only grow.
- **How the checks read it:**
  - **Fixture collision laws** (upright and posed, `sim/laws.rs`, `posed_steel.rs`, `workholding.rs`) take a `HolderStack` of real bands. `HolderStack::cylinder(geom)` reproduces the old float sums, so a tool without a body is bit-identical.
  - **Every one-cylinder check** (rest reach, solid law, multi-axis shank dodge, drill reach, cross-drill holder, machine max tool length) sees the tool with its holder replaced by the cylinder enclosing the body (`HolderProfile::enclose`). It is swapped in at three world reads: `collect_job`, the post gate's fixture walk, and the machine check. It can only over-report.
- **The body is part of the operation stamp** (it can change the generated path). It adds bytes only when present, so existing stamps are unchanged.
- **Project file v54.** An optional `body` key on the tool row holds the placed facets and placement. The envelope is re-derived on load, never saved, and a bad body refuses the file by name. The bump stops a v53 build from silently dropping the body and judging the smaller cylinder.
  - **Conflict note:** #354 also takes v54. Whichever merges second renumbers to v55, one line in the ladder plus the `51..=54` rung in `apply.rs`.
- **Deleting the tool** (`DeleteTool` / `DeleteEntity`) frees the body, and undo restores it.
- `docs/decisions/368-tool-body-step.md`

## How tested
- New `holder_profile` unit tests (7), including a facet crossing a band with no vertex in it, and a randomized check that no point on any facet lies outside its band.
- New `crates/app/tests/tool_body.rs` (8):
  - A 40 mm collar turns a move the 22 mm cylinder passed into a named holder collision, in generation and in the post gate.
  - A stepped body (narrow nose, wide flange) passes a post beside the nose that the enclosing cylinder would have hit.
  - With no body, the stamp and toolpath are identical to before.
  - Undo/redo walk set, replace and clear.
  - Save → load → save is byte-identical.
  - Deleting the tool frees the body, and degenerate input refuses by name.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main` (macOS), after merging upstream/main: tools, sim and app suites all green. That includes every existing golden_cl, fixtures, posting, project_roundtrip, commands_undo and drill suite, unchanged.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests` is clean, and `cargo check -p camcraft-ui` passes.

## Not exercised
- No UI: attaching a body is reachable from the command and the project file only. The picking UI and display are #371; ISO 13399 auto-alignment is #370 (stacking on this branch).
- Not yet in the tool library file (#348).

Changelog: Tools can carry a modelled holder body (STEP/STL/OBJ) placed by axis and tip offset; collision checks judge its revolved envelope (#368)

Fixes #368

title: feat(import): read named tool coordinate systems from a vendor STEP
body:
This is the STEP side of #370. It follows the split agreed on the issue with the #368 holder: a reader that returns a vendor tool STEP's named coordinate systems as plain data. It adds no tool-body component, command, project field or UI. Turning a found system into #368's numeric placement is the next round, which stacks on `issue/368-tool-body-step` once that branch is pushed.

## What changed
- New `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_csys.rs`:
  - `read_tool_csys(&[u8])` returns every named `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` with its name, entity id and role, its origin in mm (scaled by the file's length unit), and its unit z and x axes.
  - `CsysRole::classify` maps the ISO/TS 13399 names below, ignoring case. Any other name is `Other` and is never used for alignment.
  - `find(role)` returns the single system with that role, or the named reason there isn't one (missing, refused or ambiguous).
  - `none_found()` returns the named reason a caller falls back to numeric placement.
  - Refusals are by name, never a panic:
    - a zero or non-finite direction;
    - a non-finite origin;
    - a reference direction parallel to the axis;
    - a dangling or wrong-kind reference;
    - one name used for two different placements.
- `step_units.rs`: three helpers are now visible inside the module (`pub(super)`).
- Three original, hand-written fixtures in `testdata/models/tool_csys_*.step`.
- `docs/decisions/370-tool-csys-align.md`

## Names, confirmed before any code
The names come from public ISO/TS 13399 preview pages (iTeh samples of parts 303, 401 and 405) and are cited in the provenance comment and the decisions file:
- PCS (primary coordinate system)
- MCS (mounting coordinate system)
- CIP (coordinate system in process)
- CSIF (coordinate system interface)
- CSW / CSWx / CSWx_y (coordinate system workpiece side)

CRP is a point, not a coordinate system, so it is not read.

## Readings
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tool_csys`: 6/6 pass. The existing `import` suite and the `step_units` unit tests still pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main`: every app suite passes except `scripting`, which SIGSEGV'd once under concurrent load.
  - This branch touches nothing on the scripting path.
  - The same binary passed 45 of 45 reruns alone.
  - Filed as #379 (P1).

## Pinning tests
- `iso_13399_coordinate_systems_are_found_and_classified`
- `a_file_without_tool_coordinate_systems_says_so_by_name`
- `degenerate_or_ambiguous_coordinate_systems_are_refused_by_name`
- `origins_read_in_the_files_length_unit`
- `iso_13399_names_classify_and_others_do_not`
- `unreadable_input_is_a_clean_error_never_a_panic`

- No real vendor STEP package was tried; the fixtures are hand-written.
- Assembly transforms are not composed: coordinates are in the frame of the part that holds them. Same-named systems in different frames give the ambiguity refusal, not a silent pick.
- The issue's "aligns with no manual offsets" waits for #368's body model, so this PR is `Refs`, not `Fixes`.

title: feat(mcp): export_tool_library and import_tool_library tools
body:
**Builds on #348 - includes its commits; merge after #348.** (A cross-fork PR can't target the fork branch, so this targets `main`. The #355 change itself is commit a840ce4; once #348 merges, this branch takes `git merge upstream/main` and the diff shrinks to that commit.)

## What changed
- MCP tools `export_tool_library {path}` and `import_tool_library {path}` (`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`), each with a schema that requires one string `path`.

As in the GUI, an identical tool is skipped, a clashing name arrives as "Name (2)", and a malformed or insane file is refused naming the tool.
  - Refusals come back as MCP tool errors: an unreadable file, an unwritable path, a document with no tools to export, or "nothing to import".
- Matching job-script verbs `cam.exportTools(path)` and `cam.importTools(path)` are in the VERBS table and `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts`. The MCP tools call these verbs, so the MCP lane and the batch lane share one meaning per verb (#128).

title: feat(post): probing hooks for the Tormach PathPilot post (G38.2)
body:
**Stacked on #333** (`issue/257-gcode-comments`, which also edits `tormach.cps`). This diff includes #333's commits until it merges; the #362 work is the last commit (55b7b83).

## What changed
`assets/posts/tormach.cps` gains `onProbeMove` / `onProbeRetreat` / `onProbeResult` in LinuxCNC/PathPilot words, so a Probe op posts on the Tormach mills instead of being refused by name.

**The touch move**
- It is `G38.2`. The control halts with an error when contact never comes, or when the probe is already tripped at the start, so the post writes no no-contact test of its own.
- XY is positioned first, so a probe never starts from an unknown XY.
- `G38.3` plus a `#5070` test was rejected: it hands that safety from the control to our own branch.

**Reading the trip**
- It is read from `#5061`–`#5063`. These are in the coordinate system the G38 ran in, in program units, so they compare directly with the expected values.

**Back-off and tolerance alarm**
- The back-off is incremental (`G91 G1 … G90`).
- A deviation past the tolerance runs `o9nn if [ABS[#19x] GT tol]` / `(MSG, …)` / `M2` / `o9nn endif`, with a unique O-word per test.
- `M2`, not `M0`, so the operator can't resume onto a wrong offset. `(ABORT,…)` is not in the stable LinuxCNC reference.

**Setting the offset**
- `G10 L20 P<n> X[#5420-#190] …`: the current position in the active offset, minus the deviation. It is exact in either unit.
- `G10 L2` from `#5221+20×slot` was rejected: the reference doesn't say which unit the stored offsets use, so a G21 program on an inch-configured control could mix units.
- With no offset to set, it writes `(MSG, CHECK PROBE RESULT …)` then `M0`.

**Preamble**
- A section at 0 rpm (a touch probe) writes no spindle start, no belt note and no coolant.

**Arming**
- Nothing is written. PathPilot's probe input is always live, and the probe type is a Settings-tab choice.

The sources for every word are in `docs/decisions/362-tormach-probe.md`: the LinuxCNC G-code reference, overview and o-code pages, and Tormach's PathPilot post-processor guidelines and G38.x pages. No other CAM system's output was read.

## How tested
- New `crates/app/tests/probe_tormach.rs` (7 tests). Goldens in `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/` on the 770MX (inch): `probe_face`, `probe_edge`, `probe_corner`, `probe_bore_centre`, `probe_boss_centre`, plus metric `probe_bore_centre_mm`.
- `probe_op::the_tormach_post_probes_the_op_with_g38_2`: the op now posts on Tormach, where it used to be refused.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main` (macOS): post and app suites all green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests` is clean.

## Not exercised (draft until done)
These still need a run in PathPilot Hub (770MX), which the contributor will do:
1. Whether preview stops at the first `M2`. In preview, probe moves report the programmed end point, so tolerance tests may read as failed there.
2. That the G91 back-off right after a trip doesn't raise "probe tripped during non-probe move".
3. That `o9nn if`/`endif` is accepted and `(MSG, …)` shows.
4. That `G10 L20 P2` writes G55 correctly, inch and metric.
5. That a trip during the plain G1 descent errors (relevant to #174).
6. That G38.2 errors cleanly with no contact.

Changelog: The Tormach PathPilot post writes the Probe operation (G38.2 touch, tolerance alarm, G10 L20 work offset) instead of refusing it (#362)

Fixes #362

- Add a contributor-facing machine onboarding checklist covering sourced facts, units/coordinates, axis and spindle limits, controller/post fit, and manual citation/redistribution boundaries.

- Document current JSON-comment, unknown rigid-tapping, and headless-interface limits. MCP can verify machine data in an opened project, but has no direct `.mch` loader.
- Keep physical-machine acceptance separate: software fixtures are not machine certification. No machine, post dialect, UI, schema, verifier, dependency or toolpath change.

Seven selected Windows tests executed successfully, each with native exit 0 and one passing test:

- `machine::every_shipped_machine_mounts_and_speaks_its_declaration`

title: feat(mcp): render_stock - the simulated stock as a PNG image block
body:
## What changed
- **New MCP tool `render_stock`.** It runs the post gate's own program simulation (`stock_sim::simulate_document`) and paints what stands by deviation class: clean, rest, gouge, unjudged.
  - **CPU rasteriser.** It draws the result with a new rasteriser (`crates/app/src/raster.rs`): flat-shaded triangles through a depth buffer, orthographic camera, PNG via the `png` crate. No GPU.
  - **Answer.** The PNG comes back as an MCP image content block (`{"type":"image","data":…,"mimeType":"image/png"}`) after the text block. Alongside it, a JSON summary gives:
    - rest and gouge cell counts, volume, maximum and where it is;
    - the rest's top bounds and the drawn stock's bounds;
    - judged-cell count and image facts.
  - **Arguments:** `width`/`height` (16–2048, default 640×480), `view` (`iso` | `top`), `toolpath` (bool: feed, plunge and rapid moves drawn over the stock).
  - **Refusals, each named:** no simulation (no stock or nothing generated), no material standing above the stock floor, bad or unknown arguments. Unsupported programs (5-axis, rotary, lathe) refuse with the sim's own reason, as the post gate does.
- `mcp/mod.rs` `tool_ok` lifts the PNG out of the JSON into the image block, so neither the text nor `structuredContent` carries the base64.
- `mcp/tools.rs` gets one table row only. **Note:** PR #314 also adds a row to this table, so a one-line conflict is possible and trivial to resolve.
- **Dependency:** `png = "0.18"` is now a direct dependency of `camcraft-app`, declared in the workspace. It was already in `Cargo.lock` through `image`, so no new crate enters the tree (MIT/Apache-2.0). base64 is hand-written (a few lines) rather than a new crate.
- `docs/decisions/182-mcp-sim-render.md`

## How tested
- New `crates/app/tests/mcp_render.rs` (5 tests):
  - Uncut job: the PNG decodes at the requested size, stock covers the frame, rest volume is 8000 (40×40×5), and the base64 is not in the JSON.
  - The same session gives the same bytes twice, and a fresh session gives the same bytes too.
  - The top view with the toolpath overlay contains the feed-move colour.
  - `render_stock_shows_what_the_program_cut`: Face 2 mm down changes the bytes, the stock top goes to z 18 and rest to 4800. Facing down to the part top takes rest to 0 and removes every amber pixel (more than 10% of the frame repaints).
  - `render_stock_refuses_when_no_material_stands`: facing below the stock floor refuses by name, where it used to draw a flat sheet under the block.
  - The tool is listed with its schema, and every argument refusal is named.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_render --test mcp`: 9 passed. `clippy -D warnings` is clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main` fell back to batch because Cargo.toml changed. The only failures also fail on `upstream/main` c442118 on this machine:
  - `probe_op::every_older_kind_keeps_its_stored_id_and_digest_tag` (version pin; PR #345)
  - `swarf_pose_continuity` ×2 (PR #351)
  - the headless-GPU ui tests (no adapter here)
  - the two macOS pixel-snapshot diffs (#255 / PR #359)

## Not exercised
- Not tried from a real MCP client (Claude Desktop etc.). Only the JSON-RPC tool path is tested.

title: feat(post): probing hooks for the Haas, Mazak and Siemens posts
body:
**Stacked on #333** (`issue/257-gcode-comments`, which touches every `.cps` post). This diff includes #333's commits until it merges; the #173 work itself is the last commit. Review #333 first.

## What changed
- **`haas.cps`: probes.** It adds `onProbeMove` / `onProbeRetreat` / `onProbeResult`:
  - G31 skip; #5061–#5063 trip read; no-contact and out-of-tolerance alarms through `#3000`;
  - incremental G91 back-off;
  - `G10 L2 P` from `#5221+20×slot`, or a `#3006` operator stop.
  - Source: the Haas Mill Operator's Manual (public).
- **`mazak.cps`: probes.** The same macro-B contract in Mazak EIA/ISO words:
  - `IF[..]GOTO` with unique N labels, since `IF..THEN` is not documented on every EIA generation;
  - the operator stop is a comment plus M00.
  - Source: Mazak's EIA/ISO programming manual (Fanuc-compatible).
- **`sinumerik.cps`: probes.**
  - `MEAS=1 G1`; `$AC_MEA[1]` checks for no contact; `$AA_MW[..]` reads the trip into R50–R61.
  - `IF..ENDIF` + `MSG` + `SETAL` + `M0` alarms; incremental G91 back-off.
  - Sets the offset through `$P_UIFR[..,TR]` (FI copied when the frame changes), then re-selects the active G5x.
  - It refuses by name to set G58/G59 (axial offsets on an 840D) or to work from an offset outside G54–G57 / G505–G599.
  - Source: SINUMERIK 840D sl Programming Manual (Fundamentals / Job Planning).
- **`heidenhain.cps`: still refused by name.** The TNC 640 ISO manual this post follows documents no skip move and no trip-position variable; TNC probing lives in the separate touch-probe-cycles manual. The script now carries a comment saying so, and the existing engine refusal is pinned.
- **Spindle at 0 rpm.** Haas, Mazak and Siemens no longer write a spindle-on block at 0 rpm (a touch probe), as fanuc already did. No existing golden contained `S0`.
- `docs/decisions/173-probe-hooks-dialects.md` names every source and judgement call.

## How tested
- New `crates/app/tests/probe_dialects.rs` (7 tests): bore-centre goldens `golden/nc/{haas,mazak,sinumerik}/probe_bore_centre.nc` (G55 set from G54), both operator-stop variants, the Sinumerik G59 refusal, and the Heidenhain refusal.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` (macOS): post suites ok. App suites: everything passes except `probe_op::every_older_kind_keeps_its_stored_id_and_digest_tag`. That test pins `PROJECT_VERSION == 51`, but main is now at 53, so it fails the same way on `upstream/main`; PR #345 fixes it. This commit touches no Rust source.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests` is clean.

## Not exercised
- **No controller or simulator run yet**, so this stays a draft. The posted words follow the public manuals only.
  - Mazak is the weakest-sourced: its `#5061` / `#5221` numbering should be confirmed against a Mazak manual.
  - Sinumerik's MEAS/`$AA_MW` path needs a check on a real 840D or a simulator.
- **The probe is not armed by the post.** Arming is machine-specific and stated by no stream record. An unarmed probe never trips, so it raises the no-contact alarm, which matches fanuc.

Changelog: The Haas, Mazak and Siemens 840D posts write the Probe operation (skip move, trip read, tolerance alarm, set work offset); Heidenhain keeps a named refusal (#173)

title: fix(motion): rotary Adaptive sorts the leave-limit level as material and names a narrowed helix before planning
body:
## What changed
- **Float noise at the leave limit** (the root cause of the red heavy test `adaptive_plans_the_developed_levels_under_the_load_and_kink_laws`). On the r7 bar the wrap's ladder level comes out as 6.500000000000001, one ulp above the leave limit `air_above` = 6.5. `pocket3d_air_split` split with a bare `>`, so it sorted that level as an air level (one lap) and the plan read 19.9 % D against the 19.7 % law. The new `machining3d::entry::air_levels` counts a plane within `EPS` of the limit as a material plane, as the function's doc already said ("at or below"). `pocket3d_air_split` is only called by the rotary wrap.
- **Narrowed helix refused by name before planning.** On the wrap only (seam present), `hsm::plan_level` now asks the planner's own entry rule (`machining2d::choose_entry`, now `pub(crate)`). If that rule would narrow the requested helix, Offset rings cut the level, with a note: `adaptive: the developed level is too narrow for the helix entry (radius 1.000 asked, 0.900 fits with room to spiral out) - Offset rings cut ... instead`. The note text is exported as `machining3d::NARROW_HELIX`. Before, the narrowed spiral overloaded (15.7 % D).
- **r6.2 travel refusal: kept and recorded as final.** The 5.7 and 5.2 levels are ~78 × 7.8 and ~78 × 5.8 mm bands round the neck. The variant with lifted returns breaks the planner's own 47.5 deg bound (48.0), and the plain spiral travels 3.2× and 3.9× its cut length out of cut (budget 1.5×). Refusing by name, and cutting with Offset rings, is the safe answer. Planning thin bands properly belongs to #44 and #47. Pinned by name.
- `rotary_adaptive.rs` (474 lines) is split: fixtures and the level reader move to `crates/motion/tests/rotary_adaptive_fixture/mod.rs`, a module with no binary of its own.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/55-rotary-adaptive-levels.md`.

## Readings (release; D6 ball, leave 0.5, helix r1, limit 19.7 % D)
| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| r7 bar, radius 6.5 | 19.9 % D (red) | 19.5 % D, two laps |
| r7 bar, radius 6.0 / 5.5 | 19.5 / 18.8 % | unchanged |
| r7 bar, posted world program | - | 160,989 moves, 0 in-cut breaks > 5 deg |
| 10 mm window, stepdown 2 | helix narrowed to 0.9, then 15.7 % overload; radius 5.0 refused after 197 revolutions | both levels refused by name, 0.4 s debug |
| r6.2 bar, radius 5.7 / 5.2 | refused for travel (8,208 / 8,828 mm out of cut) | still refused, now pinned by name |

The load margin on the r7 bar is still thin (19.5 against 19.7).

## Posted output
This changes posted G-code for **rotary-wrap programs only**: a wrap level at the leave limit is cleared over two laps (as in round 2), and an Adaptive wrap level too narrow for the helix is cut by Offset rings. Planar 2D and 3D pockets are unaffected. The OffsetRings golden digest on the r6.2 bar is unchanged. The PR stays a **draft** for a PathPilot Hub run.

## Pinning tests
- `rotary_adaptive::a_window_too_narrow_for_the_helix_is_refused_by_name_before_planning` (debug)
- `rotary_adaptive::the_r62_neck_levels_are_refused_for_travel_by_name` (heavy lane)
- `rotary_adaptive::adaptive_plans_the_developed_levels_under_the_load_and_kink_laws` (heavy lane, red on main, green here)
- `machining3d::hsm::tests::a_band_too_narrow_for_the_helix_is_named_before_planning`
- `machining3d::tests::a_plane_at_the_leave_envelope_is_a_material_plane`

## Gate
- Quick gate on the merge with upstream/main: motion suites green except the known `swarf_pose_continuity` (#351).
- Worker runs: release `rotary_adaptive --ignored` 4/4, motion lib 151, the rotary and pocket motion suites, and the app rotary suites, all green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

Changelog: Rotary Adaptive: the level at the part's leave limit is no longer sorted by float noise, and a developed band too narrow for the helix entry is cut by Offset rings with a note naming it instead of an overloaded plan (#55)

Fixes #55

title: feat(sim): the scallop flank reads to the ball diameter, between contact passes only
body:
## What changed
The scallop verifier's flank reach grows from `band + 3·tol` to `max(2r, band + 3·tol)` (`ridge::reach`). It now reads a cusp at any stepover up to the ball diameter, which is the generator's own ceiling (#37 `scallop_ceiling`). Before, it stopped at 4·tol past the ball. In #37 a plain widening convicted crowns, corners and box walls as scallop. Three cusp-geometry rules in the new `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/ridge_scan.rs` keep those false cusps out:
1. **Nearest feet only.** Only segments within `max(cell, 3·tol)` of the nearest distance count. A cusp stands equally far from both passes.
2. **One foot per pass.** Segments group into passes (joined runs, merged by closed iso-Z ring). Each pass counts once, at its nearest point. A free end gives no side.
3. **Both feet in contact** (`Access::touches`). A pass riding air or skimming stock flanks nothing.

The M13.8 `Flank` struct is retired. The ridge pass moved out of `scan.rs` (431 → 359 lines) into `ridge_scan.rs` (276 lines, with a provenance header). The full decision record is in `docs/decisions/212-scallop-reach.md`.

## Readings
- Flat raster at s=4 on an r3 ball: scallop 0 before (unread), **0.606** now (the analytic cusp).
- All 88 finish3d release-lane verdict fixtures stay clean. `morphed_spiral_dome_bites_nothing` goes from 0.1321 to 0. Flow 15/15.
- **One existing heavy-lane assertion changed:** `verify::envelope_verdict_follows_the_stated_tol` (app, `--ignored`). Its tight half (tol 0.01 on cone rings laddered for tol 0.1) used to expect silence. It now expects exactly one **non-blocking** `Scallop` note, for the rings' real ~0.085 mm cusp. That is over the 0.01 budget and under the 0.1 the rings were laddered to. The envelope (gouge/rest) half is unchanged.

Nothing generated or posted changes. Only the verifier's notes change, and the Scallop note stays non-blocking.

## Pinning tests
`crates/sim/tests/ridge_reach.rs`:
- `a_flat_raster_past_the_near_reach_is_judged_at_its_cusp`

title: fix(setup)!: one WCS per setup; G54-G59 is only the setup's post label
body:
## What changed
- **One WCS per setup.** `SetupDef.wcs` is now one entity name (was a six-slot list); `SetupDef.work_offset` is only the `G54`..`G59` word the post writes for it. Relabelling moves no origin and no height. `setup::wcs_entity` / `wcs_entity_name` take no slot; new `setup::wcs_label` ("WCS (G55)").
- **Commands.** `SetWcsOrigin::new(world, location)` places the active setup's one WCS (slot argument removed). A new setup's WCS is `<setup>/WCS`; the materialized first setup keeps pointing at the legacy `G54` entity (nothing renamed). Datum transfer clones the one WCS; DeleteSetup takes its own WCS with it.
- **Browser.** The Setup section shows a single row labelled plain **WCS** (the posted word as its faint suffix). The G55-G59 / "not placed" rows are gone. Clicking it opens the WCS page (`UiTarget::Wcs`), which edits the active setup's origin through the undoable `SetWcs` (numeric origin, turns, anchors, vertex/face origin chips, 3-2-1 align, Origin ribbon cell). The Setups-page dropdown is the only place the word is chosen.
- **Wording.** The WCS page heading, setup sheet (`WCS` section, `WCS (G55)` line), rotated-WCS refusal, Heights page read-only row, viewport height chip (`(WCS G55 +25.00)`), status lines and MCP `get_job` (`wcs` is now one object: label/word/placed/entity/origin/rotation) all speak of the setup's WCS.

## Migration (project v54, `project::wcs_one`)
- Each v53 setup keeps the entity (name and placement) of the slot it posted (its pick, else G54) as its one WCS, so single-WCS documents post byte for byte.
- Placed slots that no setup posted are dropped, each with a **load note** naming the entity and where it sat. `project::open_noted` / `load_noted` return the notes, the shell shows them in the status line, and they are logged.
- A document without setups keeps `G54` as its WCS and drops the rest with notes.
- An operation naming a setup the file does not hold posted at `<setup>/G54`. That entity is renamed `<setup>/WCS`, so the operation keeps its zero.
- Two origins inside one setup only arise from v51-or-older files. The existing v52 rung refuses those by name before this rung runs, so the migration never picks an origin. A v54 file that still lists slots is refused as corrupt. A malformed old offset row is still refused by the validator, not dropped.
- The two-setups-same-word-different-origin post refusal (#196) is unchanged.
- Stamp shape unchanged (the work-offset word is still digested), so migrated stamps stay fresh. Relabelling therefore asks a work-offset-height op for one regenerate, which produces the same path.

## Readings and tests
- New `crates/app/tests/one_wcs.rs` (7):
  - single placed slot posts identically;
  - several placed slots keep the posted one and drop the rest with notes;
  - a no-setup document keeps G54 and drops G55, and resaves byte-identical;
  - two setups keep their own posted origins;
  - an operation in a missing setup keeps its zero;
  - v54 with a slot list is corrupt;
  - a WCS edit undoes inside its own setup and a relabel spawns no origin.
- New `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/one_wcs.rs` (2): the browser shows one WCS per setup with no slot rows, and the WCS row edits the active setup's origin undoably.
- Rewritten for the new model: `setup_wcs` (relabel = word only, placing moves coordinates, undo), `setup_defines_wcs` (v51 fixtures built as JSON; conflicting v51 setups still refused by name), plus setups, heights, lathe_spindle_law, commands_undo, posting, rotated_wcs, project_roundtrip, setup_align and the ui shell/law/chip tests.
- Shell snapshots regenerated (`egui_app.png`, `egui_app_light.png`, `egui_tool_editor.png`). I checked them: the six G5x rows became one `WCS G54` row, and the chip reads `(WCS G54 +0.00)`.
- Gate results:
  - Passed (debug): app setup_wcs, setup_defines_wcs, one_wcs, rotated_wcs, wcs_align, setups, setup_sheet, setup_align, posting, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, heights, machine, lathe_spindle_law, golden_cl, conformance, fanuc_post, mcp, face_origin, drilling_cross_spindle/stock, lathe_field_sim, rotary_verify, operations, post_not_judged, heidenhain_block_form.
  - Passed: all camcraft-ui suites run from `crates/ui` (lib 294 passed).
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
  - Failing, not caused by this PR: `probe_op::every_older_kind_keeps_its_stored_id_and_digest_tag` asserts `PROJECT_VERSION == 51`. It already fails on main (53), and this bump makes it read 54.

Not exercised: the GUI by hand. Decisions: `docs/decisions/342-one-wcs.md`.

Changelog: One WCS per setup - the browser shows a single "WCS" node and G54-G59 is only the setup's post label; project v54 keeps each setup's posted origin and drops unposted slots with a load note (breaking: v54 files, SetWcsOrigin lost its slot) (#342)

Fixes #342

title: fix(multiaxis): a swarf raster line rises off the blade on a rapid under its lying pose
body:
## What changed
A swarf raster line used to turn upright on its exit rise, which forced an air link (retract, swing, re-plunge) at every raster end. Now, where it is proved safe, the rise posts as a **rapid that keeps the lying pose the line cut with**; the pose carries through the clearance rapid and the next line plunges under that same pose, so there is no head swing at all. New `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp_rise.rs` decides it; `stamp.rs` calls it during posing. Every condition must hold, otherwise the rise stays the old upright feed and the existing link law handles the turn:
- a feed going straight up Z with no XY travel;
- the program has already leaned, and the held pose is a lean not below level;
- the end of the rise is in air (beyond the contact band);
- the ball never gets closer to the part on the way up than at the start (the same floor the link retract uses);
- the held pose's flank is proved clear (`flank_clear`) at every half-radius sample up the rise.

The ball travels exactly the path the plan already gave it; only the flank differs, and it is checked. The rotaries don't move during the rapid. A rapid claims no contact, so the posed-contact law that flagged #17's in-air posed feed has nothing to judge; the posed-rapid solid law still checks it like every link retract. **No verifier law changed**; the other option (excusing a feed that leaves along the surface normal) was dropped.

## Readings
`swarf_pose_continuity` was **already red on main** (3 pass / 2 fail) in the same ratchet: the advanced count had drifted to 53 (pin 51) and the advanced full band to 86 (pin 84). This PR brings every count well under the old pins and sets the pins to the new counts:

| run | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| swarf, debug band | 34 | 23 |
| advanced, debug band | 53 | 34 |
| swarf, full band | 55 | 44 |
| advanced, full band | 86 | 67 |

- `swarf_pose_continuity` 6/6 (was 3/5); motion `--lib multiaxis` 57; `swarf_reentry`, `ruling`, `pivot5d` debug all pass; `pivot5d` heavy lane (release, `--ignored`) `the_envelope_reads_every_posed_kind_as_its_plan` passes (an envelope scan #17 left owed).
- app `operations::swarf_generates_blade_lying_axes_and_verifies_clean` and `advanced_swarf_adds_the_coarse_rungs` verify clean, as do their `_full_band` twins in the ignored lane; app `verify`, `area_controls`, `center_cut_multiaxis`, the swarf `project_roundtrip` test; sim `posed_rapids`, `posed_fixture_midpose` all pass.
- Quick gate (motion suites): green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Pinning tests
`swarf_pose_continuity::every_raster_exit_rise_is_a_rapid_holding_the_lying_pose` (new; finds no lying rises on the old code), the lowered link ratchets in `swarf_pose_continuity`, and `stamp_rise` unit tests (rapid when the flank is clear; stays a feed when a wall blocks the flank; rejects anything that isn't a straight rise from a lean into air).

## Needs the maintainer's hands (why this stays a draft)
**Posted swarf G-code changes**: each raster end was retract, swing, re-plunge, then an upright G1 rise; it is now one G0 rise at the lying A/B/C angles, with the lying pose carried through the clearance move. No golden covers swarf output, so none moved. Please run a swarf program through Hub / a real machine (watch the G0 rise at the leaned pose) before marking ready.

Decision: `docs/decisions/48-swarf-exit-rise.md`.

Changelog: Swarf: each raster line now leaves the blade on a rapid that keeps its lying tool angle instead of turning upright through an air link, so a raster end no longer swings the head (air links 34 to 23 on the test blade)

Fixes #48

title: feat(probe): seed the Probe op from a picked face, edge, vertex or round wall
body:
## What changed
A pick on a Probe op now seeds the op's mode, touch directions, expected contact and (for round picks) radius, inside the same undoable `SetOperationGeometry` command, so one Ctrl+Z takes back the pick and the seeded values together. `operation::probe_from_picks(...)` + `CreateOperation` with that pick as the source creates a seeded probe directly.
- **Planar face:** Face touch against the face's outward normal (normal within 1 deg of +-X, +-Y or +Z). The target is the face centroid, or the nearest facet's centroid if the centroid falls in a hole.
- **Straight level top edge:** Edge touch on the one vertical X/Y-facing wall under it; target is the edge midpoint.
- **Vertex:** Outside corner, X/Y directions from the two walls below it. An inside corner is refused.
- **Round wall / closed round rim:** Bore or Boss centre, centre and radius from the same circle fit Circular uses, at rim height. Bore vs Boss: the walls' outward normals mostly point at the axis -> Bore (a hole's wall); away -> Boss.
- **Refused by name, op unchanged:** a face that looks down or is tilted off the axes; a bent, sloped or vertical edge; an inside corner, a corner with a sloped face, or a bottom vertex; a cone or tilted wall, or a rim that isn't round; more than one pick.
- The Geometry tab prints the seed under the pick chip ("Probe from the pick: Face touch toward -Z at (...)").

The seed is written once, at the pick; generation still reads only the typed fields, so a hand edit after the pick is kept until the next pick. No project-format change (the pick is the op's existing saved selection source; the values go into the existing Probe fields). The post logic is untouched. New code is in `crates/app/src/operation/probe_pick.rs` and `probe_pick_round.rs`; `probe_op.rs` (PR #335) and all UI files are untouched.

## Readings
- `probe_pick` 9/9; `circular_pick`, `pick`, `vertex_pick`, `commands_undo`, `area_picks`, `heights_selection` all pass.
- `a_probe_created_from_a_pick_generates_clean`: face, corner and bore probes generate with no stylus-gouge warnings.
- Quick gate (all app suites): green except `probe_op::every_older_kind_keeps_its_stored_id_and_digest_tag`, red on main (#344 / PR #345).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not pinned: an open curved edge (refused as "not straight") has no fixture; the pick doesn't check a wall is taller than the touch depth - generation's stylus check judges that.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/probe_pick.rs`)
`a_planar_face_seeds_a_face_touch_against_its_normal`, `a_straight_top_edge_seeds_an_edge_touch_on_the_wall_under_it`, `a_vertex_seeds_an_outside_corner_from_its_two_walls`, `a_round_wall_or_rim_seeds_a_bore_or_boss_centre`, `picks_the_probe_cannot_touch_are_refused_by_name`, `the_pick_command_seeds_the_probe_and_one_undo_takes_both_back`, `a_probe_created_from_a_pick_generates_clean`, `other_kinds_are_not_seeded`, `an_inside_corner_is_refused_and_an_outside_one_on_the_l_seeds`

## GUI check (why this stays a draft)
1. Add a Probe op; on its Geometry tab set "Click selects" to Faces and click the top face: Find / Touch toward / Expected contact switch to Face, -Z and the face centroid, and the seed line appears under the chip.
2. Repeat with Edges on a top edge, Vertices on an outside corner, Faces on a bore wall: Edge / Outside corner / Bore centre with its radius.
3. Ctrl+Z once restores both the source and the previous values.
4. Clicking the underside face shows "geometry selection not updated: ... looks down ...".
Posted probe programs now carry the picked target/mode/directions; worth one Hub run of a seeded probe before merging.

Decision: `docs/decisions/171-probe-from-pick.md`.

Changelog: A Probe op seeds from one pick: a face gives a Face touch, a straight top edge an Edge touch, a vertex an outside Corner, a round wall or rim a Bore or Boss centre; picks it can't touch are refused by name

Fixes #171

body:
## What changed
Part 1 of #261's triage: a path that generated with verify warnings now shows them in the viewport.
- **Viewport:** every move a warning names (Gouge, ShankHit, SweepHit, RapidInStock, FixtureHit, NonFinite, Envelope, Scallop, both moves of a Crossing) draws in the palette's colour-vision-aware gouge colour instead of its feed / rapid / plunge colour. The first move of each folded warning line also gets a small 3-axis cross in that colour - the plunge red is close to the gouge red, so colour alone wouldn't single out a warned plunge. One cross per folded line, so a long shank run doesn't litter the view.
- **Op page:** each folded warning line in the expanded status banner is a link ("show this move in the viewport"); a click centres the camera on that move's midpoint via the existing `actions::frame_at`, keeping zoom and orientation. View state only, not a command.
- `RestUnjudged` marks and frames nothing (its index is a convention, not a place). A warning index past the end of the path is ignored, never indexed.
- A path with no warnings draws exactly as before; no pixel snapshot changed.

The warned-move set is a pure app function (`crates/app/src/warned_moves.rs`); the drawing moved out of `interact.rs` into `crates/ui/src/path_lines.rs`. `shell.rs`, `egui_app/mod.rs` and `state.rs` are untouched.

Part 2 (showing a path for a *refused* generation) is not included - it's a design call, so this PR says `Refs #261`.

title: feat(tools): export and import a native tool library file
body:
## What changed
A CamCraft-native tool library file (the native half of #300's triage):
- **Export library…** on the Tool library page writes the document's tools as `{"format":"camcraft-tools","version":1,"units":"mm","tools":[{name, definition}]}` (`.camtools`). Each `definition` comes from the existing `project::tool_to_json` / `tool_from_json`, the same tool shape `.camproj` stores and MCP speaks, so there's no second field mapping. Tool numbers are not exported.
- **Import library…** reads it back (a bare MCP-style `[{name, definition}]` array is accepted too) as **one undo step** (`ImportTools`).
- The whole file is checked before anything lands. Bad JSON, a wrong format/version/units, a missing required field, a nameless tool, a name used twice, a reserved name (Stock, G54…), or a tool `Tool::is_sane` refuses each refuse the import by the tool's name, with nothing applied.
- A name already in the document is never overwritten: an identical tool is skipped, and a different one arrives as `"<name> (2)"`. A library that is already fully present refuses with "nothing to import" rather than adding an empty undo step.

Vendor formats (Fusion `.json`, `.hsmlib`) are **not** included - that stays the owner's clean-room call, so this PR says `Refs #300` and the issue stays open.

Code: `crates/app/src/tool_library.rs`, `crates/app/src/commands/tool_import.rs`, `crates/ui/src/state_tool_library.rs` (state.rs only gets a 2-line module include), about 20 lines in `pages.rs::tool_page`.

title: feat(setup): lay the part on a G17/G18/G19 plane from a picked face or two edges
body:
Builds on #341 (merged; #326, per-setup part alignment) - base `main`.

## What changed
- **App, `pick::plane` (new):** `lay_on_plane(world, picks, PlaneLay { plane, flip, place })` reads one flat face or two straight edges in the document frame and returns the setup's part alignment (rigid transform, document -> setup frame). Face: the shortest turn from the outward normal onto +Z (G17) / +Y (G18) / +X (G19), negated with Flip; the antiparallel case is a half turn about the plane's first axis (bottom onto G17 equals the "Flip over X" preset). Two edges: frame to frame, the plane normal onto the axis (outward = away from the parts' centre) and the first edge along X (G17/G18) or Y (G19). Turned about the parts' bounds centre like the #326 presets; "Face to plane level" sets the face (or the first edge's plane) to level 0 on that axis. The landing is checked (turned normal within 1e-9 rad of the axis, by the sine) before anything is returned.
- **Command:** `AlignPartToSetup::lay_on_plane(world, setup, picks, lay)` -> `AlignPartToSetup::new` (#341's door): one undoable command, the stock follows as it does for the presets. The work offset (`setup::wcs_slot`) is never touched; rotated work offsets stay refused.
