title: feat(setup): align the part to a setup's own frame, separate from the work offset
body:
## What changed

A setup can now hold the part aligned - flipped, turned, or as modelled - separate from its work offset (#326, part of #308).

- **Storage:** `SetupDef.part_alignment: Option<Location>` - the rigid transform from the document frame into the setup frame. `None` = "As modelled" (never stored as identity). Only parts (models that are not fixtures) read through it; the setup's stock, work offsets and fixtures already live in the setup frame.
- **Command:** `AlignPartToSetup` (undoable, validated at construction). `new(world, setup, Option<Location>)` takes any rigid transform (the door #330's picks will use); `preset(..)` (As modelled, Flip over X/Y, Turn 90/180/270 about Z) and `angles(.., [x, y, z]°)` turn the part about the centre of its bounds. Quarter turns use exact quaternion components.
- **Stock follows** like it follows `MoveModel` (stock from a part, or a one-part document's stock): a box/cylinder is rebuilt square to the setup frame. A cylinder that would lie on its side, or a following stock shared with another setup, is refused by name. `MoveModel` moves an aligned setup's stock as that setup sees the move. A datum transfer (`CreateSetup` from a setup) carries the alignment.
- **Work offset untouched.** `setup::wcs_slot` and the G-word come from the setup exactly as before (#331); rotated offsets stay refused at post (#315/#325).
- **Generation / stock / sim / post in the setup frame:** op material, Top/Bottom of Model and source-selection heights, the program sim's part, Fit to Models / Fit sides, stock from model, the part-size readout, the viewport's part drawing and picks (active setup's frame).
- **Stamps:** an entity source's pose is digested in the setup frame, and an aligned setup's alignment enters every op stamp of that setup. Nothing is written when as modelled, so no existing stamp moves.
- **Project v53:** `setup.part_alignment {translation, rotation}`; absent = as modelled, so every v52 file loads unchanged; a non-rigid transform is refused as corrupt. Not breaking (nothing loadable before is refused).
- **UI:** Setups page row "Part alignment" - a quick-choice combo plus typed X/Y/Z angles with Apply, queuing `CommandKind::AlignPart`.

## Refused by name in an aligned setup (this slice)

Generation is wired and pinned for **Face, 2D Contour, 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive** over a whole model or the stock. Refused at `collect_job` (the one door every generation passes), so an aligned setup never cuts in the unaligned frame:
- every other kind (3D, drilling, multi-axis, turning, ...);
- picked faces/edges as the source; area controls; a 3+2 tilt;
- any non-mill machine (lathe, mill-turn).

The program sim refuses a program spanning setups that hold the part differently (carrying cut stock between alignments is #317). An op generated before an alignment change is Stale and never posts.

## Readings

- Fixture: 40 x 40 x 20 block with a 20 x 20 hole blind to Z 10, stock 60 x 60 x 22 from Z -2, 4 mm end mill, whole-model Contour Z 20 -> 12.
- As modelled the cut levels run the hole ring at 8 mm and the outer ring at 22 mm. Flipped over X (stored rotation exactly `[1, 0, 0, 0]`, translation `(0, 0, 20)` = about the part centre Z 10): only the outer ring at 22 mm - Z 12..20 is the former bottom, solid. Posts at G54.
- The stock follows square: 60 x 60 x 22 now from Z 0 (the 2 mm under the part is 2 mm over it). A Turn 90 about Z lays a 60 x 40 block 40 x 60.
- Flip then As modelled: the op is Ok again without regenerating, and the regenerated program is byte-identical.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/setup_align.rs` (new):
- `as_modelled_is_byte_identical_and_the_stamp_returns_fresh`
- `a_flipped_setup_contours_the_former_bottom_and_posts_in_its_frame`
- `a_quarter_turn_rebuilds_the_stock_square_and_undo_redo_walk_it`
- `two_setups_hold_the_part_differently_without_touching_each_other`
- `unverified_kinds_and_picks_are_refused_by_name_in_an_aligned_setup`
- `the_alignment_round_trips_and_older_files_load_as_modelled`
- `the_program_sim_refuses_by_name_across_differently_held_setups`
- `the_pocket_and_face_kinds_cut_the_flipped_part_and_post`

`crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_align_tests.rs` (new):
- `the_alignment_control_turns_the_part_through_the_command`
- `typed_angles_reach_the_same_command_and_a_refusal_says_why`

## Gate (quick, debug, in the worktree)

- camcraft-app suites green: setup_align 8, golden_cl 23, conformance 6, posting 17, project_roundtrip 68, commands_undo 32, setups 11, setup_wcs 7, rotated_wcs 4, setup_defines_wcs 4, heights 11, heights_selection 9, fixtures 14, pick 9, remachining 6, stock_play 7, setup_sheet 7, operations 117 (6 ignored, heavy lane).
- camcraft-ui lib (CWD crates/ui): 291 passed, 2 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Goldens unchanged (as modelled is byte-identical).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/326-setup-part-alignment.md`. Found on the way: #340 (the loader does not pin a stock's geometry revision; side-stepped here).

Not done here: picks writing the alignment (#330), the setup-to-setup transform (#316), the move gizmo and setup sheet still read the document pose.

Changelog: Setups can hold the part flipped or turned (presets or typed angles), with the stock following square to the setup frame; Face, 2D Contour, 2D Pocket and 2D Adaptive generate and post in that frame, every other kind is refused by name in an aligned setup. Project files go to v53 (older files load as modelled).

body:
## Summary

- Give multi-pass, chamfer and taper turning the setup stock through additive `multi_pass_in`, `chamfer_in` and `taper_in` APIs; retain the old entry points as no-stock compatibility wrappers.
- Reuse #278's `StockEnv` / `Exit::inside` rule: feed the radial exit at the plunge feed when stock continues beyond the cut, and keep the existing rapid when it does not. Keep axial rapids outside the stock OD.
- Start multi-pass roughing from the stock top and discard stock-empty roughing rungs in restricted windows, preserving the leave floor and every finishing ride.
- Leave the verifier, simulation/posting gates, serialized schema and dependencies unchanged.

## Reproduction and pinning tests

On the original production base `b1411ab1`, the three new app regressions fail on the unsafe rapid exits. The existing verifier reports `RapidInStock` and posting refuses each program; this reproduced a caught defect, not silent unsafe output, so P1 is retained.

`crates/app/tests/turning_contour_stock.rs` exercises real setup/command generation and posting on a bar extending to Z48 with the cut ending at Z40:

- `a_multipass_in_a_longer_bar_exits_at_feed_and_posts`

- `a_taper_in_a_longer_bar_exits_at_feed_and_posts`

`crates/motion/tests/turning_contour_stock.rs` pins all three kinds' same-end/no-stock compatibility, exact path geometry apart from the required exit kind/feed, interior windows and wider-stock axial clearance. `a_wide_stock_ladder_drops_air_rungs_outside_a_restricted_window` also pins roughing engagement and finishing-ride preservation.

The app unit control `a_radial_exit_inside_a_longer_bar_is_refused_unless_it_is_a_feed` verifies that the unchanged meridian verifier refuses an intentionally rapid exit at the correct move index.

Exact head: `ced6931dad5c86b7974f8460112f07697b4be961`; integrated base: `be2019759fef54d330d8b37206dc0ef8cf33de33`.

title: feat(motion): the rotary wrap turns its seam clear of a D-flat instead of refusing it
body:
## What changed

Since #54 / PR #210, the rotary wrap refused by name a non-turned feature (a D-flat or keyway) that crossed its seam, so the user had to rotate the work. Now, when the default seam (the basis' ±π branch) is refused, the wrap looks for a seam angle itself:

- **Candidates** are the midpoints of the gaps between vertex azimuth columns. Each is judged by the unchanged #54/#228 seam law. A facet straddles a candidate when the candidate lies inside the shortest arc holding its off-axis vertices; one sweep hands every candidate its straddlers.
- **The pick** is the turned candidate farthest from any refused one, which on a D-flat is opposite the flat. Ties go to the candidate nearest the default seam.
- **The wrap** turns the azimuth basis about the axis by that angle and lays the development out again. The turned sheet is judged again before anything is cut. The world exit maps back through the same turned basis, so only the split moves and every point is cut at its true azimuth.
- **Unchanged outputs:** when the default seam is already turned it is kept, so existing wraps are byte-identical. No golden changed.
- **The refusal** happens only when no angle works (a feature all the way round), and says so by name. The search also refuses by name after handing out 20M straddler vertices, so a very dense mesh can't hang it.

Code: new `rotary_seam_angle.rs` (the search) and `rotary_sheet.rs` (the lap loop moved out of `rotary_offset.rs`, which shrinks from 401 to about 317 lines; plus `Basis::turned` and `polar`). `rotary_seam.rs` is split into `seam_columns` (the verdict) and `seam_refusal` (the error). Decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/226-wrap-seam-angle.md`.

## Readings

- All 36 off-centre flat placements wrap with 0 cut tips inside the true cross-section. Channel tips stand at the flat's true azimuth.
- A facet spread over more than half a turn (for example a non-fan end cap) makes the search pessimistic. Such a part may still be refused, but never unsafely, because the full development is judged again.
- Only Offset rings is checked for tips on world output. The Adaptive case checks that the developed channel exists; the Adaptive heavy lane (`rotary_adaptive` ignored tests) was not run.

## Pinning tests (`crates/motion/tests/rotary_dflat.rs`)

- `an_off_centre_flat_across_the_seam_never_puts_a_tip_in_the_part`: all 36 placements now wrap.
- `a_d_flat_bar_wraps_in_every_placement`: no refusal escape; tips at the flat's azimuth.
- `a_flat_channel_across_the_default_seam_develops_under_adaptive_and_rings` replaces `a_flat_channel_across_the_seam_is_refused_by_name_before_the_wrap`.
- `a_feature_all_the_way_round_is_still_refused_by_name` (new).
- Unit tests: `the_shortest_arc_runs_across_the_zero_azimuth`, `the_candidates_include_the_gap_across_zero`.

Gate: `scripts/gate.sh quick` (macOS): motion suites green apart from the known `swarf_pose_continuity` (pre-existing). Also run: app `rotary_verify`, `center_cut_multiaxis`, `project_roundtrip`, `operations` (green). clippy `-p camcraft-motion --all-targets -D warnings` clean.

Changelog: The rotary wrap turns its seam clear of a D-flat or keyway, so a flatted bar roughs in any placement; only a feature all the way round is refused (#226)

Fixes #226

title: feat(turning): a large keyway or flat no longer refuses a turned part
body:
## What changed

The lathe axis fit claims an axis only when 90 % of the answering surface meets the plain least-squares line, and the #71 robust pass only ran after that gate. A large keyway or flat failed the gate before the robust pass saw it. Example: a 10 x 20 mm keyway 6 mm deep on a D20 shaft drags the plain line 0.57 mm off, about twice the 0.29 mm band. A 50 mm keyway takes 17 % of the surface. Both were refused with "the model's normals share no rotation axis".

- New `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/axis_consensus.rs`. It is a fallback that runs **only when no candidate passes the plain gate**, so every part that already fitted gets exactly the same fit, and no golden changes. For each candidate direction, it keeps the facets whose normal lines meet the line within a cut scaled by the MAD (the kept facets' scatter). It refits on them and at least halves the cut each round, down to the sagitta band. The direction is held while the set settles, so a prism's single pencil of lines can't swing it (the #208 plate-with-boss case stays refused).
- The consensus line must be met by **75 %** of the answering surface (`CONSENSUS_SHARE`), against the plain 90 %. The coarseness and pencil gates are unchanged. It then takes the existing robust reweighting at the same share (`reweigh` / `judge_at` take the share as a parameter).
- `spindle_law.rs`: the refusal text moved into `refusal()`, so the untrusted ("biased fit") message is unit-tested.

Decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/113-lathe-axis-fit.md`.

## Readings

- Deep 20 mm keyway: the plain line is 0.57 mm off and the consensus fit is exact, with 4.7 % set aside. Long keyway: 17 % set aside.
- An off-axis lump of 30 % of the surface and a box are still refused by name.
- **Owner's call:** the 75 % share sits between the robust pass's 50 % backstop and the plain 90 %.
- A block standing on a meridian passes, as it already did under the plain gate: its walls square to the axis meet it like flats. Turning follows the part's outline about the axis, so the block is left standing, and the note names its share.
- `axis.rs` is 411 lines, just over the ~400 guideline. Most of the new code is in the new module.

## Pinning tests

- motion (`axis_consensus_tests`): `a_deep_twenty_mm_keyway_fits_on_the_true_axis`, `a_long_keyway_over_a_tenth_of_the_surface_fits`, `a_shaft_with_a_large_off_axis_lump_is_still_refused_by_name`, `a_box_is_still_refused_by_name`
- app (`lathe_spindle_keyed`): `a_deep_twenty_mm_keyway_on_g54_passes_the_spindle_law_and_generates`, `a_deep_twenty_mm_keyway_off_g54_is_refused_as_misplaced`, `a_shaft_with_a_large_off_axis_lump_is_still_refused_by_name`
- app unit (`spindle_law_tests`): `an_untrusted_fit_is_refused_as_biased_naming_its_share`, `an_untrusted_fit_never_shows_a_zero_share`, `a_trusted_fit_off_the_spindle_is_refused_as_misplaced`

Both deep-keyway app tests fail with the motion change removed.

Gate: `scripts/gate.sh quick` (macOS): motion and app suites green apart from the known `swarf_pose_continuity` (2 tests, pre-existing). clippy `-p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` clean.

Changelog: A lathe part with a large keyway or flat (over a tenth of its turned surface, or one that pulled the plain axis fit off) is read about its revolved surface and turns, with the set-aside share named; parts mostly not revolved are still refused (#113)

Fixes #113

title: feat(sim): judge the probe's stylus stem and body in the protected-move law
body:
## What changed

The probe op's protected-move law judged only the stylus ball (`probe_op::stylus_hits`). The stylus stem above the ball and the probe body were never checked. So a deep edge or corner touch beside a taller wall, or a touch under an overhang, could pass while the stem or body met the part.

- `probe_op::stylus_cutter(tool)` describes the probe as a stack the cutters' solid law can read. The ball is the cutting atom. The stem is the shank band at the ball's radius, up to the stylus length. The body and any holder form one band at the wider radius.
- `probe_op::stylus_reach_hits` runs the existing `verify::solid_hits` over every move, through its public seam with no copy. A stem or body meeting the part is a `ShankHit { part: true }`, and a rapid meeting it is `RapidInStock`. Both block the post. Only the ball may touch, so the expected contact excuses nothing above it, and a move the ball check already convicted isn't reported twice. The allowance is the existing `STYLUS_SLACK` (0.01 mm), so a stem riding tangent to the wall it touches stays clean.
- `generate_probe` adds these warnings to the ball check's.

Decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/172-probe-shank-sweep.md`. No new warning kind: `ShankHit` is reused, because a new variant would change the project file format.

## Readings

- `Tool` has no stylus-diameter field, so the stem is modelled at the ball's radius. Real stems are thinner, so this can only over-report, never miss a hit. Body and holder share one band at the wider radius, which is also conservative.
- No clean-bore fixture: the shape primitives can't build a block with a hole. The faceted-bore tangent maths matches the ball check, which already passes there.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/probe_reach.rs`, new suite)

- `a_stem_that_meets_an_overhang_is_a_shank_hit`
- `a_body_that_meets_a_tall_wall_is_a_shank_hit`
- `clean_touches_stay_clean_under_the_reach_law`
- `the_stylus_stack_is_ball_then_stem_then_body`
- `a_short_stylus_deep_on_the_stock_edge_is_refused_by_the_op`

The existing `probe_op` suite passes 11/11. Gate: `scripts/gate.sh quick` (macOS) is green. clippy `-p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

Changelog: Probe op: the stylus stem and the probe body are judged against the part on every probe move; a touch whose ball clears but whose stem or body meets a wall is refused as a shank hit (#172)

Fixes #172

title: fix(ui): macOS Cmd+Q asks about unsaved changes
body:
## What changed

On macOS, Cmd+Q, the app menu's Quit, the Dock's Quit and a logout all send `terminate:` to NSApplication. winit 0.30.13's app delegate has no `applicationShouldTerminate:`, so AppKit ended the process at once. `CloseRequested` never arrived, and the unsaved-changes prompt (#107) was skipped. The menu also takes Cmd+Q before egui sees it, so the egui Cmd/Ctrl+Q shortcut never fired on macOS either.

- New `crates/ui/src/egui_app/os_quit.rs`. On macOS, `install()` adds `applicationShouldTerminate:` to winit's delegate class through `class_addMethod`. The method answers `NSTerminateCancel` and only sets an atomic flag, so nothing can unwind across the FFI boundary. `class_addMethod` never replaces a method: if a future winit adds its own handler, the hook logs that and stays out. A missing AppKit, app or delegate is logged, never a panic. On other platforms `install()` does nothing.
- `route_pending(state)` turns the flag into `actions::quit`, the same guarded Quit the window X sends. The shell calls it in `about_to_wait`, and un-minimises and focuses the window so the prompt is seen. A clean document quits through `el.exit()`, which does not go back through `terminate:`.
- Dependency: `objc2 0.5`, the same binding and version winit already pulls in. It is macOS-only (`[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]`), and no new crate enters `Cargo.lock`.

Decisions and the alternatives dropped are recorded in `docs/decisions/144-macos-cmd-q.md`: retargeting the menu item, replacing winit's default menu, and routing to `performClose:`.

Side effect: cancelling the terminate also cancels a logout or shutdown while CamCraft is open, and macOS says CamCraft stopped it. That is the usual document-app behaviour. Letting the logout continue after the user answers was left out.

## Readings

- winit 0.30.13: `platform_impl/macos/menu.rs` wires Quit to `terminate:`, and `app_state.rs` implements only `applicationDidFinishLaunching:` and `applicationWillTerminate:`.
- Live run on a Mac: a debug build with a clean document, sent `terminate:` via `NSRunningApplication.terminate`. The request went through the hook, and the app then exited with code 0.

## Pinning test

- `egui_app::tests::unsaved::os_quit_request_over_unsaved_changes_prompts_once`: an OS quit request over unsaved work is routed once, does not exit, and shows "Unsaved changes"; Don't Save then quits.

Gate: `scripts/gate.sh quick` ran as batch (Cargo files touched). Green apart from the known swarf_pose_continuity and the GPU-adapter headless tests (headless_run_succeeds, egui_headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero, headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero: no graphics adapter in this environment). clippy `-p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

title: feat(post): comment the setup, operation and tool in posted programs
body:
## What changed

Every built-in post now writes three kinds of program comment, on by default:

- the **setup** name, once, where its first section opens;
- each **operation**'s name, kind and work offset, at its preamble;
- each **tool**'s number, name, kind, diameter and corner radius, just before its tool call.

Pieces:

- **Stream** (`crates/post/src/post/mod.rs`): four optional PARAMs, `OperationKind`, `SetupName`, `ToolKind` and `ToolCornerRadius`. Each is written only when it has a value, so a legacy stream or a user's .cps script that doesn't know them behaves as before. Documented in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`.
- **App** (`posting::op_streams`): fills them from the operation's kind label, its effective setup, and the tool's kind and corner radius.
- **Posts** (all seven under `assets/posts/`): a small, original "comments" block in each script. User text is cleaned per dialect: printable ASCII only, capped at 40 characters; `( ) % ;` become spaces, and Heidenhain also drops `*`. Every comment starts with our own keyword, so a user's name can't turn into an active comment such as LinuxCNC's `(MSG,`.

Sample lines:

| Dialect | Comments |
|---|---|
| Fanuc / Haas / Mazak / Tormach | `(SETUP: Setup1)` `(OPERATION: Contour1 - 2D CONTOUR - G54)` `(T01 EM-0600-4FL - FLAT END MILL D6)` |
| Sinumerik | `; OPERATION: Contour1 - 2D CONTOUR - G54` (unnumbered, like its machine-name line) |
| Heidenhain DIN/ISO | `N10 ; OPERATION: Plane arcs*` (numbered block; no work-offset word, since this post selects the active preset) |
| Fanuc lathe | `(T0101 TN-1600-0R8 - TURNING INSERT)` (no diameter for blades) |

Decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/257-gcode-comments.md`. The on/off post property is left to #258 / PR #302, which own the Post dialog. No UI is touched here.

## Readings

- 26 goldens regenerated (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1`). A script check confirmed only comment lines were added (50 in all): stripping them gives back each old file byte for byte. The one other change is Heidenhain's block numbers shifting. The 78 legacy `.cl` conformance goldens are unchanged, because their streams carry no PARAM or TOOL records.
- `crates/post/src/post/mod.rs` was already 491 lines and is now about 518. Not split in this PR.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/program_comments.rs`, new)

- `every_mill_dialect_comments_the_setup_operation_and_tool_in_its_own_syntax`
- `user_text_never_breaks_a_comment`
- `a_stream_without_the_commentary_params_writes_no_comment`
- `a_document_posts_its_setup_operation_kind_and_tool_kind`

Gate: `scripts/gate.sh quick` (macOS) green (post + app suites); ui lib tests that post (egui_app::tests, after_op_tests) green except the known `headless_run_succeeds`. 65 post-related test binaries pass (549 tests). clippy `-p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

## Needs a check on a real control

Every posted program changes. Before ready: a Hub / simulator run and a dry run on a real machine. The Heidenhain `N.. ; text*` form especially hasn't been tried on a TNC; the decision file names the fallbacks.

Changelog: Posted programs carry comments naming the setup, each operation (name, kind, work offset) and each tool (number, name, kind, diameter, corner radius) in every built-in dialect's own comment syntax (#257)

Fixes #257

title: fix(post): refuse a non-finite work-offset placement by name
body:
## What changed

A work offset whose placement is non-finite (NaN or infinite origin or rotation, or a zero-norm rotation quaternion) used to slip past the rotated-offset post refusal: its measured angle came out as 0, so it posted as unrotated. Such an offset is now refused by name at every entry point:

- **Post check** (`posting_wcs_rotation.rs`): a new `offset_frame(&Location)` sorts a placement into `Square` / `Rotated` / `NonFinite`. A `NonFinite` offset gets its own refusal: `work offset G54 has a non-finite placement (origin or rotation) - re-place the offset before posting (operations: ...)`.
- **`SetWcsOrigin`**: it already refused these values; its messages now name the slot (`work offset G55: rotation must be finite ...`).
- **Project load** (`project/validate.rs`): a WCS row with a non-finite translation or rotation, or an all-zero rotation, is refused as corrupt by name. Before, the loader quietly turned an all-zero rotation into the identity.
- **3-2-1 align**: no change needed. It refuses a non-finite frame already and writes through `SetWcsOrigin`.
- **Setup sheet**: a rotated offset now gets a line under its translation, `rotated 90.000 deg about Z - the post refuses a rotated offset`. A non-finite one says so too. Unrotated offsets print exactly as before.

Decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/327-nonfinite-wcs-rotation.md`.

## Readings

- A NaN rotation can't reach the world through the normal paths: the command refuses it, and `model::set_transform` replaces it with the identity. So the post-check refusal is a backstop, and its tests write the bad value onto the offset entity directly.
- JSON can't encode NaN or infinity, so the load test covers the all-zero rotation.
- Overlap with draft PR #331: it edits one line of `posting_wcs_rotation.rs` (the `wcs_slot(...)` call) next to lines this PR changes, and the "program offset" lines of `render_wcs`, which this PR leaves alone. Expect a small merge in `posting_wcs_rotation.rs`.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/rotated_wcs.rs`)

- `set_wcs_origin_refuses_a_non_finite_placement_by_slot`
- `a_non_finite_offset_rotation_is_refused_by_the_post_gate`
- `a_non_finite_offset_origin_is_refused_by_the_post_gate`
- `project_load_refuses_a_degenerate_offset_rotation`
- `the_setup_sheet_states_the_offset_rotation`

Gate: `scripts/gate.sh quick` (macOS): every app suite passes. One run of `project_roundtrip` aborted (SIGABRT) while three gates shared the machine; it was then 30/30 green run alone, and this diff does not touch that suite (noted as a possible pre-existing flake). clippy `-p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` is clean. Suites run: rotated_wcs, setup_sheet, setup_wcs, project_roundtrip, wcs_align, posting, commands_undo, setups, face_origin, app lib.

Changelog: A work offset with a non-finite or zero-length rotation, or a non-finite origin, is refused by name when set, on project load and at post, instead of posting as unrotated; the setup sheet states an offset's rotation (#327)

Fixes #327

title: fix(setup)!: the setup defines the work offset, not each height
body:
## What changed
- **Model:** `HeightReference::WorkOffset` names no slot any more. It resolves through `setup::wcs_slot(world, setup)` (the setup's pick, else G54). That is the same law the post uses, so an operation can't disagree with its setup. `posting::wcs_context` and `wcs_slot` no longer take the op's params. The #196 post refusal for "height on another slot than the pick" is removed because that state can't be built any more. The one-file shared-word refusal stays.
- **Heights page:** the Work offset reference no longer has a WCS combo. It shows a read-only "Work offset" row, e.g. `G55 (setup Setup1 - set on the Setups page)`, with a hover hint.
- **Setups page / setup sheet:** the unpicked entry was "Auto (from heights, else G54)" and is now "G54 (default)". The sheet now says `program offset: G54 (the default - not picked)`. The viewport plane chip shows the setup's G-word.
- **Project v52 + migration** (`crates/app/src/project/wcs_migrate.rs`). It runs before any world write. For each setup it collects every slot in use: the pick, each op's v51 posted slot, and every height's slot (suppressed ops included).
  - **One slot:** the slot moves onto the setup's `work_offset` (G54 stays unwritten). Stamps and posts don't change.
  - **Several slots:** the load is refused by name (`ProjectError::WorkOffsetConflict`). The message lists each op with its slots, e.g. `setup Setup1: Face1 (G55); Face2 (G56)`.
  - **No setup to hold the pick:** documents without setups load if everything is G54; any other slot is refused by name.
  - **v52 files:** a height that carries a slot is refused as corrupt. The MCP params door refuses one too.
- **Stamp:** a work-offset height feeds the resolved setup slot into the stamp. Migrated ops keep bit-identical stamps, so goldens don't change.
- Why the load is refused rather than loaded with a post refusal is in `docs/decisions/329-setup-defines-wcs.md`. Loading would mean either keeping per-height slots in memory or re-pointing the op on its next regeneration.

## Readings / tests (debug, worktree target)
- New `crates/app/tests/setup_defines_wcs.rs` (4 tests):
  - agreeing v51 file (per-height G55): the setup picks G55, the post is byte-identical and the resave equals the v52 save; a G54 file stays unpicked
  - conflicting setup: refused by name (G55/G56, G55/G54, and a picked setup with another height slot)
  - document without setups: refused by name
  - v52 height carrying a slot: refused as corrupt
- `setup_wcs::work_offset_heights_follow_the_setups_pick_and_its_undo`: picking G56 moves every work-offset height and stales the op; undo moves them back and redo moves them again. This replaces the removed #196 conflict test.
- ui lib `egui_app::setup_wcs_tests::the_heights_page_shows_the_setups_offset_with_no_wcs_choice`: one combo only (From), and the row follows the setup's pick. Run from CWD `crates/ui`: 286 passed, 0 failed.
- Green: setup_wcs, rotated_wcs, wcs_align, posting, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, conformance, golden_cl, fanuc_post, heights, heights_selection, setups, setup_sheet, lathe_spindle_law, lathe_post_refusals, heidenhain_block_form, mcp, operations, app lib, ui operations. No golden or snapshot changed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not exercised: the GUI by hand, the release heavy lanes, and batch suites outside the list above.

Changelog: A height measured from the work offset now reads its setup's offset (picked on the Setups page); the Heights page no longer offers a per-height WCS choice, and older projects migrate their slot onto the setup, or are refused by name when one setup's operations used different offsets (project v52) (#329)

Fixes #329

title: feat(setup): pick the work offset (G54-G59) a setup posts at
body:
## What changed

A setup now picks the work offset its program runs in (G54..G59), builds on #325 (merged).

- **Storage:** `SetupDef.work_offset: Option<usize>`. `None` = **Auto**, the inferred per-operation law every older document posted with (first slot the op's heights reference, else G54). New setups also start on Auto, so existing fixtures and goldens post byte-identically.
- **One law:** `posting::wcs_slot::wcs_slot(world, setup, params)` reads the setup's pick first. `wcs_context` and all of its callers follow it (generation, stamp, spindle law, machine travel check, single-file / per-op / script post, the #315 rotation clause).
- **Command:** `SetSetupWorkOffset`, undoable and validated at construction (setup exists, slot < 6, not the current value). A datum transfer copies the source's pick.
- **UI:** the Setups page has a "Work offset" combo under each setup (Auto, G54..G59). It queues the command and never writes the world itself.
- **Project v51:** the setup payload carries `"work_offset": "G55"`, left out when nothing is picked. v50 files step up with absent = Auto. An unknown word is a corrupt file. The version bump makes older readers refuse the file instead of posting a G55 setup at G54.
- **Refusals by name:**
  - In the verification gate: an op whose heights are measured from a different slot than its setup's pick (`Face1: its heights are measured from G56 but setup Setup1 posts at G55 - ...`).
  - In the one-file / script post: two setups posting the same word from different placements (`setups Setup1 and Setup2 both post at G54 from different placements ... pick another work offset for Setup2 ..., or post one file per operation`). Per-op files are exempt because each file belongs to one setup.
  - Note: the one-file refusal also catches documents that pick nothing. Before this change they posted that case silently.
- **Setup sheet:** WCS OFFSETS ends with `program offset: G55 (picked for this setup)` or `program offset: per operation - ... (not picked)`.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/196-setup-wcs.md`

## Readings

- A G55 pick at (10, 20, 5) gives the same program as G54 at the origin except for the G-word and the coordinates. Every X/Y/Z in the program (not counting the G28 home lines) shifts by exactly (-10, -20, -5).
- Milling stamps do not read the program origin, so a pick leaves milling paths fresh. Turning kinds go stale through the spindle-origin stamp (#62), as they did before.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/setup_wcs.rs` (new, 7 tests):
  - `a_picked_offset_posts_its_word_and_moves_coordinates_by_exactly_the_offset`
  - `the_pick_undoes_and_redoes_exactly`
  - `a_datum_transfer_carries_the_pick`
  - `the_pick_round_trips_and_old_files_read_the_inferred_law`
  - `a_height_on_another_slot_than_the_pick_is_refused_by_name`
  - `two_setups_on_one_word_from_different_placements_refuse_one_file`
  - `the_setup_sheet_names_the_program_offset`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_wcs_tests.rs`:
  - `the_picker_sets_the_setups_work_offset_through_the_command`: kittest; combo click, G55, then Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y.
  - `a_refused_pick_changes_nothing_and_says_why`
- `probe_op`: the version pin is updated from 50 to 51.

## Quick gate (local, debug)

- **App suites, all green:** posting, setups, wcs_align, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, conformance, golden_cl (goldens unchanged), fanuc_post, rotated_wcs, setup_sheet, probe_op, lathe_spindle_law, machine, per_op_files, scripting, setup_wcs, plus the app lib.
- **UI lib (CWD crates/ui):** 287 tests, all green. No snapshot changed: the picker only draws on a document that has setups.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

Changelog: A setup picks its work offset (G54-G59, default Auto = inferred per operation) on the Setups page; every op of the setup posts at it, the setup sheet names it, and conflicting picks are refused by name (project v51)

Fixes #196

title: fix(post): refuse a rotated work offset by name instead of posting it unrotated
body:
## What changed
- New verification-gate clause `posting::wcs_rotation::rotated_wcs_problems` (`crates/app/src/posting_wcs_rotation.rs`), called from `verification_report`, so the one-file post, the per-op post and the script API all refuse. It produces one line per rotated offset entity a posted op uses:
  `setup Setup1: its work offset G54 is rotated 90.000 deg about Z; posting a rotated work offset is not supported yet - re-align it without rotation or post from an unrotated setup (operations: Face1)` (in a legacy document with no setups it reads `work offset G54 is rotated ...`).
- The op-to-slot law moved into `wcs_rotation::wcs_slot`. `wcs_context` and the clause both read it, so the gate judges exactly the offset that gets posted.
- Tolerance: an angle (`2*atan2(|xyz|,|w|)`) of at most 1e-9 rad counts as unrotated, so identity offsets post byte-identical.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/315-rotated-wcs.md`. G68/G68.2, CYCLE800/ROT, PLANE/CYCL 10 and baking the rotation into coordinates were all set aside for now because none is trivially verifiable. That is step 3 of #315.

- Reproduced first. With the clause disabled, a G54 turned 90 deg about Z posts without error (`a_rotated_work_offset_is_refused_by_name`, `a_setups_rotated_offset_names_the_setup` and `an_unrotated_offset_posts_exactly_as_before` fail at the `expect_err`). title: feat(app): MCP detect_holes, through the app's own Detect holes rule
body:
A new MCP tool, `detect_holes {name}`, fills a Drill, Bore or Thread operation's hole list from its source model, through the same rule as the app's Detect holes button. Before, an agent's drill on a model with holes always refused "no holes to drill".

### What was wrong (`main` 8f30bee and 8cf3c90)

- The drilling kinds machine only the holes stored in their parameters. Only the UI's `State::detect_holes` filled them; the MCP tool table had nothing equivalent.
- Reproduced through `camcraft-cli mcp` on `testdata/models/Milling-test.step` (see #312).

### What changed

- `operation::detect_holes(world, name, params, setup, src)` (`operation/material.rs`): the rule moved out of the UI unchanged. It reads the source now (`holes_of`), fills whichever list the kind has, adds the drill's radial list on a turret machine (`cross_holes_of`), and refuses by name.
- `State::detect_holes` calls it: the same refusal texts and the same draft rule, with 55 lines of duplicated logic gone.
- MCP `detect_holes`: calls it and executes one undoable `EditOperationParams`. It answers `{operation, holes, radial_holes, status}`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/312-mcp-detect-holes.md`.

### Tests

- `crates/app/tests/mcp.rs`: `detect_holes_fills_a_drill_from_its_model_and_undo_empties_it`. A 20 mm disc with a 6 mm blind bore, as STL (the bore suites' `common::bore::revolve`):
  - the drill refuses "no holes" before detection;
  - `detect_holes` finds 1 axial and 0 radial holes, stored in the drill's params;
  - the drill generates;
  - two undos (the generation, then the detection) empty the list;
  - a Face op is refused "not a drilling operation".
- `handshake_and_tool_list` now expects `detect_holes`.
- With the tool row taken back out (`git stash` of `tools.rs`), the new test fails: "unknown tool 'detect_holes'". The UI's `detect_holes_refuses_recognizes_and_undo_empties_again` passes through the shared rule.

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 8cf3c90 plus this commit)

- The quick gate's plan for this diff (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand with `-j 3`): app lib, `mcp`, `turning`, `turning_profile` (104 pass), and ui lib, `boundary`, `boundary_picks`, `feedback`, `fixtures`, `gpu_render`, `machine`, `models`, `operations`, `shell` (366 pass, 2 ignored).

title: fix(motion): distinguish concave returns from inter-hole gaps
body:
## Summary

Fix facing's false "two holes" refusal on concave cutouts. A missing scanline piece does not prove a narrow strip between separate holes: both crossings can belong to a return of the same boundary.

- Retain boundary-loop identity with each crossing and require distinct boundaries, a positive gap no wider than the cutter, and a missing row piece before issuing the inter-hole refusal.
- Preserve the existing radius-grown clipping, row geometry, swept-area leftover notes, and post-verification. Concave returns remain clipped; they are not driven through to manufacture a successful path.
- Retain genuinely narrow and exactly-tool-width inter-hole refusals. Add wide/narrow U-notch regressions in both cutting directions, including cutter-radius-clearance checks.
- Record the decision in `docs/decisions/260-facing-gap.md`.

## Readings and diagnosis

The #260 report and attached `cutouts.camproj`, the facing generator and hole clipping code, `Region`'s normalized-loop contract, and the repository contribution/test rules. title: fix(app): STEP import reads the file's length unit
body:
STEP import now reads the file's declared length unit and converts to millimetres. A part saved in metres or inches imports at its true size, instead of having its numbers read as millimetres.

### What was wrong (`main` 8b0d784)

- `geometry/import/step.rs` tessellated the shells and kept every coordinate as millimetres. Nothing in `crates/` read a STEP `LENGTH_UNIT`.
- The repo's own `testdata/models/sample_ap214.step` (`CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT('METRE', ..)`) imported 0.0647 mm wide. An inch export would import 25.4 times too small, then generate, verify and post at that size.

### What changed

- New `geometry/import/step_units.rs`: `mm_per_unit` reads every representation context's `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` and resolves its `LENGTH_UNIT`:
  - an `SI_UNIT(prefix, .METRE.)` by its prefix (`$` is the metre; KILO through NANO);
  - a `CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT(name, #m)` by its `LENGTH_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` value times that measure's own unit, so `'INCH'` -> 25.4 x millimetre.
- `step::parse` reads the unit before tessellating and scales the facets to millimetres afterwards. That's safe because the tolerance schedule is relative to each shell's extent, so the mesh quality is the same in any unit.
- Refused by name (an `ImportError::Step`): a unit this reader can't convert, and contexts that state two different length units. A file with no unit context keeps millimetres, as before.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/306-step-units.md`.

### Tests

- `crates/app/tests/import.rs`:
  - `a_step_file_in_metres_imports_at_its_size_in_millimetres`: the AP214 sample is 60-70 mm wide.
  - `a_step_file_in_millimetres_keeps_its_numbers`: Milling-test's max corner is unchanged.
- `step_units::tests` (4): SI prefixes (milli, centi, none); an inch conversion through a measure is 25.4; no unit context keeps mm; two disagreeing contexts and an unknown prefix (`EXA`) refuse by name.
- With `step.rs` and `mod.rs` checked out from `main`, `a_step_file_in_metres...` fails ("the part is 0.06468733557556011 mm wide"), and the millimetre pin passes either way.

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 8b0d784 plus this branch)

- The quick gate's plan for this diff (app lib, `large_models`, `stock_export`), plus the whole `import` suite: 92 + 22 + 3 + 2 pass, 1 ignored.
- Every other app suite that imports a STEP fixture: `area_controls`, `area_open`, `commands_undo`, `heights_selection`, `lead_approach`, `level_links`, `pick_agnostic`, `pocket3d_hsm`, `shoulder_adaptive`, `solid_law`, `wall_arc_entry`. 97 pass, 3 ignored. `box.step` and `Milling-test.step` both declare millimetres, so their sizes don't move.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- A note on how this was checked: the first gate run reused another worktree's build (a shared `target` folder with older file times) and compiled none of this code. I touched every source in this worktree and confirmed with `cargo test -- --list` that the new tests were built before the runs above.
- Not run: the windowed app, Linux, macOS, and a real inch STEP export. The inch path is covered by the unit test's conversion chain, not by an exported file.

Changelog: STEP import reads the file's length unit, so a part saved in inches or metres imports at its true size; a unit it can't read is refused by name (#306)

Fixes #306

title: fix(cl): the text dump, is_prismatic and TiltedFrame keep the stated spindle C
body:
The CL text dump, `Toolpath::is_prismatic` and `TiltedFrame::world_path` now keep a move's stated spindle C (`Move::rotary`, #33). Before, all three dropped or ignored it.

### What was wrong (`main` 8b0d784)

- `cl::text::to_text` wrote a C-live path without its C angle, and `from_text` had no word to read one. A C-live cut written through the headless binaries' dump (#279) read back as a 3-axis path cutting somewhere else.
- `is_prismatic` looked only at the tool axis, so a C-live path counted as prismatic, and the dump wrote it as v1/v2.
- `TiltedFrame::world_path` rebuilt every move with `rotary: None`.

### What changed

- `to_text` writes ` SC<millidegrees>` after any pose letters, the spelling the app's golden writer (`crates/app/tests/common`) already uses. `from_text` reads it back through `Move::with_rotary`. The reader matches the two-letter `SC` before the one-letter words, so it can't be taken for the arc sense `S`. A path with no C dumps byte for byte as before.
- `is_prismatic` is false when any move states a C, so the dump (and the golden writer, which reads the same method) writes v4.
- `world_path` copies `rotary` onto every move it maps, chords included. No tilted kind is C-stamped today (the rotary kinds take no tilt, `OpParams::tilt`), so this keeps the angle rather than refusing. Why, and what was dropped, is in `docs/decisions/295-cl-text-rotary.md`.
- No golden holds an `SC` word, so none moved.

### Tests (`crates/cl/src/cl/tests.rs`)

- `a_stated_spindle_c_is_not_a_prismatic_path`
- `the_text_dump_round_trips_a_stated_spindle_c`: v4 header; ` SC-90500` / ` SC-450250` on the moves; read back to -90.5 / -450.25 deg; nothing else moves; a path with no C has no `SC`.
- `a_frame_keeps_a_stated_spindle_c_on_every_move_it_maps`: an upright frame and a 30-degree tilted one.
- With `path.rs`, `text.rs` and `frame.rs` put back to `main` (`git stash` of those files only), all three fail: "assertion failed: !c_live().is_prismatic()", "C None, want -90.5", and "a C-live path is not prismatic, so v4: ; HSMW-CL v1 ...".

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 8b0d784 plus this commit)

- The quick gate's plan for this diff, which for a `cl` change is every suite of every crate except the four slow binaries (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand with `-j 3` because other sessions had the CPU near 100%): 2472 pass, 29 ignored, 3 fail.
- The 3 failures are the ui pixel snapshots (`egui_shell_snapshot`, `egui_shell_snapshot_light`, `tool_editor_snapshot`), with the same pixel counts as clean `main` on this machine (1544, 1815, 2080). The owner's reviewer saw them pass on its own machine (#276's review).
- `cargo clippy` over geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app and ui (`--all-targets -D warnings`): clean.
- Not run: the slow release-tier binaries, Linux, macOS, and a C-live job through the headless binaries end to end.

Changelog: The CL text dump keeps a C-axis live-tool path's spindle angle (the SC word), and such a path is no longer reported as prismatic (#295)

Fixes #295

title: fix(motion): a deburr leaves each edge run straight up before travelling
body:
A deburr now leaves each edge run straight up to the clearance plane before it travels to the next. It used to rapid diagonally from cutting depth, with the cone still in the break, up and across the part.

### What was wrong

- `finishing3d::deburr` opened every run with `Rapid` to `(next start, clearance)` from wherever the previous run ended: the tip `drop` below the edge, the cone touching the break it just cut. Only the last run got a vertical retract.
- On `main` 8f30bee, the brick from `operations.rs`'s deburr test (stock = the brick, `CM-0600-90`, width 2, window z 6..8) gives `Rapid (20,-10,8) -> (-20,10,25)`. Verify convicts `RapidInStock` at moves 3, 8 and 13, so the post is blocked.

### What changed

- `deburr::retract`: a vertical rapid from where the path stands to the clearance plane, or nothing when it's already there. It runs before every run's traverse and once at the end, replacing the old inline final retract, so the path's end is unchanged.
- Cut moves don't change. The existing deburr tests compare cut points and pass as before. No golden holds a deburr path.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/304-deburr-retract.md` (a feed retract, and a retract plane, were considered and dropped).

### Tests

- `crates/motion/tests/deburr.rs`: `every_run_leaves_its_cut_straight_up_before_the_next_traverse`. A closed box rides as several runs, and every rapid that starts below clearance is vertical and ends at clearance.
- New `crates/app/tests/deburr_links.rs`: `a_deburr_on_a_finished_brick_links_its_runs_without_a_rapid_in_stock`. Through the commands, on a finished part: no `RapidInStock`, and no diagonal rapid from cutting depth.
- With `deburr.rs` put back to `main` (`git stash` of that file only), both fail: "rapid 10 leaves cutting depth diagonally: (40, 0, -12) -> (0, 20, 20)", and "a link rapids through the part: [RapidInStock { at: 3 }, RapidInStock { at: 8 }, RapidInStock { at: 13 }]".

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 8f30bee plus this commit)

- The quick gate's plan for this diff (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand with `-j 4`): motion lib plus `deburr` (157 tests), app `deburr_links`. All pass.
- Every app suite that creates a Deburr operation, too: `operations`, `area_controls`, `project_roundtrip`, `ribbon`, `tool_law`, `probe_op`. With `deburr_links`, 225 pass and 6 ignored (ignored on `main` too).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run: the windowed app, Linux, macOS.
- Not fixed here: the deburr's intended break still reads as a gouge to the post gate (#303), so a deburr still can't post until that's decided. This PR removes the part of the refusal that was a real motion fault.

Changelog: A deburr leaves each edge run straight up to the clearance plane instead of rapiding diagonally from cutting depth through the part (#304)

Fixes #304

title: fix(ui): the Post dialog opens where the document last posted
body:
The Post dialog now opens where this document last posted, proposing the same file, or beside the saved project as `<project name>.nc`. It used to open with no folder and `program.nc` every time.

### What changed

- New `crates/ui/src/post_file.rs`: `post_target(last_post, project)` is the rule, and `for_document(&State)` feeds it the G-code viewer's file (the last successful post) and `State::project_path`.
  - Folder: the last post's, else the project's, else none (left to the OS).
  - Name: the last post's file name, else `<project stem>.nc`, else `program.nc`.
- `state.rs::post_program_dialog` takes that target: `set_directory` when there is a folder, and `set_file_name` from the target.
- The remembered file is `PostView::path`, which New and Open already clear, so a new document never inherits another one's folder. A refused post writes nothing and doesn't move it.
- One change from my claim on #258: the last post's name comes before the project's, so posting again after an edit proposes the file the shop already loads. The project name is the fallback for a document's first post. Reasons and dropped options (saving the folder in the project file) are in `docs/decisions/258-post-output-file.md`.

### Tests (`post_file::tests`, ui lib)

- `a_new_unsaved_document_proposes_program_nc_and_no_folder`
- `a_saved_project_proposes_its_own_name_in_its_folder`
- `the_last_post_sets_both_the_folder_and_the_name`
- `a_documents_project_file_and_last_post_feed_the_dialog`: a real `State`, with the viewer's window closed.
- `a_bare_file_name_opens_no_folder`
- These test a new function, so there's no "fails on main" run. On `main` the dialog's arguments were the constants `program.nc` and no folder.

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 8f30bee plus this commit)

- The quick gate's plan for this diff (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand with `-j 4`): ui lib plus `boundary`, `boundary_picks`, `feedback`, `fixtures`, `gpu_render`, `machine`, `models`, `operations`, `shell`, and `theme_files` too. 368 pass, 2 ignored, 3 fail.

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run: the native file dialog by hand (rfd can't run headless), Linux, macOS.

title: fix(ui): the G-code viewer lists every line from the left edge
body:
The G-code viewer now lists every program line from the left edge, and a line wider than the window stays on its one row.

### What was wrong

- `pages::gcode_listing` drew each line with `ui.add_sized([width, row_h], Label)`. egui lays that widget out in a centred-and-justified layout, so every line's text was centred in its row. On `main` 8f30bee, in the test program below, `M30` is painted at x 273 and the motion line above it at x 159.
- The same layout let a line wider than the window wrap onto a second row (30 px against a 15 px row). Every row below it was then off the scroll-cursor arithmetic, which divides by one fixed row height.

### What changed

- Each row is a left-to-right box exactly the listing's width and one monospace row tall (`allocate_ui_with_layout` plus `set_min_size`). The text starts at the left edge, and the row height is unchanged, so the cursor law (the clip rect's middle row is the published line) holds as before.
- A line wider than the window is truncated on its row, and egui shows the whole line on hover.
- Syntax colouring, the issue's second ("see about") ask, is not in this PR. It needs new per-word text colours that pass the contrast law on both built-in themes and every colour-vision mode, and maybe new theme-file keys, so I've left a proposal on the issue for the owner. Hence `Refs`, not `Fixes`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/256-gcode-left-align.md` (`Label::halign` inside `add_sized`, and a horizontal scroll bar, were considered and dropped).

### Tests (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/gcode_viewer.rs`, through the real shell layout)

- `every_gcode_line_starts_at_the_listings_left_edge`: `%`, `M30` and a long motion line are painted at the same x. It reads the painted text shapes from the frame output, because the accessibility rect is the row's box and spans the row either way.
- `a_line_wider_than_the_viewer_stays_on_one_row`: a 120-character comment is one row tall and starts at the same left edge.
- With `pages.rs` put back to `main` (`git stash` of that file only), both fail: "`M30` starts at x 273, the longer motion line at x 159", and "the wide comment is 30 tall, a one-line row 15.125". The two existing viewer tests (`the_viewer_window_publishes_the_scroll_cursor`, `a_successful_post_opens_the_viewer_and_new_document_retires_it`) pass with the change.

- The quick gate's plan for this diff (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand with `-j 3` because another session was using most of the CPU): ui lib plus `boundary`, `boundary_picks`, `theme_files`. 283 pass, 2 ignored, 3 fail.

title: fix(ui): a refused post keeps its reason in a window past the status line
body:
A refused post's reason now stays on screen in a "Post refused" window. A viewport click no longer erases it.

### What was wrong

- `State::post_program_path` put a refusal only on the status line ("post refused: <reason>").
- The status line is shared. The next viewport click (`interact::pick_model` writes "selected <name>" or "no model under the cursor"), face or edge pick, or command wrote over it, so the reason was gone before the user could act on it. Posting the seeded demo (refused for a shank hit) and clicking the viewport centre replaces the refusal on the status line with the pick's own line, and on `main` 8f30bee was the only place the reason was shown.

### What changed

- A refused post also keeps its reason in `State::post_refusal` (`PostRefusal { path, reason, doc_version }`). The status line is unchanged.
- New `egui_app/post_refusal.rs`: a "Post refused" window (an in-app `egui::Window`, like the G-code viewer) shows the reason in the error ink, and says nothing was written to the file and a program already there is unchanged. It closes by its ✖, like the G-code viewer. A long reason scrolls.
- The window goes when the user closes it, when a later post succeeds, or when the document is switched (New, Open).
- An edit or regenerate after the refusal keeps the window and adds "The document has changed since this post was refused - post again to check it.", so the reason is never shown as current when it may not be. A pick does not count as an edit.
- The window draws nothing while no refusal stands, so no shell snapshot moves.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/265-sticky-post-refusal.md` (sticky status line, closing on any edit, and putting the refusal in the G-code viewer were considered and dropped). PR #232's status-strip alert styling is separate and doesn't conflict: it makes a refusal stand out while it is on the line, and this keeps it after the line moves on.

### Tests (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/post_refusal.rs`, through the real shell layout)

- `a_refused_posts_reason_survives_a_viewport_click`: post the seed (refused), click the viewport centre. The status line moves on, and the window still shows the gate's exact reason. No changed-since note, and no file written.
- `an_edit_after_the_refusal_notes_it_and_a_successful_post_retires_it`: the skim edit and regenerate keep the reason and add the note; the skim then posts and the window is gone.
- `closing_the_refusal_window_retires_it` and `a_new_document_retires_the_refusal`.
- With the window call taken back out of `shell.rs` (`git stash` of that file only), `a_refused_posts_reason_survives_a_viewport_click` fails ("a refused post opens its window"). The other three read the new `State::post_refusal` field, so they don't build without the fix.

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 8f30bee plus this commit)

- The quick gate's plan for this diff (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand with `-j 3` because another session was using most of the CPU): ui lib plus `boundary`, `boundary_picks`, `feedback`, `fixtures`, `gpu_render`, `machine`, `models`, `operations`, `shell`, `theme_files`. 367 pass, 2 ignored, 3 fail (below).

title: feat(kernel): union/intersect and edge blends on the kernel seam, benched (M12.1 stage 2)
body:
M12.1 stage 2 of the Solidcore retirement gate. Stage 1 (68efb11) put solidcore 1.0.1 (tangency-labs' Apache-2.0 pure-Rust port of NVIDIA's SMLib) behind a `Kernel` seam in `camcraft-kernel`, with truck as the reference impl, and benched subtract and offset. This PR adds **union, intersection and edge blends (round/chamfer)** to the seam and the bench. **No production path is switched**: nothing outside `camcraft-kernel` depends on it.

## What changed
- `Kernel` trait: `boolean_union`, `boolean_intersect`, `blend_edges(solid, picks, radius, Blend::Round | Chamfer)`. truck implements union/intersect through truck-shapeops `or`/`and`. Its `blend_edges` returns `Unsupported` (truck has no fillet), and a test asserts that.
- `src/solidcore_blend.rs` (new): picks resolve to edges (256 samples plus golden-section refinement, `PICK_TOL` 1e-3). A pick on two edges at once (a vertex, or a point on a cylinder's seam) is refused as ambiguous. Then the port's `fillet_edges`, followed by a result law: a manifold solid, inside the source box, whose volume actually moved.
- Seam guards: face-less boolean operands are refused (the port returns the **whole box** for `box & empty`, now pinned). The blend radius guard is conservative on purpose (decision 4).
- `tests/common/mod.rs` holds the shared `Want`/`verdict`. Stage 1's 8 tests are all kept, and the count goes to 16.

## Agreement numbers (debug, default tolerances: truck mesh 1e-3 + boolean 1e-2)
| fixture | solidcore abs. error vs closed form | truck abs. error | cross gap (default) | cross gap (heavy lane, 10x finer) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| box-union-box-corner (1875) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| box-union-cylinder-boss (1000+20π) | 2.6e-9 | 1.7e-2 | 1.7e-2 | 2.9e-3 |
| box-intersect-box-corner (125) | 2.8e-14 | 0 | 2.8e-14 | 2.8e-14 |
| box-intersect-cylinder (40π) | 7.6e-9 | 3.4e-2 | 3.4e-2 | 5.7e-3 |
| (stage 1) cylinder-through-box / blind-pocket | 2.8e-8 / 4.2e-8 | 3.4e-2 / 2.6e-2 | same | 5.7e-3 / 2.8e-3 |

All bounding boxes agree within 1.5e-5 (truck's chord), and solidcore's within 1e-14.

Blends (solidcore only, checked against closed forms at 1e-6 relative; **truck: not yet - no blend in truck**):
| fixture | abs. error |
|---|---|
| cube round 1 / 4 / all 12 edges r2 (12 = Steiner, spherical corners) | 4.7e-8 / 9.0e-9 / 4.7e-7 |
| cube chamfer 1 / 4 / all 12 edges d2 (12 = inclusion-exclusion + bevel tetrahedra) | 1e-13 / 2e-13 / 1e-13 |
| L-block concave round r2 / chamfer d2 (material added) | 1.2e-9 / 4.5e-13 |
| cylinder top rim / both rims round r1 (Pappus) | 3.1e-6 / 2.2e-6 |
| hole rim round r1 on a boolean result (Pappus) | 4.4e-7 |
| **NOT YET** cylinder rim chamfer d1, port default path | 5.3e-4 (1.9e-6 rel - fails), upstream WR-421; pinned as a finding |
| same with opt-in `fillet_chamfer_cone_on_arc` | 1.1e-5 (4e-8 rel) - passes |

## Port findings (pinned in `KNOWN_PORT_VERDICTS_STAGE2`)
- `box & empty` -> `Ok solid V=1000` (a wrong answer that looks like a valid solid). The seam refuses empty operands.
- `box & disjoint box` -> `Ok non-solid`. The seam's result check turns it into `Err`.
- `fillet r NaN` -> `Err`. `fillet r6 on a 10-cube edge` -> correct (922.743), but the seam still refuses it (conservative guard).
- solidcore never panicked on any degenerate input.

## Gate
- `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel`: agreement 2 + 2 ignored, blend 6, corrupt_input 6, all green
- `cargo test --release -p camcraft-kernel -- --ignored` (heavy lane): green
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p camcraft-kernel`: passes

Pinning tests: `boolean_fixtures_agree_across_kernels`, `boolean_fixtures_agree_at_fine_tessellation`, `cube_blends_match_closed_form`, `concave_l_blends_match_closed_form`, `rim_rounds_match_pappus`, `not_yet_rim_chamfer_default_path_stays_a_finding`, `rim_chamfer_agrees_with_cone_on_arc_fix`, `truck_offers_no_edge_blend`, `seam_refuses_degenerate_blends_and_empty_booleans`, `port_stage2_degenerates_never_panic_and_match_pinned_verdicts`.

## Still owed before truck's kernel role retires (#27 stays open)
- A corrupt-input corpus through a solidcore importer. None exists, and STEP stays on truck-stepio.
- M4.2's wasm CI job taking `camcraft-kernel` (the local check passes).
- Healing benched.
- The first production consumer (boolean stock ops, or face/island recognition) switched behind this bench.
- Upstream reports for the pinned port findings.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/27-solidcore-bench.md`.

title: feat(ui): machined mesh paints deviation classes and lights the hovered facet
body:
## What changed

The machined mesh in the viewer's stock slot (M13.1) now shows two things it did not before:

- **Deviation classes on the mesh.** Each facet is judged once per mesh, using the same rule the GPU eye uses: the model's `DistanceLattice` (`pack_target`) is read at the facet centroid, with the gate `gate_tol(DEV_TOL, view cell)`. The result is one of four classes: clean, rest, gouge or unjudged. The code is in the new `app::machined_classes` module. The classes are cached in `stock_export::MeshCache` (`classify` / `viewed_classes`) and computed in `ui::machined::prime` alongside the extraction. `world::collect_parts` expands them into the stock part's per-vertex class buffer, so the mesh uses the sheet's and the eye's legend colours. Nothing is computed per frame, and the STL export path does not pay for the classes.
- **Hovered facet highlight.** When the mesh answers a stock hover, `machined::filter_hit_facet` returns the triangle the ray hit. It is stored in `State::hover_mesh`, which is view state, not a command, and is cleared on every hover refresh. The shell draws it as a yellow translucent fill with an outline in the hover colour, projected through the camera each frame, so moving the pointer causes no GPU re-upload. If no mesh stands, or a corner projects behind the camera, nothing is drawn.

The extractor is unchanged. The sim crate is untouched, apart from public items it already exported.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/25-mesh-hover-deviation.md`.

## Results

- Faced fixture (12x12x20 box faced to z 18 over a 12x12x18 model): every up-facing facet on the faced top classifies clean. The class buffer has the same length as the vertex buffer, and only the four class values appear.
- A second `prime` reuses the same classes `Arc`, so nothing is judged twice.

## Tests

- `app::machined_classes::tests`: `the_boundaries_belong_to_clean`, `no_number_no_verdict` (NaN, infinite readings and a NaN tolerance give unjudged; nothing panics), `no_target_paints_every_facet_unjudged`, `facets_on_above_and_under_the_model_class_as_such`.
- `ui::machined_tests`: `nothing_before_a_view_and_one_extraction_after` (now checks the classes, which were previously asserted to be empty), `the_hovered_mesh_facet_is_the_one_the_ray_hit_and_projects`.
- `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick` fell back to the batch set, and every step passed: geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion and app suites, the ui suites run from `crates/ui`, and clippy with `-D warnings` (19.5 min). No snapshots changed.

Not hand-tested in the GUI yet.

Changelog: The machined stock mesh paints the Deviate classes (clean / rest / gouge / unjudged) and highlights the facet under the pointer.

Fixes #25

title: feat(multiaxis): continuous C-axis live tooling - stated C on cl moves, the C word in the lathe post
body:
Continuous C-axis live tooling, first shippable slice: the rotary kinds (Rotary Contour / Parallel / Offset) on a mill-turn whose spindle is C now generate, verify and post through the Fanuc lathe post, instead of refusing "pinned (M13.5 B)".

## What changed

- **cl**: `Move::rotary: Option<f64>`, the spindle's stated C in unwrapped degrees, beside the part-frame `to`/`axis`. `cl::stamp_c` (new `cl/rotary.rs`) stamps a radially posed part-frame path: C = minus the tip's azimuth (Rz(C) turns the tip onto the +X live-tool station), unwrapped move to move. Every move is split collinearly until the machine's X/Z/C-linear motion follows the verified chord within the op's tolerance. Refused by name: arcs, moves with no pose or a pose off the radial station, moves it cannot split near the spindle line, and paths carrying cycle/comp/thread/probe records. When the field is absent nothing changes: goldens, streams and project files stay byte-identical (the project field skips serialization).
- **app**: the rotary letter gate now returns 'C' for the spindle line, and the three rotary arms stamp their path (`rotary_gate::stamp_spindle_c`, the line must be world Z). `machine::check_document` checks a C move for a rotary named C and its stated travel, and no longer reads the part-frame axis as A/B for it. `MoveDto.rotary` persists the angle.
- **post stream/engine**: a C path writes `PARAM LiveTool radial` and `A 0 B 0 C <c>` on every move. The engine refuses that section by name for any script that does not declare `liveTooling = true` (same pattern as `coolantModes`), so every mill post refuses it.
- **.mch grammar**: `tool_station.live_tool { c_axis_on, c_axis_off, spindle_on, spindle_off }`, the builder-specific engage and live-spindle words (all four or none), mirrored to `machine.liveTool`.
- **fanuc-lathe.cps**: the C section. G98, the machine's C-on word, `<spindle_on> S<rpm>`. Every move is turned by C and must land on the station (5 um), otherwise it is refused and never projected. Output is `G01 X<2r> Z C F`, with F scaled for the control's composite rotary feed law (C degrees counted as mm). Rapids are G01 at the machine's stated max feed, never G00. The first move positions with `G00 C` and then `G00 X Z`. Arcs and cycles in the section are refused. Afterwards: spindle off, C off, G99. With no `live_tool` words stated, the section is refused by name.

## Readings

- The wrapped helix golden at r10, 30 deg chords, tol 0.01: each chord splits into 8 pieces. X dips to 19.318 at the chord midpoints, so the tool follows the planned chord, not an arc. F is about 2250-2370 for a 400 mm/min tip feed (composite degree-as-mm scaling).
- The Rotary Contour on the standing r6/r5 bar (mill-turn C) generates with every move on the station, posts with zero warnings, and contains no M03.

## Tests

- `cl::rotary::tests::*` (3): unwrap, winding, refusals.
- `c_axis_live.rs` (new, 4):
  - `a_rotary_contour_on_the_spindle_states_c_on_every_move_and_posts`: generate + post.
  - `the_wrapped_helix_posts_to_its_golden`: `golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/c_axis_helix.nc`.
  - `every_post_without_c_or_without_the_machines_words_refuses_by_name`: mill post / no live_tool words / C disagreeing with XY.
  - `the_c_word_rides_the_stream_and_parses_back`: also proves a path without C stays byte-shape identical.
- `rotary_letter.rs`: the pinned test is replaced by `the_mill_turn_spindle_as_c_axis_answers_c_and_stamps_it`. `operation::rotary_gate` unit test updated the same way.
- Touched suites run: see the PR comment for the gate readings.

## Limits (owed on #33, see docs/decisions/33-continuous-c.md)

- The machine C-sense word.
- Unwinding C on links against a stated travel. The shipped millturn.mch states -360..360, so a multi-ring path is refused by the letter gate.
- Axial/face live-tool stations and G12.1 polar interpolation.
- Arcs on a C turn.
- The composite feed law is a stated assumption about Fanuc-style controls, to be confirmed on a real control.
- The shipped millturn.mch states no live_tool words, so in-app posting of a C op refuses by name until the user's machine file states them.
- Size: `post/src/post/mod.rs` (465 -> 483) and `fanuc-lathe.cps` (424 -> ~520) were already over the 400-line target and grew.

Changelog: Continuous C-axis live tooling: rotary kinds on a mill-turn's spindle C state the C angle per move, split to tolerance, and post through the Fanuc lathe post (X Z C under G98 with the machine's live_tool words); every post without liveTooling refuses by name

Refs #33 (first slice: generates, verifies and posts; the owed list above stays on the issue)

title: build(wasm): camcraft-app links for wasm32 via a pinned wasi-sysroot (#31 rung 1)
body:
Rung 1 of the app/UI-on-wasm work. **This is a partial PR**: the domain layer builds and links for wasm32. The UI does not yet.

## What builds
- `web/build-app-wasm.sh` builds `camcraft-app` for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and links `camcraft-cli.wasm`. That covers flecs' C, boa, truck, clipper2 and rayon. Before this, only geometry, cl and post compiled for wasm32.
- flecs' C needs a libc, and this target has none. The script downloads the wasi-sysroot 34 tarball, checks its sha256, and passes its headers through `CFLAGS_wasm32_unknown_unknown`. It also adds `-D__COSMOCC__` (flecs' generic-POSIX path) and `-D__wasi__`. At link time its `libc.a` resolves malloc, printf, pthread, clock and the rest.
- flecs_ecs 0.2.2 and flecs_ecs_sys 0.2.1 do not compile for wasm32 as published; upstream says that support is still in progress. The script copies both crates and makes three edits to the copies:
  - `libc::FILE` becomes `c_void`.
  - The pre-generated bindings use `"C"` in place of `"C-unwind"`.
  - meta_fn_types' wasm-gated `WorldRef`/`Entity` import is no longer gated.

  The copies are used through `cargo --config patch.crates-io...` for this build only. Each edit checks that its patch point is still there, so a flecs bump that moves one fails the build instead of passing silently. The tracked `Cargo.lock` is restored when the script exits.
- The `wasm` job in `ci.yml` now runs the script. Like every job in that file it is `workflow_dispatch` only, so it adds no push, PR or schedule trigger.
- No Rust source, manifest or lock file changed, so the native build is unchanged.

## Readings
- Local run (Windows, Git Bash, clang 21.1.8): `web/build-app-wasm.sh` finished in 2m52s and printed `linked .../wasm32-unknown-unknown/debug/camcraft-cli.wasm` (270 MB, debug). Afterwards `git status` was clean, which shows the lock was restored.
- The linked module has two groups of imports:
  - the wasm-bindgen placeholders;
  - nine `wasi_snapshot_preview1` functions: `clock_time_get`, `fd_close`, `fd_fdstat_get`, `fd_prestat_get`, `fd_prestat_dir_name`, `fd_seek`, `fd_write`, `poll_oneoff`, `proc_exit`.
- I have not run the CI job. It is manual and the Actions budget applies.

## What does not build yet, and why (#31 stays open)
`cargo build -p camcraft-ui --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, with the flecs patches applied, stops at:
```
error[E0407]: method `bytes` is not a member of trait `egui::DroppedFile`
  --> egui-winit-0.36.2\src\dropped_file.rs:19:5
error[E0046]: not all trait items implemented, missing: `bytes_async`
error: could not compile `egui-winit` (lib) due to 2 previous errors
```
egui-winit 0.36.2 is native-only, so the browser shell needs eframe's web runner in its place. After that, the following are still owed; details are in `docs/decisions/31-wasm-ui.md`:
- Move `shell_layout` out of `shell.rs` so both shells call it.
- Bring up the GPU asynchronously. About ten `pollster::block_on` sites remain.
- Replace the synchronous `rfd::FileDialog` (9 sites) with an async version or an `<input type=file>` seam.
- Add a `web_time` seam for `std::time::Instant`, which panics on this target.
- Run work inline where the code calls `std::thread::spawn`.
- Write a JS shim for the nine wasi imports.
- Pin wasm-bindgen CLI 0.2.129.

## Tests
No Rust code changed, so there are no new pinning tests. The proof is the script itself, run locally above. `bash -n web/build-app-wasm.sh` passes.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/31-wasm-ui.md`.

title: fix(motion): a plain two-ring bar fits its true axis and wraps; the seam refusal names its causes
body:
A plain bar meshed as two rings now wraps in every orientation. The cause was the axis fit leaning by rounding, not a feature on the seam. The seam refusal now names its real causes.

### What was wrong

- A bar meshed as two rings (long side facets, axis-fan caps; this is how CAD exports a plain cylinder) was refused by the rotary wrap: "a feature that is not turned (a flat, a keyway, a cross hole) crosses the rotary wrap's seam". On `main` 0015347, with the issue's fixture (R6, Z ±40, 2 mm tool, Ø13 stock), n 16 at turn 0, n 64 at turn 0 and n 64 at turn 0.3 are refused (15, 37 and 38 seam columns). Only n 16 at turn 0.3 wraps.
- The cause is the axis fit, as the issue guessed, though the size differs: the lean is tens of microradians, not 1e-9.
  - On a two-ring bar, every side facet is a long right triangle. Its circumcenter (where `axis.rs` anchors its normal line) is the midpoint of the long diagonal, which is the bar's mid-station. No normal line can see a tilt about that point.
  - The eigen direction came out exactly Z (residual 7.4e-14 mm). The Gauss-Newton refinement (`axis_refine::refine_dir`) then returned a tilt of 2.6e-5 rad at n 16 and 2.5e-6 rad at n 64, and the fit kept it because its residual was "lower" by rounding noise (7.4159e-14 vs 7.4196e-14). At turn 0.3 the noise fell the other way, so the same bar fit exactly and wrapped.
  - With the axis leaning, the cap centres sat about 1 µm off it at arbitrary azimuths. Every cap facet near the ±π branch then read as a seam straddler, and the seam check counted far more than two columns.

### What changed

- `axis_refine::worth_refining`: the fit does not refine an eigen line whose residual is already below `CONCURRENT = 1e-9` mm per mm of mean radius. That line meets every normal line to rounding, and a refinement can only add a tilt the rows can't see. A real lean (the #62 uneven cone, microns of miss) is far above that floor and is still refined.
- `rotary_seam::SEAM_TH_TOL = 1 / WELD` (1e-6 rad, was 1e-9): seam vertices within the weld grid's grain, read as an angle, share a column. That is the same relative quantum the column profiles are compared at, and coarser than a float32 STL's azimuth noise. A flat's ragged vertices stand whole degrees apart; every D-flat refusal test still refuses.
- The seam refusal also names a mesh whose diameters were tessellated with different column counts, and says what to do about each cause ("rotate a feature clear of the seam, or export the model with one column count"). The phrase "crosses the rotary wrap's seam" is kept.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/228-seam-columns.md`. Widening only the seam tolerances was dropped: with the axis 2 µm off at the bar's end, the column profiles also differed by 2 µm in radius.

### Tests (`crates/motion/tests/rotary_dflat.rs`)

- `a_two_ring_bar_fits_its_true_axis`: n 16 and 64, at turns 0 and 0.3. The fitted axis leans less than 1e-12 rad.
- `a_plain_two_ring_bar_wraps_in_every_orientation`: the same four bars wrap, with more than 50 cuts and no cut tip inside the true polygon cross-section (0.05 margin).
- `a_shaft_meshed_with_mixed_column_counts_is_refused_naming_the_tessellation`: a stepped shaft with 16 columns on the neck and 64 on the body is refused, and the message names the column counts. Wrapping it would also answer the issue, but nothing pins what such a wrap would cut, so the refusal is what this test pins.
- With `axis.rs`, `axis_refine.rs` and `rotary_seam.rs` put back to `main`, all three fail; the four existing D-flat tests pass either way.

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 0015347 plus this commit)

- `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier batch` (every debug suite minus the four slow binaries, the ui crate, and clippy over every crate): 2400 tests pass. The axis fit is shared by the rotary kinds, the turning frame and the lathe spindle law, so this is the run that matters. It includes `lathe_spindle_fit`, which pins the #62 uneven-tessellation lean that the refinement exists for.

A `docker/` directory (local tooling - no workflow, no Actions minutes) with a per-target answer for every release.yml asset:
